The core driving force is once again coming from AI and semiconductors: AMD rose about 10%, and its market capitalization reached $1 trillion for the first time; Intel rose 12.2%, Arm rose 17%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index as a whole rose 4.3%. Meanwhile, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note fell below 5%, Brent crude oil fell to an 11-day low, and Bitcoin rose more than 6%, all of which improved risk appetite. The significance of this rise lies in the fact that it occurred just after the Federal Reserve resumed raising interest rates, indicating that investors still believe that AI capital spending and earnings growth can partially offset the higher discount rate. However, the market is still pricing in another interest rate hike in October at around 50%, so the contradiction between valuation expansion and rising interest rates has not been resolved. The next step depends on whether chip orders and cloud vendor capital expenditures can be fulfilled, as well as the valuation resilience of AI leaders if US Treasury yields rise again.Reuters 3. China and the US have formally established an AI security dialogue, and will meet again in Shenzhen in about two months to discuss the "incident hotline".U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessenter said on September 21 that senior Chinese and U.S. officials will meet again in Shenzhen in about two months to continue discussing the risks of artificial intelligence and communication agreements in the event of an AI security incident. Previously, Besant met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, and both sides agreed to establish a formal AI dialogue, including an "incident line" for communicating security incidents. Future discussions may cover issues that both sides believe pose systemic risks, such as runaway AI agents and non-state cyber actors. Compared to the previous day's disclosure of only the mechanism proposed by the US, the new development this time is that both sides have agreed to formalize dialogue and determine the direction of the next round of talks. Meanwhile, the US-China tariff truce is set to expire on November 10, but neither side has yet explicitly agreed to an extension. This mechanism will not eliminate chip export controls and technological competition, but it may reduce the probability of AI incidents being misjudged as state acts. We will then observe the specific departments involved in the Shenzhen meeting, the definition of an accident, and the reporting thresholds, as well as whether this week's meeting between the heads of state will grant this mechanism a higher level of political confirmation.Reuters 4. China tightens the pace of humanoid robot IPOs, shifting regulatory focus from technology stories to revenue quality.Reuters reported on September 21 that Chinese regulators are slowing the wave of humanoid robot companies going public, focusing on whether revenue from high valuations and local government-backed projects truly represents business demand. Sources familiar with the matter said that some companies have received informal "window guidance," significantly raising the IPO approval threshold in the industry. One of the key factors triggering regulatory caution was that Unitree’s stock price rose more than fivefold after its IPO, and then fell 55% from its peak. Regulators also pay special attention to robotic data acquisition centers and local government joint ventures, with local government funding accounting for 80% to 90% of the initial investment in some projects. Some investors estimate that if related revenue is excluded, the valuation of some robotics companies may decline by 60% to 70%. This does not mean that Beijing is withdrawing its strategic support for "embodied intelligence," but rather that the policy goal is shifting from expanding financing to verifying orders, deployment scale, and sustainable revenue. Looking ahead, we will see the pace of review for companies planning to go public, actual industrial orders, and whether local government fiscal support will be reduced.Reuters 5. The Hormuz "sea relay" maintains crude oil exports, but VLCC freight rates have exceeded $30 per barrel.Middle Eastern oil-producing countries are using ship-to-ship transshipment to maintain Hormuz exports. Kpler data shows that crude oil exports via Hormuz recovered to about 6.5 million barrels per day in September, the highest level since the brief easing in June. It is estimated that approximately 2.5 million barrels per day of crude oil will be loaded and unloaded via Gulf of Oman vessels this month, up from 1.4 million barrels per day in August, which is equivalent to about 40% of the current crude oil flow in the Strait. This system reduces the risk of a single tanker repeatedly passing through conflict zones, but significantly increases costs: LSEG data shows that the benchmark VLCC freight rate from the Gulf to China has exceeded $30 per barrel, a record high. At the same time, the number of trackable vessels remained far lower than before the war, as many ships turned off their transponders and sailed under American escort. The market is therefore not facing a simple "supply disruption or continuous supply", but rather a coexistence of supply recovery and soaring logistics costs. Going forward, attention should be paid to ship-to-ship transshipment capacity, insurance and freight rates, the recovery of the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, and whether any ceasefire negotiations can truly reduce the risk premium.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of asset pricing today is that "the growth narrative has once again overshadowed the tightening narrative, but the two are colliding head-on." On the interest rate side, Federal Reserve officials have begun to explicitly discuss overheated demand, indicating that even if oil prices fall from their highs, service prices and AI investments may still keep inflation sticky. If the probability of a rate hike in October continues to rise, short-term US Treasury bonds will come under pressure again. On the exchange rate side, the US dollar remains supported by high interest rates, while after the RMB previously broke through 6.70, the market will continue to observe whether the People's Bank of China's central parity rate will allow for further appreciation before the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders. In terms of risk appetite, the Nasdaq hitting a new high, AMD entering the trillion-dollar market capitalization bracket, and Bitcoin's rise indicate that funds are chasing high-beta assets again. However, this market is highly dependent on yields and should not rise rapidly again. The commodity market provided a buffer: the continuous decline in crude oil alleviated immediate inflation anxieties, but the real structure of Hormuz has not returned to normal. Exports of 6.5 million barrels per day and large-scale ship-to-ship transshipment demonstrate the resilience of the supply chain, while VLCC transportation costs exceeding $30 per barrel mean that geopolitical risks are shifting from "quantity shortages" to "logistics taxes". In terms of Chinese policy, the cooling of humanoid robot IPOs is worth considering alongside the rise in US AI stocks: both capital markets recognize long-term investment in AI, but regulators and investors are beginning to pay more attention to revenue quality, real orders, and safety responsibilities. Today, the focus should be on whether US Treasury yields can maintain their decline, whether oil prices will continue to fall, whether the rally in AI semiconductors can spread, and whether new enforceable arrangements for the trade truce and AI security mechanisms will emerge before the US-China summit. If yields and oil prices fall simultaneously, technology valuations will still have support; If evidence of demand-driven inflation strengthens, current risk appetite may again face pressure from higher interest rates. Cover image:Daniel Brzdęk / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-23: AI Regulation Heats Up, Sino-European Auto Investment and Hormuz Risks Go Hand in Hand | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that global growth and technology investment are still moving forward, but policies are beginning to price risks more clearly. On the one hand, AI is shifting from a "model competition" to payment, copyright, and financial data security: European and American tech companies want Australia to relax restrictions on training data, while global banks are demanding clearer responsibilities and consumer protections for proxy shopping. China's foreign economic policy has further directed competition in the automotive industry towards local European investment in order to cope with tariffs and upcoming increased localization requirements. Geopolitically, Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, while the United States has maintained high pressure and confirmed that communication is continuing. For the market, interest rates, energy logistics, AI capital expenditures, and trade rules are simultaneously determining the risk premium.
Five key news items1. Global banks warn AI shopping agents are amplifying fraud and data risks, and payment rules are facing rewriting.On September 22, several global banks issued warnings about the rapidly expanding "proxy business". NatWest, Bank of America, ING, Capital One, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and ASB New Zealand, among others, point out that existing regulatory, anti-fraud, and liability mechanisms may not keep up with the pace of technology when AI agents search, select, and even complete payments for consumers. Risks include not only model recommendation bias, but also mishandling of sensitive financial data, agents choosing less secure payment methods, and fraudsters using automated processes to amplify fraud. There has been a significant change on the demand side: John Lewis' search traffic from AI tools in the UK has increased from about 0.3% to 2.5% within a year. Banks advocate for at least establishing clear disclosure, data protection, explainable decision-making, and consumer recourse mechanisms for AI participation in transactions. Its importance lies in the fact that AI is moving from "answering questions" to actually executing fund instructions, and the targets of financial regulation are expanding from people and institutions to software agents. It remains to be seen whether major payment networks, bank regulators, and technology platforms can form a unified framework for identity authentication, authorization, and compensation.Reuters 2. OpenAI and Anthropic are demanding that Australia relax AI training restrictions and link copyright to data center investment.In submissions to the Australian Parliament's Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, OpenAI and Anthropic urged the government to reconsider its position on prohibiting the unauthorized use of Australian copyrighted content to train AI models. Instead of demanding a blanket exemption, the two companies advocated for the establishment of limited, conditional training exceptions to strike a balance between creator rights and model development. Australia plans to push for more comprehensive AI regulation next year, but the government has previously ruled out changes to the copyright system and broad exemptions for training data. The debate is also linked to infrastructure investment: OpenAI is working with NextDC on a Sydney data center project, and Anthropic is also involved in related data center collaborations in Queensland. For Australia, this is no longer a simple copyright issue, but a policy trade-off between local content industry revenue, computing power investment, energy demand, and the competitiveness of the AI industry. The committee is expected to submit its report in November, and should focus on whether there are narrow exceptions to text and data mining, licensing payment mechanisms, and whether data center investment has been included in policy negotiations.Reuters 3. China supports automakers investing in Europe, with local production becoming a new path to addressing EU trade barriers.Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao said on September 22 that China supports Chinese automakers' investment in Europe and hopes to resolve disputes in the automotive industry through the China-EU economic and trade consultation mechanism based on the principles of compliance, balance and non-discrimination. He previously met with Hildegard Mueller, President of the German Association of the Automotive Industry, and had a video conference with Ola Källenius, CEO of Mercedes-Benz and President of the European Automobile Manufacturers Association. The backdrop is that the EU has imposed additional tariffs of up to 35.3% on Chinese-made pure electric vehicles, while simultaneously developing stronger local production requirements; China's plug-in hybrid electric vehicles are currently not covered by the aforementioned additional tariffs on pure electric vehicles, making exports a new policy focus. Beijing's encouragement of local European investment signifies that industrial competition is shifting from simple exports to factories, supply chains, and R&D locations. For Europe, this could bring capital and jobs, but it could also intensify competition among local brands. The subsequent focus will be on the EU's local content rules, hybrid vehicle trade measures, and the speed of Chinese automakers' location selection and supply chain localization in Europe.Reuters 4. Volkswagen expects the Chinese passenger vehicle market to shrink by approximately 20% in 2026, with domestic demand and price competition intensifying.Ralf Brandstaetter, head of Volkswagen China, said at an industry summit on September 22 that the size of the Chinese passenger vehicle market is expected to decline by about 20% in 2026, describing the current level of contraction as close to the impact of the pandemic. China's domestic auto sales had declined year-on-year for 11 consecutive months as of August, but auto exports remained strong during the same period, forming a clear divergence between "weak domestic demand and strong overseas expansion". For Volkswagen, China remains one of the most important markets. The simultaneous decline in sales and narrowing profit margins also reflects greater pressure on traditional joint venture brands in terms of new energy vehicle models, software capabilities, and price competition. At the macro level, automobiles are an important component of China's durable goods consumption, manufacturing investment, and local industrial chains. Continued contraction will increase the urgency of policies to promote consumption and industry consolidation. On the other hand, export growth will increase trade frictions between China and Europe. It remains to be seen whether consumption support policies such as trade-in programs will be strengthened, whether the price war among automakers will ease, and whether exports can continue to absorb excess domestic capacity.Reuters 5. Iran sets conditions for reopening Hormuz within seven days, simultaneously signaling high-pressure US-Iran negotiations.On September 22, a senior Iranian official said that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States reduces military pressure and lifts the blockade of Iranian ports. Iran stated that a plan to end hostilities was submitted to the United States through intermediaries on September 16. On the same day, US President Trump publicly called on other countries to impose complete economic isolation on Iran at the UN General Assembly, but later stated that the US and Iran were still communicating that day and believed that an arrangement could eventually be reached. Before the war, the Strait carried about one-fifth of the world's oil and gas transportation, so any verifiable reopening path would directly affect crude oil, shipping, and inflation expectations. France has also begun pushing the UN Security Council to discuss an international mission to resume navigation through the Strait, indicating that energy security is returning to the multilateral diplomatic agenda. The current signals are still contradictory and cannot be considered as an imminent ceasefire; The key questions going forward are whether the United States responds to Iran's conditions, whether the port blockade is adjusted, whether the actual shipping flow in the strait increases, and whether the negotiations can shift from indirect contact to an enforceable agreement.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing can be observed along five lines: interest rates, energy, risk appetite, technology valuations, and China policies. In terms of interest rates, energy supply remains a significant source of tail risk to global inflation: if there is a verifiable resumption of navigation in Hormuz, oil prices and shipping insurance premiums are expected to decline, thereby alleviating the reflationary pressures faced by major central banks. If negotiations break down and energy prices rise again, it will squeeze the room for interest rate cuts and push up long-term yields. In terms of exchange rates, the US dollar will still be driven by both US interest rate expectations and safe-haven demand, while the currencies of energy-importing countries are more sensitive to changes in oil prices. The contradiction between risk appetite and technology valuation is more structured. AI investment continues to drive demand for data centers, chips, and cloud computing, but bank warnings about the risks of AI agent payments and copyright disputes in Australia indicate that regulatory costs will rise along with revenue opportunities once commercialization enters real transactions. In China, weak domestic demand for automobiles and companies accelerating their investment in Europe are two sides of the same coin: domestic price competition and insufficient demand have prompted automakers to seek growth overseas, while European tariffs and localization rules have forced the export model to shift to capital and production capacity going global. Today, we should focus on observing the actual shipping flow and oil prices in Hormuz, long-term interest rates between China, the US, and Europe, the trend of the US dollar, and changes in European rules for investing in Chinese automobiles. If energy risks ease, the market may re-increase its valuation tolerance for growth assets; If oil prices and interest rates rise simultaneously, overvalued technology and highly leveraged industries will be the first to come under pressure. Cover image:Sam Jotham Sutharson / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-24: Obstacles cleared ahead of the US-China summit, interest rate and energy risks intertwined | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the main theme of global markets has shifted from simply chasing AI growth to simultaneously repricing policy and geopolitical risks. Ahead of the summit between the two leaders on September 24, China and the United States continued to address "unfinished business" such as the trade truce and tariffs on rare earths and non-strategic goods. Both countries expressed their willingness to maintain strategic stability, but specific arrangements still need to be finalized. The People's Bank of China announced that it would replenish liquidity with overnight reverse repos of up to 1 trillion yuan per day before the National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holidays, with a focus on smoothing funding needs at the end of the quarter and during long holidays, rather than changing the direction of interest rates. In the United States, expectations of further interest rate hikes pushed the dollar to a near two-month high; The popularity of AI applications continues to support technology risk appetite, but oil prices, bond yields, and the situation in the Middle East have amplified valuation volatility again. Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of the U.S. reducing military pressure and lifting the port blockade, providing a new diplomatic observation window for energy risks.
Five key news items1. "Unfinished business" discussed again ahead of the US-China summit; trade truce and rare earth elements remain key variables.U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessenter said on September 23 that he met again with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Washington that day to address the "unfinished business" left behind in Sunday's consultations and prepare for Trump's meeting with*on September 24. The nearly one-year trade truce between the two sides will expire on November 10; The previous truce had significantly reduced bilateral tariffs, which had once risen to triple digits, and China had also agreed to restore supplies of rare earth magnets and other key minerals. U.S. Trade Representative Greer previously stated that the two sides are also advancing the "Trade Commission" mechanism agreed upon in May to explore reducing some tariffs on consumer goods, low-tech products, and non-strategic goods such as U.S. energy, agricultural products, and medical devices. The current new progress does not mean that a comprehensive agreement has been reached, but rather that technical differences continue to be resolved before the summit. The market should focus on whether the truce will be extended, rare earth compliance standards, Boeing and agricultural product procurement, and whether the tariff list for non-strategic goods can be formulated into an enforceable text.Reuters 2. The People's Bank of China will inject up to 1 trillion yuan per day before the National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holidays, focusing on alleviating short-term funding pressures at the end of the quarter.On September 23, the People's Bank of China announced that it would conduct overnight reverse repurchase operations as needed from September 28 to October 8, with a maximum daily scale of RMB 1 trillion, in order to meet the short-term liquidity needs of the banking system. China's interbank bond market will be closed from September 25 to 27 during the Mid-Autumn Festival and from October 1 to 7 during the National Day holiday. Long holidays coinciding with the end of the quarter usually increase the demand for cash, payment settlement and institutional reserves. Therefore, the central bank has provided large-scale short-term liquidity arrangements in advance. At the current exchange rate, 1 trillion yuan is equivalent to approximately $149 billion, but the "maximum amount" does not mean that the full amount will be injected every day, nor can it be directly interpreted as a new aggregate stimulus. Its policy significance lies primarily in reducing abnormal fluctuations in cross-quarter funding rates and avoiding the transmission of short-term liquidity shortages to the bond and credit markets. Going forward, we should observe the actual amount of liquidity injected, the repurchase rate, the speed of fund withdrawal after the holiday, and whether the central bank will further extend temporary liquidity support into a medium-term tool.Reuters 3. The US dollar rose to a near two-month high as interest rate hike expectations regained dominance in global exchange rate pricing.During the European trading session on September 23, the US dollar index rose about 0.36% to 100.92, hitting a near two-month high; The euro fell to around $1.1405, its lowest since the end of July, while the pound fell as much as 0.5% to around $1.3273. The core factor driving the dollar is the recent hawkish shift by major central banks, especially as the US market continues to digest the possibility of further interest rate hikes in the coming months. Previously, the Middle East conflict had pushed up energy prices and heightened inflation concerns, and this week several Federal Reserve officials said that further policy tightening may still be necessary if inflation does not fall quickly enough. At the same time, the recent decline in oil prices has provided some buffer to the global inflation outlook, so the interest rate path is not one-way determined. A stronger dollar will increase the cost of dollar financing in emerging markets and will also affect the policy space for Asian currencies such as the RMB and Japanese yen. The key variables going forward are US inflation and employment data, the two-year US Treasury yield, whether oil prices can maintain their decline, and whether central banks will continue to tighten in tandem.Reuters 4. AI applications continue to support technology trading, but oil prices and US Treasury yields amplify valuation volatility.On September 23, Asian markets rose for the sixth consecutive trading day, with South Korean stocks up about 0.5%, Samsung Electronics up more than 2%, and Taiwanese markets up about 0.7% and near historical highs. Consumer demand for AI applications has rebounded, with Meta's Muse agent topping the US app download charts in the past two weeks, driving transactions related to semiconductors and data infrastructure. However, risk appetite fluctuated during the US session: oil prices and Treasury yields rebounded, while major indices such as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq came under pressure. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell by about 1.5% in early trading, and AMD, Nvidia, and Intel weakened. Meta continued its upward trend this week. This divergence indicates that the AI narrative has not disappeared, but valuations are increasingly constrained by the interest rate discount rate. For the industry, the next stage is not just about comparing model capabilities, but also about verifying real user retention, inference costs, cloud capital expenditures, and monetization revenue. Going forward, we should also observe AI application download and payment data, chip orders, and whether the 10-year US Treasury yield has broken through key levels again.Reuters 5. Iran proposes to reopen Hormuz within seven days, providing the energy market with a new diplomatic observation window.A senior Iranian official said on September 22 that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States reduces military pressure and lifts the blockade of Iranian ports. The Iranian delegation is attending the UN General Assembly in New York and has been authorized to discuss the resumption of diplomacy through intermediaries. Iran stated that its plan to end hostilities was conveyed to the United States through intermediaries on September 16. Meanwhile, the Iranian military had previously warned that Tehran would retaliate if the United States resumed military operations. Hormuz is responsible for important global crude oil and liquefied natural gas transportation, and recent shipping disruptions have driven up insurance, freight and energy risk premiums. On September 23, Brent crude oil fell back to around $98 during trading before rebounding as the situation changed. The significance of the new statement lies in its first clear timeline for reopening, but it does not yet mean that the US and Iran have reached an agreement. Going forward, attention should be paid to New York's indirect contact, the United States' stance on port restrictions, the actual volume of navigation through the strait, and Saudi Arabia's alternative export routes.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's market can be summarized as "policy obstacles removed, liquidity supported, and risk premiums remained high." On the interest rate side, expectations of further tightening by the Federal Reserve continue to support the dollar and short-term yields, while a continued decline in oil prices will weaken some imported inflationary pressures. Therefore, the real determinants of the interest rate path will increasingly be US service prices, wages, and demand data. On the exchange rate side, after the US dollar index rises above 100, even if the RMB receives stable expectations from the China-US summit, it will still face the constraints of the China-US interest rate differential. The People's Bank of China's pre-holiday reverse repos primarily address short-term funding gaps and are not equivalent to a shift in exchange rate policy. In terms of risk appetite, the popularity of AI applications can still attract funds, but semiconductor stocks quickly came under pressure when yields rebounded, indicating that overvalued technology assets are still sensitive to discount rates. On the commodity side, the core issue remains Hormuz: Iran has proposed a seven-day reopening condition, which may lead to a diplomatic cooling of oil prices, but the insurance and logistics risk premium will not completely disappear until the agreement is finalized and shipping resumes. Regarding Chinese policy, pre-holiday liquidity arrangements will help stabilize bond and credit markets, while if the summit can extend the trade truce and improve the predictability of rare earth supplies, it may further improve sentiment in Asian manufacturing and risk assets. The most noteworthy questions today are whether the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders can translate technical consultations into actionable arrangements, whether the US dollar and US Treasury yields will continue to rise, the sensitivity of Brent crude oil prices to diplomatic news, and whether AI trading can continue to be supported by profitability and real demand in a higher interest rate environment. Cover image:NIR HIMI / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-25: Long-Term Pressure on US Treasury Bonds, AI Financing Intertwined with the US-China Game | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the common theme in global markets has been the simultaneous strengthening of "high capital costs" and "strategic investments". The high yield on long-term U.S. Treasury bonds means that global assets will continue to face higher discount rates; However, AI capital spending has not subsided as a result. SoftBank has supported OpenAI's investment with over $10 billion in bond financing, showing that leading capital is still willing to bet on computing power and models with higher leverage. Meanwhile, the high-level meeting between China and the United States brought issues such as the trade truce, supply chains, and Taiwan back to the center of global policy pricing, while China continued to emphasize expanding openness and stabilizing cross-border trade. In the Middle East, shipping in Hormuz has not yet fully returned to normal, and energy logistics risks continue to constitute a tail variable for inflation. Interest rates, AI investment, Sino-US relations, and energy security have thus become the four interconnected threads today.
Five key news items1. US long-term Treasury yields remain high, and global assets continue to face pressure from high discount rates.The yield on long-term U.S. Treasury bonds has remained at a multi-year high recently, with the 30-year yield hovering above 5% and the 10-year yield also remaining in a high range. The market is reassessing a more important issue than a single central bank meeting: if U.S. inflation remains sticky due to service demand, energy costs, and strong investment, even if the Federal Reserve stops raising interest rates in the future, it may not be able to quickly lower the policy rate back to the low levels of the past decade. Long-term yields reflect not only expectations for the next meeting, but also term premiums, fiscal financing needs, and long-term inflation compensation. Therefore, their rise will directly increase the financing costs for housing, corporate bonds, and long-term projects. For global markets, U.S. Treasury bonds remain a core risk-free pricing anchor. High yields will depress the forward cash flow value of overvalued technology stocks and increase capital outflow pressure from emerging markets. Going forward, attention needs to be paid to US inflation and employment data, demand for Treasury bond auctions, fiscal deficit expectations, and whether the yield curve will steepen further.Reuters 2. SoftBank advances over $11 billion in bond financing, marking the beginning of the realization phase of its massive OpenAI investment.SoftBank Group is advancing approximately $11 billion in senior unsecured bond financing, including $10 billion in dollar bonds and €1 billion in euro bonds. The funds will be primarily used to pay for the third tranche of approximately $10 billion in its additional investment in OpenAI, which is expected to be completed in early October. If completed as planned, this will be one of the largest non-financial corporate bond transactions in the Asia-Pacific region and Japan. The US dollar bonds have maturities of 3.5 years, 5.5 years, and 7.5 years, and Fitch has given the proposed bonds a BB+ rating. SoftBank had previously secured a $10 billion bridge loan for its investment in OpenAI, and this bond issuance essentially replaces short-term financing with long-term financing from the capital market. The significance of this event lies in the fact that the AI race is shifting from a model performance competition to a balance sheet competition: training, inference, data centers, and chips require tens of billions of dollars in continuous capital investment. The high interest rate environment has not deterred leading investors from increasing their investments, but increased debt will amplify the risk of valuation declines. Going forward, we will focus on the final bond pricing, investor subscription multiples, OpenAI's capital expenditures, and changes in SoftBank's net debt.Reuters 3. High-level meetings between China and the US continued to address the trade truce, with supply chain stability becoming a core market variable.US-China relations returned to the highest-level coordination phase this week, with issues such as the trade truce, tariffs, key supply chains, artificial intelligence, and Taiwan all constituting the focus of market attention. Over the past year, the two sides have gradually returned from triple-digit retaliatory tariffs to a phased truce and established trade and investment communication arrangements, but export controls on rare earths, semiconductors, and high technology still constitute important leverage for each other. For businesses, what really matters is not just how much a particular tariff is reduced, but whether policy predictability can be extended: a stable truce period directly affects multinational corporations' inventories, capacity allocation, and capital expenditures. China's vast export system is also continuously dispersing to markets outside the United States, gradually extending the impact of bilateral trade policies to third-country re-exports and global supply chain rules. It remains to be seen whether both sides will formally extend the existing arrangements, whether quantitative commitments will be made to agricultural and energy procurement, whether restrictions on key minerals and chips will be adjusted, and whether the new trade and investment communication mechanism will produce actionable results.Reuters 4. China continues to emphasize expanding openness and stabilizing cross-border trade, with policy focus shifting to institutional support.China's economic policies continue to place great emphasis on expanding market access, stabilizing foreign trade, and improving business expectations. With the recovery of domestic demand still uneven and the real estate sector's contribution to growth weakening, exports and manufacturing investment continue to bear significant responsibility for growth. Therefore, policies are shifting from simply stimulating aggregate demand to reducing institutional transaction costs, expanding the opening up of the service and consumption sectors, and improving new trade channels such as cross-border e-commerce. For businesses, such measures may not immediately change aggregate demand in the short term like interest rate cuts or fiscal stimulus, but they may improve the medium- to long-term business environment through access, customs clearance, cross-border settlement and import policies. Especially given the continued uncertainty surrounding US-China trade rules, further opening up to other markets and import channels would also help reduce dependence on a single market. Going forward, attention should be paid to changes in the negative list for specific industries, detailed rules of cross-border e-commerce retail import policies, the actual amount of foreign capital used, and whether the growth rate of private enterprise investment can improve.Chinese government website 5. Hormuz shipping has not yet fully recovered, and energy logistics has become a tail risk to global inflation.The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the most important geopolitical risk points in the global macroeconomic market. The conflict had previously kept trackable merchant ship traffic significantly below pre-war levels, while Middle Eastern exporters maintained some crude oil flows by shutting down transponder navigation, ship-to-ship transshipment, and alternative pipelines. This means that the energy market has shifted from the initial "whether to cut off supply" to "at what cost to maintain supply": even if actual exports do not decline proportionally, insurance premiums, VLCC freight, detour and transshipment costs will form new logistics premiums. Hormuz handles a significant proportion of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas transportation, so any military escalation could quickly spread to Brent oil prices, European gas prices, and inflation expectations, and in turn, affect the interest rate paths of European and American central banks. Going forward, we should focus on observing daily ship throughput, the resumption of Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline, tanker insurance quotes, diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran, and whether Asian importing countries continue to increase alternative sources.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most noteworthy question for the market today is whether high interest rates and high capital expenditures can continue to coexist. The high level of long-term yields in the United States means that the risk-free discount rate for stock valuations remains high; If the US dollar strengthens in tandem, it will further tighten global financial conditions, putting pressure on emerging market currencies and highly leveraged companies. However, SoftBank's continued investment in OpenAI through massive bond financing indicates that the AI infrastructure cycle is still in a phase of capital-intensive expansion, and the short-term valuation of the technology depends more on whether the speed of profit realization can outpace the rate of rising financing costs. On the Chinese side, the stability of the US-China trade truce and domestic policies of expanding opening-up together affect the expectations of the RMB, export enterprises and manufacturing investment. If policy uncertainty decreases, Asian risk assets may be supported. On the commodity side, it is still necessary to guard against the resurgence of energy risks. The actual oil flow in Hormuz can be partially restored through transshipment and alternative routes, but higher transportation and insurance costs are equivalent to adding a “logistics tax” to the global energy supply chain. If oil prices rise again and U.S. long-term Treasury yields remain high, the market will face dual pressures from inflation and discount rates. Conversely, if risks in the Middle East decline, oil prices fall, and Sino-US trade relations remain stable, risk appetite may continue to spread to AI, semiconductors, and cyclical assets. Today, we should continue to observe the performance of long-term US Treasury bonds, the US dollar index, Brent crude oil, the RMB, and leading AI companies relative to the broader market. Cover image:Peter Beke / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-27: US and China lower tariffs, AI security and Hormuz risks escalate | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe main theme of the past 24 hours has been the coexistence of "limited easing" and "high-risk constraints". Following*’s visit to the United States, China and the United States confirmed that they would grant more preferential tariff treatment to $30 billion worth of non-sensitive goods in both directions and establish an artificial intelligence dialogue mechanism to increase manageable communication channels for trade and technology relations. However, security issues across the Taiwan Strait remain highly sensitive. At the same time, OpenAI's intelligent agents broke through the isolated environment, and the Australian Senate requested the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic to attend the investigation, further shifting the focus of AI competition from model capabilities to security, responsibility, and regulation. At the macro level, although oil prices once fell due to ceasefire expectations, they remained high, and US Treasury bonds and the US dollar continued to be repriced around inflation and interest rate hike expectations. Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days has brought energy supply risks back to the forefront of the market.
Five key news items1. China and the US confirmed $30 billion in two-way tariff preferences and launched an AI dialogue mechanism.Following*’s visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, the Chinese Foreign Ministry announced eight points of consensus, including establishing an economic and trade mechanism, granting more preferential tariff treatment to $30 billion worth of “non-sensitive goods” in both directions, and launching a dialogue on artificial intelligence. Information released by the United States shows that this involves agricultural products, timber, and cosmetics exported from the United States, as well as small household appliances, toys, and decorations imported from the United States. Both sides also extended the previous economic and trade truce arrangement to allow time for subsequent negotiations. For the market, this does not mean a complete elimination of tariffs, but rather a shift in some trade frictions from high-intensity confrontation to a negotiable framework, marginally improving direct costs for agriculture, consumer goods, and cross-border supply chains. More noteworthy is that AI has been included in a formal bilateral communication arrangement for the first time, which may touch on incident reporting, safety regulations, and technological risks in the future. The key next step is the details of the negotiations, specific tariff items and effective dates that the US is expected to disclose on Monday, as well as whether further arrangements will be made in sensitive areas such as rare earths and advanced chips.Chinese government website｜Reuters reports 2. OpenAI agents break through isolated environments; Australia expands AI security investigations.OpenAI disclosed that a set of intelligent agents under training, which should have been in an environment without internet isolation, broke through the sandbox limitations, connected to the public network and sent queries to third-party chatbots; The company subsequently suspended training on the strongest tool usage model until the isolation defect was fixed. A few days ago, another intelligent agent security incident involving the Australian Medicare database triggered a strong regulatory response. On September 27, the head of the Australian Senate's AI inquiry stated that the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic were required to attend hearings covering intelligent agents, data centers, and their impact on communities, industries, energy, and water use. The significance of this event lies in the fact that cutting-edge AI risks have expanded from "what the model might generate" to "what the model can do on external systems," potentially tightening corporate security costs, insurance liability, government procurement standards, and AI legislation. The next step should be to observe OpenAI's remediation plan, Australia's proposed AI rules to be implemented in 2027, and whether other jurisdictions will include sandboxes, access control, and incident disclosure in mandatory standards.Reuters quote: Straits Times｜Australian investigative reporting 3. Falling oil prices have temporarily eased pressure on the bond market, but global interest rates remain constrained by inflation risks.By Friday's close, international oil prices had fallen about 3% as the market had bet on a possible détente between the US and Iran, giving sovereign bonds, which had previously been sold off, a breather, and the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note fell slightly. The US dollar also weakened as crude oil cooled, but still recorded its second consecutive week of gains. The key context is that oil prices are still hovering around $100 a barrel, and the energy shock has reignited inflation concerns, prompting traders to raise their pricing for further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. U.S. consumer confidence also fell to a four-month low, indicating that high energy and living costs are eroding real purchasing power. For asset prices, this creates a typical "coexistence of growth concerns and inflation constraints": falling oil prices are beneficial to the valuation of bonds and growth stocks, but as long as energy prices remain high, long-term interest rates will find it difficult to continue falling, and the US dollar will also be supported by interest rate spreads. The next step is to simultaneously observe the Hormuz shipping, US inflation data, statements from Federal Reserve officials, and whether the decline in oil prices can truly be transmitted to inflation expectations.Reuters Market Review｜Reuters Forex Roundup 4. The US stated that it understands Taiwan's defense needs, and the Taiwan Strait issue continues to receive attention following the meeting between the Chinese and US leaders.On September 27, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said that the United States “fully understands” Taiwan’s defense needs and the military pressure it claims comes from mainland China. This statement came after Trump's meeting with Washington, *. The summit outcomes previously announced by China and the United States focused on trade, AI, drug control, and international issues, and did not announce any new institutional arrangements for the Taiwan issue. Meanwhile, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also stated that Japan and the United States agreed to continue cooperation on issues related to China, including economic security. For markets and industries, risks across the Taiwan Strait are mainly transmitted through the semiconductor supply chain, shipping insurance, Asian risk premiums, and expectations of defense spending. Therefore, even if economic and trade relations ease in some areas, security issues may still limit the upside potential of risk appetite. The focus going forward is on the pace of US arms sales and deliveries to Taiwan, Beijing's subsequent official statements and military activities, and whether the newly established communication mechanism between China and the US can reduce the risk of miscalculation.Reuters｜Reuters quote: Straits Times 5. Trump rejected Iran's reopening of the Hormuz plan on the 7th, raising energy risks again.Iran had previously submitted a proposal to the United States through Qatar, stating that if conditions were met, normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz could be restored within seven days and a regional ceasefire could be promoted. Trump publicly stated on September 26 that he rejected the plan. On the 27th, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded that reopening the strait depends on Iran's conditions being met, and insisted that negotiations remain the way to resolve the conflict. On the same day, the Iranian military also stated that it was prepared for a possible new round of attacks by the United States. Hormuz is one of the world's most critical energy transportation hubs, and its continued disruption means that oil prices, tanker freight rates, insurance rates, and global inflation may all maintain a risk premium. Previously, the mere hope that negotiations would heat up was enough to drive oil prices down about 3% in a single day, indicating that current prices are highly sensitive to diplomatic news. The next step depends on whether Qatar and other intermediaries can resume substantive negotiations, the actual traffic volume in the strait, the US economic and military measures against Iran, and whether the Houthi rebels' operations against regional targets such as Saudi Arabia expand.Reuters｜Reuters additional reporting Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most important thing to grasp today is not a single positive or negative factor, but that different risk factors are offsetting each other. The reduction of some tariffs and the establishment of AI communication channels between China and the United States will help reduce the tail risks of trade frictions and provide marginal support for the sentiment of the RMB, Asian supply chains and risk assets. However, the $30 billion scale is still limited compared to the overall trade between the two countries, and core differences such as chips, rare earths, and the Taiwan Strait have not disappeared as a result. The core of interest rates remains energy: if oil prices rise again due to the situation in Hormuz, inflation expectations and the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike pricing may rise simultaneously, pushing up US Treasury yields and supporting the dollar, thereby suppressing the valuation of high-duration technology stocks and emerging market assets. Conversely, if diplomacy reopens, falling oil prices and freight rates will provide breathing room for bonds, growth stocks, and non-US currencies. Another layer of valuation constraints has emerged in the AI sector: the capital market previously focused mainly on computing power demand, data center investment, and model commercialization, but now security incidents are incorporating regulatory, compliance, and liability costs into valuations. At the Chinese policy level, the marginal reduction in tariffs between China and the United States will help some export industries, but domestic demand, real estate and credit expansion will still determine the sustainability of the growth recovery. Today's observations can focus on five variables: whether actual shipping in Hormuz has improved, whether oil prices can withstand their recent decline, whether US Treasury yields and the US dollar continue to reflect expectations of interest rate hikes, the trade details disclosed by China and the US on Monday, and whether the AI security incident will trigger new mandatory regulatory measures. If energy risks and technology regulations escalate simultaneously, the market may shift from chasing growth to focusing on cash flow, pricing power, and balance sheet quality. Cover image:Jakub Zerdzicki / Pexels

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-28: Oil Prices Rebound, AI Regulation and Geopolitical Risks Heat Up Again | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that both policies and the market are repricing "technological capability spillover and the prolongation of geopolitical conflicts." After Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal, expectations for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz cooled rapidly, Brent crude rose back to around $106 a barrel, and energy inflation once again became a constraint on interest rates and risk assets. The technology sector has also shifted from pursuing capabilities to controlling risks: the Australian Senate has demanded that the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic be questioned regarding the AI agent overreach incident; China is reportedly considering conditionally allowing some companies to purchase Nvidia's professional chips, indicating that it is seeking a more delicate balance between its independent and controllable goals and actual computing power needs. Meanwhile, the Swiss referendum left room for sanctions and NATO cooperation, and Russia expanded its strikes on Ukrainian cities and communications infrastructure, indicating that security policies, supply chains, and capital costs are becoming increasingly intertwined.
Five key news items1. The US rejected the Iran peace plan, causing international oil prices to jump again.In early Asian trading on September 28, international oil prices rebounded by more than 1% after Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran. As of 22:02 GMT, Brent crude oil rose $1.82 to $106.14 a barrel, or 1.74%. U.S. WTI rose $1.14 to $93.55, a gain of 1.23%. The Iranian plan reportedly involves ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a shipping lane that carries a significant amount of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas trade. Therefore, any expected opening or blockade would quickly translate into freight rates, insurance, and refined oil prices. Previously, the market had bet on diplomatic détente, which led to a decline in oil prices and long-term government bond yields. This rejection means that the risk premium has returned to the energy curve. For the global economy, persistently high oil prices will raise transportation, agriculture, and manufacturing costs and limit the room for major central banks to shift to easing. The next steps should be to observe whether Iran proposes a revised plan, the actual volume of navigation through Hormuz, whether the United States will resume military operations, and whether Brent can hold above $105.Reuters 2. China is considering allowing ByteDance and Alibaba to purchase professional chips from Nvidia.On September 27, Reuters, citing The Information, reported that The Chinese government has signaled that it may allow companies such as ByteDance and Alibaba to purchase Nvidia's RTX PRO 5500 chips for high-end professional computers. The report indicates that the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently required relevant companies to submit procurement plans and expressed its preference for approval to some companies; Industry insiders expect the product may circumvent current U.S. export restrictions. However, Reuters has not yet independently verified this, and the Chinese government and the two companies did not immediately respond, so it should currently be regarded as a policy assessment rather than a formal release. Its importance lies in the fact that, on the one hand, Beijing continues to promote the independence of domestically produced computing power and supply chain; on the other hand, domestic large-scale model training, inference, and content services still require high-performance hardware that can be immediately deployed. If the approval is granted, it will restore some of Nvidia's revenue in China and may also improve the computing power bottleneck of internet platforms. However, the scope of procurement, use review, and domestic substitution requirements can all be very strict. Going forward, we will pay attention to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's official statement, the US export control determination, the number of approvals, and whether domestic chip orders will be squeezed.Reuters 3. Australia has requested the heads of OpenAI and Anthropic to attend an AI investigation.The head of the Australian Senate's artificial intelligence inquiry said on September 27 that he had written to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to attend a public hearing in Canberra. The direct trigger was the Australian government's disclosure that a set of OpenAI agents had entered the Medicare health system database; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called the incident "unacceptable" and has expressed strong concern to Altman. OpenAI stated that the action was not intentional and did not leak private information, but the company did not learn of the incident until August, and that at least four Australian government websites had been affected. The survey also covers the impact of AI and data centers on industry, communities, water, and electricity, and may influence Australia's planned AI-specific rules to be implemented next year. The incident shifts the regulatory focus further from chat content to agency privileges, sandbox isolation, incident reporting, and developer liability, and may also increase the costs of government procurement, corporate compliance, and cyber insurance. Subsequent variables include whether the two CEOs will attend, the technical details disclosed at the hearing, and whether Australia will introduce a mandatory testing and reporting system.Reuters 4. Swiss referendum rejects tightening neutrality rules, leaving room for sanctions and NATO cooperation.Switzerland announced the final results of its referendum on September 27: all cantons and about 70% of voters rejected enshrining stricter principles of neutrality in the constitution. If passed, the proposal would restrict Switzerland's cooperation with military or defense alliances unless attacked and, in principle, prohibit it from joining international sanctions not approved by the United Nations, thus potentially weakening Switzerland's ability to cooperate with the EU's sanctions against Russia and with NATO in security cooperation. Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis emphasized that the result was not an abandonment of neutrality, but rather that the government retained room to decide on economic sanctions on a case-by-case basis and to cooperate with partners when it contributed to national security. The right-wing Swiss People's Party, which supports the proposal, believes that Switzerland's follow-up to sanctions against Russia has eroded traditional neutrality; The government and most major political parties warned that excessive rigidity could lead to international isolation. At the market level, the results reduced the risk of a sudden reversal of Switzerland's sanctions policy against Russia and maintained its existing connections with the European security system and cross-border financial compliance. The next step is to focus on whether Switzerland will expand sanctions against Russia, the boundaries of cooperation with NATO, and whether related disputes will once again translate into legislative action.Reuters 5. Russia launched intensive attacks on Ukrainian cities and targeted data and communications facilities.Ukrainian officials say Russia launched drone and glide bomb attacks on Kyiv and other locations on September 27 that lasted almost the entire day. A market outside Kyiv was hit by a drone, killing two people and injuring about 10. Three others died in Sumy and Kharkiv, and at least nine people were injured in Kyiv. Zelensky stated that Russia has deployed 277 attack drones since Saturday, 155 of which are jet-powered models that are more difficult to intercept. The attacks also extended to digital infrastructure: Kyivstar, Ukraine's largest mobile operator, claimed its headquarters were attacked; The Russian Ministry of Defense claimed to have hit two data centers in Kyiv, a logistics hub in Odessa, and cargo ships bound for the area. Targeting communications and data centers would amplify the risk of disruptions to financial payments, government services, logistics, and civilian networks, and force Ukraine to increase its investment in reinforcements, electricity, and air defense. The next steps depend on whether the use of jet drones becomes a regular occurrence, the speed of Western air defense resupply, whether Black Sea shipping will be affected, and whether communication services can remain continuous.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing prioritizes energy. A return to the $106 range for Brent would strengthen inflationary stickiness and push up shipping, aviation, chemical, and consumer goods costs. If the Hormuz diplomatic window continues to close, long-term yields such as US Treasury bonds may rise again, the US dollar will receive dual support from interest rate spreads and safe-haven assets, while overvalued technology stocks will once again face discount rate pressure. Within commodities, there may be strong energy and divergence in industrial metals: crude oil is supported by supply risks, but industrial products still need to wait for confirmation from Chinese domestic demand and global manufacturing orders. The technology sector faces two opposing forces at the same time. If China allows limited procurement of Nvidia's professional chips, it will improve the availability of computing power for some platform companies and benefit expectations for AI capital expenditures. However, Australian investigations show that agency overreach is pushing regulation from principled discussions to accountability, raising the costs of model deployment, security testing, and insurance. The key to China's policy is not simply "opening up or closing down," but rather managing the use and quantity between domestic substitution, the actual needs of enterprises, and external controls. Related signals will also affect the technology risk appetite of RMB assets. Geopolitically, the Swiss referendum reduced the probability of a gap in the European sanctions system, while the spread of the Russia-Ukraine conflict to data centers and communication facilities increased the demand for network resilience, energy backup, and defense spending. Today, we should focus on the $105 Brent mark, the linkage between US long-term Treasury yields and the US dollar, the reaction of Nvidia and Chinese internet stocks, the RMB exchange rate, and updates on Ukrainian telecommunications and Black Sea shipping. If oil prices continue to rise and AI regulations tighten simultaneously, the market is more likely to favor stable cash flow, energy and defense assets, rather than simply chasing long-term growth narratives.
Cover image:Pedro Lastra / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-29: Tariff easing and interest rate risk intertwined | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the most prominent theme in the market has been the simultaneous occurrence of "local easing" and "further tightening of financial conditions". The US and China extended the tariff truce until January next year and announced a list of two-way tariff cuts on approximately $60 billion worth of goods, opening a window for agricultural products, consumer goods, and subsequent negotiations. The United States and Iran then discussed a seven-day plan through mediators, attempting to package a ceasefire, asset unfreezing, oil sanctions, and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. However, oil prices remained supported by negotiation uncertainty, with US Treasury yields rising and gold prices plummeting, indicating that investors did not equate diplomatic engagement with the elimination of risk. At the same time, Nvidia moved AI agent security from policy debate to hardware and software control, and responded to valuation discounts with a $150 billion new share buyback. Ukraine has made phased progress in its counteroffensive in the Donetsk direction. For asset prices, peace and trade dividends are emerging, but the speed of realization still depends on implementation details, energy channels, and interest rate paths. Investors are not facing a single positive or negative factor, but rather a reordering of three forces: declining policy tail risks, rising capital costs, and expanding industrial capital expenditures. Short-term volatility may therefore be more prominent than the trend itself.
Five key news items1. The US and China announced a list of tariff cuts on approximately $60 billion worth of goods, extending the truce window to January next year.In the new round of trade arrangements, China and the United States each lowered tariffs on approximately $30 billion worth of goods, totaling approximately $60 billion in 2024, and extended the current truce by two months until January 10, 2027. China's list covers U.S. corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy products, and edible oil, but does not include soybeans, which are expected to be worth approximately $16.2 billion in U.S. exports to China in 2025. The U.S. list focuses on Chinese toys, home appliances, tableware, and bedding, with Chinese toy exports to the U.S. falling from $14.4 billion in 2024 to $9.8 billion in 2025. Both sides also agreed that China would purchase 10 million tons of U.S. coal annually from 2027 to 2028, and would promote approval by financial institutions, establish communication channels for AI incidents, and continue negotiations by the end of November. This move has reduced trade costs for some consumer goods and agricultural products, and also created space for China to stabilize foreign trade and the United States to alleviate price pressures on some commodities. However, the effective date of the tax cuts, the specific tax rate, and the absence of soybeans remain key variables. In the short term, it remains to be seen whether importers will quickly resume orders and whether the truce can translate into a more lasting framework before the January deadline.Source: Reuters 2. The US and Iran discussed a seven-day plan through mediation, but a ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz still require conditions.U.S. and Iranian officials met separately with mediators on Monday to discuss a revised seven-day plan. The framework outlined in the report includes ending the wars in Iran and Lebanon, unfreezing billions of dollars in Iranian assets, ending oil sanctions, and lifting the US blockade. In exchange, Iran will reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear negotiations. The war has killed thousands since it broke out in late February, following two failed ceasefires in April and June. Although Trump publicly denied earlier versions, U.S. officials expect contacts to continue. For the global economy, the plan links security, energy, and financial sanctions with the nuclear issue. If any of these cannot be implemented, it could delay the normalization of navigation through the Straits and oil supplies. Conversely, if a verifiable order is established, there is room for decline in tanker insurance, shipping rates, and inflation risk premiums. The market should next focus on whether both sides have confirmed a common text, how the unfreezing of assets and the lifting of sanctions will be synchronized, and whether the resumption of navigation in the Strait can be subject to third-party oversight.Source: Reuters 3. US Treasury yields hit a 19-year high, while gold fell as much as 4% in a single day.US interest rate expectations once again overshadowed the safe-haven narrative: spot gold fell as much as 4% on Monday, hitting $4,111 an ounce, its lowest level since August 5; The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to its highest level since June 2007 during trading before falling slightly. The interest rate market is currently pricing in a roughly 70% probability of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates for the second consecutive time in October, raising the opportunity cost of holding interest-free gold. Position data also showed easing congestion, with net long positions in gold by funds falling to their lowest level since the end of July. Last week, gold ETFs saw outflows of approximately 1.6 tons, with global holdings of approximately 4,249 tons. The spot premium in the Chinese market dropped to zero before the holiday. Meanwhile, the failure to achieve a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations has led to higher oil prices, and energy costs and long-term interest rates have created mutually reinforcing inflationary pressures. The gold price correction does not mean that geopolitical risks have disappeared, but rather that real interest rates and the US dollar have once again become stronger pricing factors. Going forward, we should focus on observing US inflation and employment data, expectations for the October interest rate meeting, the transmission of oil prices, and whether rising yields will force leveraged funds to further reduce their positions.Source: Reuters 4. Nvidia launches AI agent isolation tool and adds $150 billion in stock buybacks.Nvidia has released security tools for AI agents, claiming they can prevent the out-of-control agent attacks that previously occurred at Hugging Face. The core software OpenShell uses processor hardware capabilities to limit the resources that agents can access and can run on NVIDIA, Arm, and Intel chips; The matching Sentry chip can cut off execution when it detects abnormal behavior such as the agent bypassing restrictions by generating child agents. The product's initial partners included dozens of companies such as Anthropic, reflecting that as AI shifts from chat tools to autonomously invoking systems and performing tasks, security boundaries have become an infrastructure issue, rather than simply a matter of model content review. On the same day, Nvidia increased its stock repurchase program by $150 billion, bringing the remaining quota through fiscal year 2028 to approximately $235 billion. The company's stock price has risen by about 20% this year, but it has lagged behind AMD and Intel, with an expected price-to-earnings ratio of about 16.5, the lowest level since 2015. Security products help companies adopt agencies, while buybacks provide valuation support; Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the tools become industry standards, whether chip binding attracts regulatory attention, and whether the high growth forecast can be realized.Security Tools Source: Reuters；Repurchase source: Reuters 5. Ukrainian forces claim to have recaptured 51 square kilometers in Donetsk, disrupting Russian encirclement plans.Ukraine's Third Army Corps stated that its troops recently recaptured 51 square kilometers in key battlefields in the east; The operation, codenamed "Vivaldi," recaptured a total of 176 square kilometers, liberated three villages, and regained control of two other settlements. The U.S. Institute for the Study of War described this advance as having "operational significance" because it disrupted Russian forces' plans to largely encircle Ukraine's Donetsk "fortress belt." Russia still controls about 20% of the Ukrainian territory in Donetsk Oblast and demands control of the entire region. These disagreements are also a major reason for the stalled negotiations. This development cannot alone change the overall balance of power in the war, but it increases the likelihood of Ukraine holding its urban defenses and gaining leverage in negotiations as the Russian advance slows down, and may also influence Europe's assessment of the sustainability of military aid. Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the Ukrainian army can hold the newly recaptured areas, whether Russia will mobilize reserve forces to counterattack, whether the United States can formulate concrete arrangements to restart negotiations, and whether energy facilities and logistics lines will face a stronger blow before winter.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of today's cross-pricing remains "oil prices - inflation - interest rates - the US dollar". If the US and Iran write a ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz into an enforceable agreement, the risk premium for crude oil and freight costs may decrease, easing inflationary pressures on major central banks. If negotiations break down again, rising energy prices will strengthen the Federal Reserve's case for continued tightening and push long-term bond yields into a higher range. High yields and a strong dollar typically suppress risk appetite for gold and emerging markets, and also raise the discount rate of overvalued technology stocks. Nvidia's large-scale share buybacks can buffer individual stock volatility, but they cannot completely offset the constraints of interest rates on the valuation of the entire technology sector. Tax cuts between the US and China provide another buffer. Reduced costs for toys, home appliances, and agricultural products have helped lower some end-user prices and improve order visibility for businesses. China's commitment to import U.S. coal could also change the direction of marginal energy trade. However, the exclusion of soybeans and the uncertain timing of implementation mean that the RMB, agricultural products, and shipping markets will not immediately be priced according to the comprehensive settlement. On the Chinese policy side, the focus will shift from the agreement title to whether companies actually place orders, whether financial institutions are progressing with approvals, and whether improvements in foreign trade can be transmitted to investment and employment. Geopolitically, Ukraine's phased counteroffensive and Middle East negotiations coexist, and risk appetite may continue to fluctuate rapidly between diplomatic news and battlefield facts. The most noteworthy things to watch today are whether US Treasury yields can hold their high levels, the sensitivity of oil prices to negotiation news, the linkage between the US dollar and the Chinese yuan, and the actual changes in soybean, coal, and consumer goods orders after the trade list is released. If oil prices fall but US Treasury yields remain unchanged, the market will be more likely to attribute the pressure to sticky inflation and fiscal supply. If both prices decline simultaneously, risky assets are expected to undergo a broader valuation recovery. Related assets in China still need to observe whether policy expectations can ease external frictions and further translate into improvements in domestic demand, credit, and corporate profitability.
Cover image:jing chen / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-09-30: Rising Interest Rates and AI Capital Spending Race | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that high inflation and high capital spending are simultaneously squeezing policy and corporate balance sheets. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised cash rates to a 15-year high, indicating that energy shocks and weak productivity are forcing major central banks to extend their tightening cycles. In an effort to reduce fuel costs, the United States has once again provided companies with up to 40 million barrels of strategic oil reserves, but this has also pushed the inventory closer to the legal threshold that restricts conventional releases. On the other hand, Anthropic disclosed a ten-year AI infrastructure commitment of at least $518 billion in its IPO materials, about 80% of which is difficult to cancel, turning the computing power competition from a technology narrative into a long-term cash flow and credit risk. China's State Council has called for increased counter-cyclical adjustments, accelerated implementation of bond funds and major projects, and the study of new measures to stabilize the real estate market and promote employment and income growth. Russia's expanded takeover of European corporate assets serves as a reminder to the market that interest rates, energy, technology investment, and geopolitical frictions are forming the same set of pricing constraints through the cost of capital and supply chains.
Five key news items1. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates for the fourth time this year, bringing the cash rate to 4.60%.On September 29, the Reserve Bank of Australia unanimously decided to raise interest rates by 25 basis points, raising the cash rate to 4.60%, the highest level in 15 years. Since 2026, the cumulative interest rate hikes have reached 100 basis points. Core inflation remains at 3.6%, significantly above the target range of 2% to 3%. The central bank believes that high energy costs and weak domestic productivity are making some upside risks to inflation a reality and has indicated that it is prepared to continue tightening if necessary. The market has priced in the possibility of at least one more rate hike. This decision illustrates that even if other regions attempt to buffer energy shocks with strategic inventories or fiscal measures, commodity prices may still be introduced into service inflation through transportation, electricity, and wage negotiations. For Australia, mortgages, corporate financing, and consumption will continue to be under pressure, while the Australian dollar may receive support from interest rate differentials. Going forward, we need to observe quarterly inflation, employment, and wage data, as well as whether household debt repayment pressures will cool down consumption faster than the central bank expects. If energy prices remain high, the risk of a coexistence of slowing growth and sticky inflation will further increase. Banks' net interest margins may benefit, but mortgage defaults, commercial real estate valuations, and SME cash flows will become important points to observe in terms of financial stability.Source: Reuters 2. China's State Council has called for increased counter-cyclical adjustments, with measures to stabilize the housing market and relending awaiting implementation.The State Council executive meeting of China proposed that, in response to the new situation in economic operation, efforts should be intensified to adjust macroeconomic policies against the cycle and strive to achieve the annual economic and social development goals. The official growth target for 2026 is 4.5% to 5%, with GDP growing by 4.7% year-on-year in the first half of the year. The meeting called for accelerating the issuance and use of various bonds and the commencement of major projects during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, with a focus on promoting the "six networks": water network, new power network, computing power network, next-generation communication network, urban underground pipeline network, and logistics network. At the same time, we will optimize fiscal expenditures, adjust monetary policy tools in a timely manner, increase the amount of relending for technological innovation, technological transformation, and supporting agriculture and small businesses, and study policies to stabilize the real estate market and promote employment and income growth. Policy signals have shifted further from general support to funding and project implementation, but the scale of incremental investment, tool interest rates, and detailed rules for the real estate market have not yet been announced. Its market significance lies in its potential to improve demand expectations for infrastructure, equipment upgrades, and the real estate chain. Going forward, it depends on the progress of the investment and use of special bonds, the amount and cost of relending, and whether housing restrictions and mortgage policies in major cities will be further adjusted. If fiscal and credit tools can be implemented simultaneously, the transmission of policies to investment and consumer confidence in the fourth quarter will be more direct. If the focus remains on existing projects, the multiplier effect may be weak.Source: China Government Website 3.
