entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-02: High Bond Market Pressure and Tightening Global Fuel Supply | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the common theme in global markets has shifted from "whether central banks will raise interest rates next" to "whether energy shortages and long-term financing costs can be alleviated simultaneously." The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to 5.34% intraday, the highest since 2002, before falling as Federal Reserve officials hinted at a possible pause in October. However, Chinese refineries suspended exports of refined oil products to regions outside Hong Kong and Macau, and Russia extended its ban on diesel exports, pushing Brent crude oil back above $100 per barrel. AI capital expenditures have also entered a more complex financing phase: Broadcom plans to provide Anthropic with a loan of up to $42 billion, while also serving as its chip design and computing equipment supplier, with industry orders, credit risks, and conflicts of interest intertwined. Geopolitically, the United States has expanded sanctions against Iran's railway and automotive industries, while Russia has warned the West against escalating the Kaliningrad dispute through nuclear deterrence. The start of the fourth quarter indicates that even with a brief pause in policy interest rates, energy, geopolitics, and AI investments are likely to maintain high market discount rates.
Five key news items1. The 10-year US Treasury yield hit 5.34%, and Federal Reserve officials lowered expectations for an October rate hike.The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to 5.34% on Thursday, the highest since 2002, before falling back to about 5.237%. Previously, US Treasury bonds experienced one of their worst quarters since 1994, and global long-term financing costs rose accordingly. New York Federal Reserve President Williams and Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Jefferson said that the next step can wait for more data, and the market has therefore shifted its expectations from an October rate hike to a more likely one in December. Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari still expects further tightening before 2027, but is unsure whether action will be taken this month. Stagnant manufacturing activity, rising input prices, and a drop in initial jobless claims to 197,000 continued to diverge inflation and growth signals. The stock market barely closed higher after yields fell, with the S&P 500 rising 0.20%. The key issues going forward are non-farm payrolls, energy prices, and long-term bond buying: even if the probability of short-term interest rate hikes decreases, housing, corporate credit, and technology valuations will still be under pressure if term premiums and fiscal supply continue to push up long-term yields. The market also needs to determine whether overseas buyers view the current yield as a value range or demand higher risk compensation. This choice will affect dollar liquidity and global asset repricing.Source: Reuters；Market Data 2. Chinese refineries suspend most refined oil exports, causing Brent crude to return to $102.Four sources familiar with the matter said that Chinese refineries have suspended exports of refined oil products to regions outside of Hong Kong and Macau, awaiting further notification from Beijing, with the core objective of prioritizing domestic supply. China's main exports include diesel, aviation kerosene, and gasoline; Domestic commercial gasoline inventories had previously fallen to their lowest level since 2011, diesel inventories to their lowest level since 2015, and refinery processing volume fell by about 7% this year. The news, coupled with troop surges in the Middle East and Russian diesel restrictions, pushed Brent crude oil settlement prices up 4.37% to $102.31 per barrel in December, and WTI crude oil up 2.71% to $92.87. China is not the world's largest exporter of refined oil products, but it is an important marginal supplier in Asia. Exiting would increase diesel cracking price spreads and regional refining profits, and exacerbate transportation, agriculture, and aviation costs. The duration of the policy depends on the speed of inventory recovery and refinery operations after the National Day holiday. It remains to be seen whether Beijing will issue new export quotas, state-owned refineries will cancel the scale of ship cargo, and whether Europe's release of diesel reserves can offset the supply gap in Asia. If restrictions continue into winter, Asian airlines and logistics companies may be forced to lock in fuel costs in advance, and terminal fares and freight rates will also face a new round of adjustments.Source: Reuters；Oil price impact 3. Broadcom plans to provide Anthropic with up to $42 billion in chip financing.Anthropic’s IPO filings disclosed that Broadcom has agreed to provide up to $42 billion in financing to support its AI infrastructure spending; The relevant convertible debt could cover approximately one-third of Anthropic’s five-year, $125.2 billion TPU computing power lease commitment. Broadcom is also involved in Google's TPU design, equipment leasing, and financing, and expects Anthropic to become its largest computing customer by 2027. Anthropic will have access to several gigawatts of next-generation TPU computing power starting in 2027, while Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue to reach approximately $115 billion in fiscal year 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal year 2028. This cycle of "suppliers providing financing and customers repurchasing chips" can accelerate data center construction, but it also closely links the balance sheets and demand forecasts of both parties. Anthropic warned that payment or performance defaults could cause large lease obligations to expire immediately, while restricting the use of the $42 billion credit line; Broadcom's pricing and hardware decisions may also affect its computing power acquisition. Going forward, we should observe the IPO terms, conversion price, computing power utilization, and regulatory agencies' scrutiny of conflicts of interest and concentration. If the model's revenue growth rate cannot cover long-term lease payments, the debt swap will dilute equity; If demand materializes, Broadcom can simultaneously earn revenue from chips, leasing, and financing.Source: Reuters 4. The United States extends sanctions to Iran's railway and automotive industries, extending the blockade pressure from sea to land.The U.S. Treasury Department announced sanctions against Iran's railway and automotive industries and their overseas suppliers, expanding the "economic exile operation" launched in August. The list includes Iran's Khodro and Sepa, which together account for more than 90% of Iran's domestic automobile market; The state-owned Islamic Republic of Iran Railway Company, Raja Passenger Transport Company, and major private freight companies were also included. The U.S. port blockade has restricted Iran's oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz and forced it to rely more on road and rail transport for petroleum products, fertilizers, and chemicals. The new sanctions are intended to cut off these alternative routes. Some suppliers in Indonesia, the UAE, and Türkiye were also affected. The measures may further reduce Iran's war financing and industrial logistics, but they will also increase the costs of transportation, employment, and living for ordinary residents, and weaken the political space for the seven-day confidence-building plan. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether third-country companies will stop supplying goods, how Iran will circumvent settlement and parts restrictions, and whether sanctions and Qatari mediation can be included in the same negotiation order. Automobiles and railways are highly linked to domestic employment, and the new restrictions may also force Iran to prioritize civilian supplies and increase the cost of government subsidies and exchange rate stabilization.Source: Reuters 5. Putin warns the West against escalating the Kaliningrad dispute; Russia extends diesel export ban.Russian President Vladimir Putin stated at the Valdai Forum that the world is in a dangerous moment, and if NATO attempts to isolate Kaliningrad, located between Poland and Lithuania, Russia will respond with all means, including nuclear weapons. He also denied any intention of attacking NATO and said he was willing to talk to the leaders of the United States and China. Russia had previously sent a diplomatic note to NATO hinting at nuclear retaliation against the blockade of Kaliningrad, while NATO emphasized its defensive nature and refused to accept nuclear blackmail. Putin also acknowledged that Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries cost Russia about 1% of its GDP and stated that diesel would not be supplied to the global market until sanctions were lifted. Russia has extended its ban on diesel exports to producers until the end of October, while U.S. diesel prices have risen above $6.50 per gallon. Military warnings and energy restrictions reinforce each other, directly transmitting European security risks to inflation. Next, we need to observe NATO's military deployment in the Baltic Sea, the attack and defense of Ukrainian and Russian refineries, and whether Russia is using diesel supply as a bargaining chip in sanctions negotiations.Nuclear deterrent source: Reuters；Diesel Policy Sources Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of today's pricing is that "policy suspension does not equate to an easing of financial conditions." Federal Reserve officials lowered expectations for an October rate hike, which may weaken short-term yields and the upward momentum of the dollar; However, the 10-year US Treasury yield once touched 5.34%, indicating that energy shocks, fiscal supply, and AI capital expenditures are still driving up actual financing costs. If non-farm payrolls are strong and oil prices remain above $100, long-term yields may continue to fluctuate at high levels, with overvalued technology stocks, real estate, and highly leveraged corporate bonds being the first to come under pressure. The Broadcom-Anthropic financing arrangement can support chip orders, but it has also made the market focus more on revolving financing, customer concentration, and computing power utilization, rather than valuing the technology sector solely based on revenue growth. In terms of commodities and exchange rates, China's suspension of refined oil exports, Russia's restrictions on diesel supply, and Iranian shipping disruptions have all pushed up the risk premium for refined products. Strong oil prices typically support the US dollar and depress the currencies of energy-importing countries, which is particularly detrimental to the euro, Japanese yen, and Indian rupee. Gold, on the other hand, was simultaneously pulled by safe-haven buying and high real interest rates. China's policy of prioritizing domestic inventory can reduce domestic energy shortages, but it may increase imported inflation and limit the room for global central banks to cut interest rates. Today, the focus should be on whether Brent can hold above $100, the diesel cracking spread, the divergence between the long and short ends of US Treasury bonds, the reactions of Asian currencies, and whether a new implementation order emerges between the escalation of US-Iran sanctions and Qatar's mediation. If oil prices continue to rise while the Federal Reserve remains on hold, the yield curve may steepen further; If fuel supply is released or negotiations achieve a breakthrough, long-term bonds and cyclical stocks will be the first to receive a buffer. China also needs to observe refinery startups, inventories, and export quotas after the holidays, as this will determine whether the restrictions are short-term inventory management or longer-term energy security policies.
Cover image:Alpha Perspective / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-03: Energy Shocks Reshaping Global Policy Paths | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme over the past 24 hours has been that energy supply shocks and cooling growth are simultaneously squeezing policy space. U.S. job creation plummeted to 29,000 in September, reducing the urgency for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again in October. However, Eurozone inflation jumped to 3.8% due to energy prices, and China suspended refined oil exports to regions outside Hong Kong and Macau in October, further intensifying the risk of global fuel shortages and secondary inflation. On the other hand, AI infrastructure investment is still attracting equity funds, but this is accompanied by net outflows from technology funds and high long-term bond yields, indicating that the market is shifting from "only looking at growth" to examining the return on capital expenditures. The Russian military's escalated attacks on Kyiv's transportation and energy-related facilities have continued to intertwine supply chains, security premiums, and fiscal pressures. The coexistence of growth, inflation, and geopolitical risks means that it is more difficult for central banks and investors to rely on a single data point for judgment.
Five key news items1. US employment plummets, expectations of a Fed rate hike in October subside.The U.S. Department of Labor announced on October 2 that non-farm payrolls increased by only 29,000 in September, significantly lower than the market expectation of 90,000. The unemployment rate rose from 4.1% to 4.2%, and the labor force participation rate fell to 61.8%. The total number of new jobs added in July and August was revised down by 60,000, with average hourly wages increasing by only 0.1% month-on-month and 3.0% year-on-year, indicating that companies' recruitment and wage pressures are cooling down in tandem. Meanwhile, layoffs remain low, and the labor market is closer to "low hiring, low layoffs" than a sudden recession.ReutersTraders are now further betting that the Federal Reserve will hold rates steady at its October 27-28 meeting. However, inflation remained at 3.4% in August, far above the 2% target, and whether to raise interest rates again in December still depends on the next CPI and wage data. For the market, the easing of short-term interest rate pressures is beneficial to growth stocks, but long-term government bonds are still constrained by inflation, fiscal supply and oil prices, and weakening employment cannot be simply equated with comprehensive easing. 2. Eurozone inflation rises to 3.8%, as energy shocks approach monetary policy.EurostatPreliminary readings released on October 2 showed that the Eurozone's harmonized consumer price index rose 3.8% year-on-year in September, up from 3.2% in August and reaching a nearly three-year high, with a monthly rate of 0.6%. Energy prices surged 18.8% year-on-year, accelerating further from 14.3% in August; Services inflation rose from 3.0% to 3.2%, while food, alcohol and tobacco inflation rose from 1.1% to 1.4%, while core inflation excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco was 2.5%. This structure suggests that the main driver remains energy, but service prices have not cooled sufficiently, and the European Central Bank cannot simply view the shock as temporary noise. Full data will be released on October 16, and the next preliminary value will be released on November 4. If oil and gas prices persist and companies pass on transportation and raw material costs to consumers, European interest rate expectations, the euro, and financing costs for highly indebted member states may all rise further. Conversely, with core and wage data stable, the central bank may still wait until the end of the year to take action. 3. AI narratives continue to attract investment, but divergence is emerging within the technology sector.The latest weekly data from LSEG Lipper shows that as of September 30, global equity funds saw net inflows of $34.76 billion for the second consecutive week, down from $44.31 billion the previous week, indicating that risk appetite has not been completely suppressed by high bond yields. U.S. funds absorbed $20.6 billion, while Europe and Asia saw inflows of $6.19 billion and $6.16 billion respectively. One of the supporting factors is the demand for AI infrastructure: Micron's revenue outlook is higher than expected, while Goldman Sachs estimates that major U.S. cloud service providers will spend about $800 billion on capital in 2026, with market consensus expecting it to rise to $1.1 trillion in 2027.ReutersIt was also pointed out that technology sector funds saw a net outflow of $2.63 billion that week, high-yield bonds saw an outflow of $2.29 billion, and money market funds redeemed $116.52 billion. In other words, funds are still willing to pay for AI growth, but are beginning to reprice chips, cloud services, cash flow, and valuation. The next step is to observe whether the backlog of orders can translate into bottlenecks in revenue, memory, and power supply, and whether the return on capital expenditures can catch up with financing costs. 4. China suspends refined oil exports in October, causing a sudden tightening of the Asian fuel market.China suspended exports of refined oil products to markets outside Hong Kong and Macau in October, directly reducing the supply of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel in Asia.ReutersAccording to reports, Singapore's gasoline imports from China this year have decreased by 62% compared to 2025, and local fuel inventories have fallen to a record low. The spread between Asian gasoline cracking prices once exceeded $50 per barrel, and the near-monthly premiums for diesel and jet fuel markets have also widened significantly. Jet coal to Hong Kong is unrestricted, while traditional buyers such as Singapore, Australia, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Japan need to find alternative sources. This move comes against the backdrop of Russia restricting diesel exports and Europe discussing the use of reserves. Therefore, the impact is not only on China's export volume, but also on the rearrangement of global refining and chemical product flows. For China, prioritizing domestic supply helps stabilize inventories during holidays and winter; For regional markets, this means rising costs in transportation, aviation, and manufacturing. Next, we need to look at export quotas in November, domestic refinery operating rates, whether Europe will release diesel reserves, and whether the high cracking price differential will stimulate other Asian refineries to increase production. 5. Russian military's continuous strikes on Kyiv bridges have once again highlighted winter air defense gaps.On October 2, Russia struck bridges across the Dnieper River, connecting the east and west banks of Kyiv, for the second consecutive day. The southern bridge remained closed after being attacked by drones, and the other two bridges were also fully or partially shut down. About one-third of Kyiv's population, or one million people, lives on the east bank, and about 500,000 people commute across the river every day. The attack on transportation nodes has rapidly amplified the pressure on the city's operation and supply security. On the same day, an attack on a residential building in Kyiv killed one person and injured two others, while a guided bomb attack in Kharkiv killed two people and injured 32. Russia stated that the targets involved military transport, power plants, ports, and ships.ReutersAccording to reports, the Ukrainian Foreign Minister stated that the minimum defense requirements for this winter include 300 Patriot interceptor missiles and is seeking millions of rounds of F-16 cannon ammunition. The escalation of the infrastructure war will increase European aid, energy security and reconstruction budgets, and may also continue to disrupt Russian oil supplies. The key issues going forward are the speed of allied deliveries, Russia's monthly production capacity of approximately 120 to 140 ballistic missiles, and the intensity of both sides' attacks and defenses against refineries, power grids, and transportation hubs. Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe most important asset pricing contradiction today is that "slowing growth" is not enough to offset "energy reinflation". Weak US employment has lowered the probability of an October rate hike, which is theoretically beneficial to bonds and high-duration technology stocks. However, oil prices, 3.8% inflation in Europe, and a shortage of refined oil products will support term premiums, preventing long-term yields from falling simultaneously. The US dollar may also remain strong thanks to interest rate spreads and safe-haven demand. The euro faces a dilemma: a more hawkish stance from the European Central Bank could provide interest rate support, but it would increase financing pressure on highly indebted economies such as France. In terms of commodities, a distinction should be made between crude oil and refined chemical products. Currently, the spread between the cracking prices of diesel, jet fuel, and gasoline reflects tight real supply better than the price of a single oil, while gold continues to be pulled by geopolitical risks and real interest rates. Risk appetite is still maintained by AI investment, but the coexistence of $34.76 billion in equity fund inflows and net outflows from technology funds suggests that a strong index does not mean that sectors rise indiscriminately. Highly valued companies need to demonstrate a return on nearly trillion-dollar capital expenditures using orders, utilization, and free cash flow. The immediate variable in Chinese policy is refined oil export arrangements: ensuring domestic supply helps reduce volatility in domestic fuels, but it could push up external costs through Asian trade chains, which in turn could affect export manufacturing, shipping, and exchange rate expectations. Today, we should focus on interest rate pricing before the US CPI, the trend of the US dollar and euro, the Asian spread, signals of European reserve release, and whether winter air defense aid to Ukraine can be implemented. These variables will collectively determine whether the market will trade for "cooling growth" or resume trading for "longer periods of high inflation and high interest rates." Cover image:Jakub Żerdzicki / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-04: Security anxiety reshapes the capital and policy agenda | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, the common theme of global policies and markets has shifted further from simple growth and inflation to how the "cost of security" is being repriced. Public questions have once again emerged within the AI industry regarding the imbalance between development speed and security governance; China is reducing weaknesses in its financial system through large-scale consolidation of rural and regional banks; Germany has extended its aid to Ukraine to include joint drone production and energy infrastructure repair; North Korea continues to test medium-range strategic missiles. Meanwhile, Australia and Japan launched their annual finance ministers' dialogue, discussing investment, strategic financing, energy prices, and high bond yields within the same framework. Technological security, financial security, energy security, and military security are simultaneously entering fiscal, capital expenditure, and asset valuation models. Investors are no longer just concerned with "when interest rates will change," but how much long-term cost economies are willing to pay to reduce vulnerability.
Five key news items1. Australia and Japan launch annual finance ministers' dialogue, with strategic financing becoming a core element of bilateral economic cooperation.Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers departed for Japan on October 4 to hold the first Australia-Japan Finance Ministers' Dialogue with Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama. The two sides plan to establish this mechanism as an annual forum, focusing on investment opportunities, strategic financing, and international economic cooperation. Japan will be Australia's fourth-largest source of foreign investment in 2024, with an investment stock of approximately AU$282.9 billion. Chalmers will also meet with more than 30 business executives during his trip, hoping to expand Japanese capital investment in Australia.ReutersThe report points out that the two countries are currently facing similar constraints: rising energy prices are pushing up inflation, while rising long-term bond yields are increasing fiscal budget pressure. For the market, this means that Australia-Japan cooperation is deepening from traditional trade relations to key minerals, energy, infrastructure and long-term capital allocation. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether the two parties can reach a specific investment agreement, and whether high financing costs will change the project's return threshold; If strategic capital continues to flow into resource and energy security, it may also increase the Australian dollar's sensitivity to commodity cycles and Asian capital flows. 2. OpenAI security personnel resign, reigniting controversy over cutting-edge model governance.Former OpenAI security officer David Robinson publicly resigned on October 3, criticizing the company for not giving enough weight to security research when rapidly advancing stronger models, and stating that "the era of trial and error is over" for advanced AI. Robinson said he worked at OpenAI for about three and a half years, participated in drafting the Preparedness Framework, and oversaw 12 security reports released by cutting-edge models. He particularly questioned the approach of relying on "iterative deployment," which involves launching a system first and then gradually strengthening protection based on actual problems.ReutersOpenAI was quoted as saying that the company will ensure that the model's capabilities do not exceed the scope that can be safely managed and protected, and will suspend training or postpone the model if necessary. The event itself will not immediately change the demand for AI, but it has reinforced the capital market's focus on governance costs: the stronger the capabilities, the more likely testing, red teams, cybersecurity, insurance, and compliance expenses are to become fixed costs. The key questions going forward are whether OpenAI and its peers will adjust their security thresholds, whether regulators will translate internal security processes into clearer external requirements, and whether governance investment will affect model iteration speed and profit margin expectations. 3. China has closed more than 670 banks in four years, and the risk disposal of small banks has entered a phase of accelerated consolidation.China's financial system is accelerating the handling of risks of small and medium-sized banks through mergers and exits.Financial TimesAccording to a report on October 4, China has closed more than 670 banks in the four years ending 2025, bringing the total number of banking institutions down by about 23% to 3,139. The main entities exiting the market are rural and regional banks. China's banking system has assets of approximately US$64 trillion, with small rural and regional banks accounting for more than a quarter of its total assets. Against the backdrop of a prolonged real estate correction, low interest rates, weak credit demand, and narrowing net interest margins, these institutions are more likely to expose asset quality, capital, and corporate governance issues. The purpose of regulation in promoting mergers and acquisitions is to shift risk diversification to entities with stronger capital and governance capabilities, and to reduce the probability of local institutional instability being transmitted to deposit confidence. For the economy, short-term consolidation may tighten traditional financing channels for some county-level and micro and small enterprises, but in the medium term it will help improve the resilience of the financial system. Going forward, we should observe the pressure of local government capital injection, the speed of non-performing asset recognition, the availability of rural credit, and whether large banks can more effectively meet local financing needs after replenishing their capital. 4. German Chancellor visits Kyiv to finalize drone cooperation and provide additional energy and military aid.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv on October 4 to advance new German-Ukrainian defense cooperation amid increased Russian airstrikes.ReutersThe report states that Germany will provide €1 billion in military aid and allocate €350 million to repair Ukraine's energy infrastructure. During his trip, Merz also led the German Economy Minister and executives from companies such as Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, and Quantum Systems to finalize cooperation on the rapid production of anti-jet drones. Germany's Quantum Systems and Ukraine's WIY Drones had previously established a joint venture to produce Strila interceptor Drones, and the two sides also discussed jointly developing long-range weapons capable of striking targets within Russia. This move indicates that the European aid model for Ukraine is shifting from inventory transfer to joint production, industrial capacity building, and energy resilience, meaning that defense spending is more likely to become a multi-year fiscal project. The market should next focus on Germany's budget arrangements, orders from European defense companies, the speed of Ukraine's winter power grid repair, and whether Russia will further expand its attacks on energy and industrial facilities. 5. North Korea tests medium-range strategic missiles, pressures on regional air defense and military spending continue to rise.On October 4, North Korea confirmed through official media that it had completed medium-range strategic missile drills under the supervision of Kim Jong-un, stating that the tests were used to train troops to operate hypersonic strategic weapons systems and to test their war deterrent capabilities.ReutersAccording to reports, the South Korean military determined that the missile was launched from eastern North Korea and flew more than 700 kilometers. North Korea claimed that the weapon hit a maritime target about 1,000 kilometers away. Kim Yo-jong then emphasized that the missiles adopt more complex flight trajectories and criticized the tracking capabilities of South Korea and Japan. This test launch occurred amid renewed tensions between North and South Korea over the demilitarized zone landmine incident and was part of more than a dozen missile activities by North Korea since 2026. The economic impact is mainly reflected in risk premiums and fiscal channels: South Korea and Japan need to continue to invest in missile early warning, interception and US military coordination systems, and the Northeast Asian supply chain will also maintain higher insurance costs for sudden upgrades. Going forward, attention should be paid to the joint assessment of test launch data by Japan and South Korea, the arrangements for US-Japan-South Korea military exercises, and whether North Korea will continue to test variable-orbit or longer-range systems. Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's five news items collectively point to a pricing shift: security is no longer just a geopolitical add-on, but is becoming a long-term capital expenditure for businesses and governments. In terms of interest rates, energy costs remain high, and the government has to bear the burden of defense, infrastructure, and financial stability expenditures, which means that even if some economic data weaken, long-term bond yields may not decline rapidly. The term premium may continue to limit the expansion of overvalued assets. In terms of exchange rates, the US dollar remains supported by safe-haven assets and higher yields, while the Australian dollar, Japanese yen, and euro are more sensitive to energy import costs, strategic investment flows, and fiscal burdens. Commodity markets need to monitor crude oil, natural gas, and key minerals simultaneously: if Australia-Japan strategic financing further targets energy and resource projects, it may strengthen policy premiums for key minerals. The escalation of the Russia-Ukraine infrastructure war continues to add tail costs to Europe's energy risks. The contradictions in technology valuations are also becoming clearer. AI demand and infrastructure investment can continue to grow, but security assessments, computing power protection, regulatory and liability costs will enter the profit model, and the market may emphasize cash flow more than simply model capability leadership. In China, the accelerated consolidation of small and medium-sized banks does not conflict with previous policies to stabilize growth: the former aims to reduce tail financial risks and create a more stable transmission environment for monetary and fiscal support. However, if local banks handle risks too quickly, they also need to be wary of a further contraction in credit related to county-level, micro and small enterprises, and real estate. Today's focus should be on long-term bond yields, the US dollar versus the Japanese yen, European energy prices, the valuations of defense technology stocks and leading AI companies, and changes in credit issuance following the merger of China's small and medium-sized banks. These variables will determine whether the market views "safe investing" as a new source of growth or more persistent fiscal and cost pressures. Cover image:Quentin Guiot / Pexels

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-05: Interest Rate Cut Expectations Resurge, Security Costs Continue to Rise | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, a set of seemingly contradictory but actually interconnected signals have emerged in global markets: cooling US employment has prompted investors to quickly reduce their bets on the Federal Reserve continuing to raise interest rates, causing the dollar and US Treasury yields to fall and giving risky assets a breather. However, energy transportation, European security, AI governance, and the consolidation of small and medium-sized banks in China are all reminding the market that the "security cost" affecting long-term valuations is still rising. The attack on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the infrastructure conflict between Russia and Ukraine make it difficult for energy and defense premiums to disappear quickly. The AI industry has moved from a model competition to a discussion on the boundaries between public regulation and responsibility. China continues to address weaknesses in its financial system by reducing the number of high-risk small banks. A favorable short-term liquidity environment, coupled with rising medium- to long-term structural risks, constitutes the most noteworthy asset pricing portfolio today.
Five key news items1. Cooling US employment reshapes interest rate bets, sharply reducing the probability of an October rate hike.During Monday's Asian trading session, global stock markets strengthened, the dollar weakened, and US Treasury bonds stopped falling. The core catalyst came from the US employment data released last week: new jobs in September were weaker than expected, and the data for the previous two months were significantly revised downward, causing the market to reassess its previously aggressive interest rate hike path. According to CME FedWatch data, the probability that traders expect the Federal Reserve to continue raising interest rates in October has dropped from about 64% a week ago to 22%. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield fell to approximately 5.26%, and the 2-year yield to approximately 4.81%. The euro rebounded from a 17-month low to around $1.124. Japan's Nikkei index rose about 2% in early trading, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures also rose.ReutersIt is pointed out that government financing pressures, increased bond supply, and high energy prices have kept long-term bond yields in major economies at multi-year highs, so this does not mean that the global tightening cycle has ended. The key issues ahead are US inflation, wages, and statements from Federal Reserve officials: if employment continues to cool while inflation eases simultaneously, the dollar and long-term yields may come under further pressure. If energy pushes up inflation again, the current easy trading of risky assets could still quickly reverse. 2. AI security controversy enters New York legislative hearings, industry self-regulation faces stronger external scrutiny.Pressure on AI governance continues to shift from internal debates within companies to local legislation. Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon will testify at a hearing on artificial intelligence at the invitation of New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin; New York City councilors are discussing a package of bills aimed at establishing AI security guarantees. When Coxon left Anthropic last month, he publicly warned that cutting-edge AI could pose serious social risks and criticized labs including Anthropic and OpenAI for taking too high risks on security issues.ReutersThe report states that information about the hearing schedule was initially reported by Bloomberg, and Reuters has not yet independently verified all the details. The significance of the incident lies not only in the individual accusations, but also in the fact that AI regulation in the United States is forming a multi-tiered, parallel landscape at the federal, state, and city levels: as model capabilities, agent autonomy, and infrastructure access continue to expand, it is becoming increasingly difficult for companies to meet public accountability relying solely on internal security frameworks. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether the hearings will result in a specific legal text, third-party audit and incident disclosure obligations, and whether local rules will further increase the compliance costs of AI companies and affect the pace of model release. 3. China is accelerating the consolidation of small and medium-sized banks, shifting the financial system from "expanding the number of banks" to "reducing risks."The structural consolidation of China's banking industry is accelerating significantly. The Financial Times reported on October 5 that China has been continuously closing and merging banking institutions over the past four years, with the number of banks decreasing by about 23% to 3,139 by 2025. Last year alone, more than 670 banks exited, the vast majority of which were small rural and local institutions. Although small banks serve county-level areas and small and medium-sized enterprises, they have long faced problems such as weak asset quality, insufficient capital buffers, and limited governance capabilities. In an environment of real estate adjustments, weak credit demand, and narrowing net interest margins, these risks are more likely to be concentrated and exposed.Financial TimesCitation analysis indicates that one of the immediate goals of consolidation is to reduce the likelihood of liquidity events occurring in small institutions. At the same time, China has recently replenished capital with some large banks and insurance institutions, indicating that its policy approach is not simply to compress financial supply, but to concentrate capital and risk-taking capacity on stronger institutions. For the economy, short-term consolidation may weaken credit competition in some regions, but improved governance and non-performing asset disposal will reduce tail risks in local finances. Going forward, it is necessary to observe the asset quality after the merger, the level of local government support, and whether new financing gaps have emerged for rural and micro and small enterprises. 4. Middle Eastern crude oil exports have recovered to pre-war levels, but shipping risks in Hormuz have increased accordingly.A new situation has emerged in the Middle East's energy supply, characterized by "recovery in quantity but increased transportation risks". Kpler shipping data shows that Middle Eastern crude oil exports exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the last week of September, with daily exports once reaching 19.5 million to 22.5 million barrels. The 7-day moving average ending October 1 was approximately 18.5 million barrels per day, higher than the average of approximately 18 million barrels per day before the US-Israel conflict with Iran. Combined exports of crude oil, refined oil products, chemicals and other non-gaseous liquids averaged 22.4 million barrels per day in the week ending September 30, and LNG exports through the Strait of Hormuz also rose to their highest monthly level since February in September.ReutersIt was also pointed out that since October 2, ship attacks have occurred almost daily in the relevant waters, with at least seven incidents reported. The rebound in supply has temporarily alleviated the physical shortage, but it cannot eliminate the risk of war, freight costs, and detour costs. Brent crude oil is still around $102 a barrel. The most important variable going forward is whether the attack will begin to systematically affect shipowners' willingness to pass through, insurance rates, and loading plans. Once logistics are disrupted, the secondary impact of oil prices on inflation and global interest rates will be amplified again. 5. Germany increases military aid and energy funding in Kyiv, further shifting the Russia-Ukraine competition towards industrial capabilities.During his visit to Kyiv, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an additional €1 billion in military aid to Ukraine and an investment of €350 million to repair the energy system. During the visit, German companies signed 14 agreements with the Ukrainian government and businesses, totaling approximately 6.6 billion euros, covering IRIS-T air defense missiles, radar equipment, and drone interception systems. Meanwhile, Russia has recently intensified its drone attacks on Ukraine's power, communications, and transportation infrastructure, bringing winter energy resilience back to the core of Europe's security agenda.ReutersThe report shows that Germany's more closely integration of aid with domestic corporate orders, joint production, and technological cooperation means that competition in the Russia-Ukraine war is shifting from simple inventory depletion to sustainable industrial capabilities such as air defense, drones, electronic equipment, and energy restoration. For European finances, this will continue to squeeze other budget space while supporting capital expenditures in the defense industry. Going forward, attention needs to be paid to the speed of agreement delivery, the intensity of Russia's winter strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities, and whether Europe can transform temporary military aid into a stable multi-year procurement and capacity expansion mechanism. Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe core of asset pricing today is the tug-of-war between "cyclical easing expectations" and "structural safety premium". Weaker U.S. employment has significantly reduced the probability of an October rate hike, directly suppressing expectations for the U.S. dollar and short-term interest rates, and providing discount rate support for overvalued technology stocks. However, the 10-year US Treasury yield is still above 5%, indicating that fiscal supply, energy inflation, and term premiums have not disappeared. In terms of foreign exchange, if the Federal Reserve turns to a pause while Europe and Japan remain tight, the dollar's short-term momentum will weaken, but the US growth advantage will still limit its downside potential. The commodity side is more complicated: Middle Eastern exports have recovered to or even exceeded pre-war levels, which should have lowered the risk premium of oil prices. However, the continuous ship attacks in Hormuz have re-factored the risk of logistics tails into prices. Brent crude oil maintaining above $100 will continue to constrain the decline in global inflation. The AI sector is supported by improved interest rate expectations on the one hand, and on the other hand, the New York hearings show that regulatory, auditing and security investments may become new fixed costs, and valuation divergence will place greater emphasis on cash flow and governance capabilities. In China, the continued consolidation of small and medium-sized banks helps reduce tail financial risks, but it also requires policies to strike a balance between mitigating risks and maintaining financing at the county level and for micro and small enterprises. Next, we should simultaneously monitor US inflation and Fed statements, the frequency of the Hormuz shipping accident, European military spending and energy restoration expenditures, and the reaction of credit and risk assets to news of financial consolidation after China's holidays. Cover image:carmen dominguez / Unsplash

entry.title: With just 8GB of video memory, you can deploy a 30 tk/s multimodal AI in your laptop | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. My Laptop is a very ordinary gaming Laptop: a Ryzen 7 8845H, 16GB of RAM, an RTX 4060 Laptop, and only 8GB of video memory. According to many people's impression, this configuration can only be used to "play around" with local large models. But now, when I double-click a startup file every day, the browser opens a chat page: I can view images, watch videos, switch the depth of my thinking, and call native tools. My text generation speed is approximately... 31 tokens/sThe entire process involves no internet connection and no API fees. The one running inside is Qwen3.5-9BThe reasoning framework is llama.cpp。 This article is divided into three parts: How I chose the framework and model; An installation tutorial for beginners, written for every command; And the pitfalls I've encountered and the corresponding solutions.
First, let's talk about the conclusion: What ultimately gets started?
Project My Configuration
Operating system Windows x64
CPU AMD Ryzen 7 8845H
graphics card NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop, 8GB Memory
memory 16GB
reasoning procedure llama.cpp b10909, Windows CUDA 12.4 Precompiled Packages
model Qwen3.5-9B, Q4_K_M quantization (ca. 5.75 GiB)
multimodal assembly Compatible BF16 mmproj (approx. 0.86 GiB)
context length 4096 tokens
Access method Browser opens http://127.0.0.1:8080, or OpenAI compatible interface
Actual measurement data (all records from my machine at the time, not lab benchmarks):
configuration generation speed Memory usage of the entire graphics card
Qwen3.5-9B, Plain Text, 8K Context Approximately 31.3 tokens/s 6429 MiB / 8188 MiB
Qwen3.5-9B, Loading Multimodal Components, 4K Context The webpage displays approximately 34.6 tokens/s during short replies. 7364 MiB / 8188 MiB
Control: Gemma 4 E4B, Multimodal, 8K Context Approximately 51–54 tokens/s 5209 MiB / 8188 MiB
Two points to clarify. First, the "30 tk/s" in the title comes from that test in plain text mode; In multimodal mode, the 34.6 generated only 5 word elements, which is too short and only means that "the speed is on the same order of magnitude" and cannot be considered a formal result. Second,nvidia-smi It shows the usage of the entire graphics card, including the desktop and browser, and is not equivalent to the model's exclusive memory. Why llama.cppThere are many tools for running large models locally, but the one I ended up using was... llama.cppWhat I valued were these points:
There is no need to compile or install a Python environment. The official release page directly provides a pre-compiled compressed package for Windows + CUDA, which can be extracted and used. I didn't install the CUDA Toolkit or compile any C++ code throughout the process. A program gets things done. llama-server.exe Once launched, it provides both a web chat interface and an OpenAI-compatible API, allowing other clients to connect directly. The GGUF quantization model was used. After quantizing the 9B model to Q4_K_M, it is less than 6 GiB, and 8GB is enough to store it. All the parameters are clearly displayed. The length of the context, the number of layers placed in the graphics card, and the precision of the cache are all command-line parameters, so you know which one to adjust when there is not enough graphics memory.
The price is that it doesn't "click" like some graphical tools, requiring you to type several commands. That's why I wrote this tutorial. Why was Qwen3.5-9B ultimately chosen?I didn't choose the right one from the beginning; I changed it three times in between:
The first one downloaded was Qwen3-8B. Halfway through the download I changed my mind and stopped the download; it never started running from beginning to end. The first one to actually run was Google's Gemma 4 E4B.(Official QAT Q4_0 quantified version). It's fast, with 51–54 tokens/s on my machine, only about 5.2GB of video memory, and it has multimodal and can even enable 8K contexts. Finally, it was replaced with Qwen3.5-9B. The speed dropped to around 31 tokens/s, and the video memory was tighter, but I wanted the one with stronger overall capabilities.
Before switching, I compared several models that could be considered with 8GB of video memory: Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma 4 E4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, and gpt-oss-20b. To be honest, only the speed of the Gemma 4 E4B in that comparison chart was tested by me. The speed of other models was estimated based on hardware, and the capability score was also a reference value obtained by combining various publicly available benchmarks. The test conditions are not uniform. It helped me make trade-offs, but it wasn't a rigorous ranking. What really made me decide was the data in the official Qwen model card. The image below is from Official Model Card for Qwen3.5-9BThis is a comparison of the scores of the Qwen3.5 small-sized model with other models: Benchmark comparison chart in the official Qwen model card: Scores of Qwen3.5 small-sized models compared to other models Image source: Qwen official model card. The model card also contains a complete score table; I've selected a few representative lines. First, let's look at pure language capabilities. The comparison object is a model with a much larger number of parameters:
test GPT-OSS-120B GPT-OSS-20B Qwen3-30B-A3B (Thinking) Qwen3.5-9B Qwen3.5-4B
MMLU-Pro (Knowledge) 80.8 74.8 80.9 82.5 79.1
C-Eval (Chinese knowledge) 76.2 71.4 87.4 88.2 85.1
GPQA Diamond（ Scientific reasoning) 80.1 71.5 73.4 81.7 76.2
IFEval (instruction followed) 88.9 88.2 88.9 91.5 89.8
LongBench v2 ( (Long text) 48.2 45.6 44.8 55.2 50.0
LiveCodeBench v6 ( programming) 82.7 74.6 66.0 65.6 55.8
Looking at visual understanding, the comparison objects are two lightweight cloud models and the visual model of the previous generation 30B:
test GPT-5-Nano Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B Qwen3.5-9B Qwen3.5-4B
MMMU (Multidisciplinary Illustration and Text) 75.8 73.4 76.0 78.4 77.6
MathVision (doing math by looking at pictures) 62.2 52.1 65.7 78.9 74.6
OCRBench (character recognition) 75.3 82.5 83.9 89.2 85.0
RealWorldQA (Real-world Q&A) 71.8 72.2 77.4 80.3 79.5
VideoMME (Video with subtitles) 71.7 74.6 79.9 84.5 83.5
There are three things to keep in mind when reading these numbers:
This is Qwen's official resultsIt tests a model with complete accuracy. I'm running the Q4_K_M quantitative version locally, and the context is only 4096, which will reduce actual performance. I didn't retest these benchmarks on my own machine. It is not a comprehensive lead. In programming tests (LiveCodeBench, OJBench), the 9B is significantly inferior to the GPT-OSS-120B, which is clearly visible in the table. For me, the key points are two other things: a 9B model can match or even surpass the previous generation 30B model in terms of knowledge, instruction compliance, and long text; Moreover, it natively supports viewing images and videos, eliminating the need to find a separate visual model.
To sum up my trade-offs in one sentence:The Gemma 4 E4B is faster and more memory-efficient, while the Qwen3.5-9B is more comprehensive. If you care more about speed, or if you only have 6GB of video memory, the former is a good choice; The following steps in this article also apply to replacing the model file. Before you start: What you need to prepare One Windows 64-bit Computer, with NVIDIA graphics card, around 8GB of video memoryAnd the graphics card driver has been installed. about 8GB of free hard disk space(Program approx. 0.6GB, model approx. 6.6GB). Networks with access to GitHub and Hugging Face. The model file is over 6GB, so be patient if your internet speed is slow.
All commands in this article are in PowerShell It runs inside. How to open: Press Win Keys, input powershellPress Enter. Simply copy the entire command and press Enter. Anti-quotation marks at the end of a command ` This indicates that "this line is not over yet," and pasting the entire paragraph together will prevent errors. All files will be placed in the "Documents" folder. llama.cpp In the directory, the command will automatically find your own "document" path, without having to manually change the username. Step 1: Confirm the hardwareFirst, check if the graphics card and memory meet the requirements: 1nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader
Normally it will output a line similar to NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, 8188 MiB, ... The content. Let's take another look at the CPU and memory: 1234567Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, NumberOfCores, NumberOfLogicalProcessorsGet-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select-Object @{Name='RAM_GiB';Expression={ [math]::Round($_.TotalPhysicalMemory / 1GB, 1) }}

Cannot be found message nvidia-smiThis indicates that no NVIDIA drivers are installed, or that this computer does not have an NVIDIA graphics card. Step 2: Download and extract llama.cppI use it regularly b10909 This version, not the "latest version". The reason is simple: I verified every step in the tutorial on this version, and the "latest version" may look different in a few months. Download requiredTwoCompressed files are indispensable: one is the llama.cpp program itself, and the other is the CUDA runtime it depends on. The following command will create the directory, download it, and extract it: 12345678910111213141516171819202122$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'$llamaRoot = Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyDocuments')) 'llama.cpp'$downloadDir = Join-Path $llamaRoot 'downloads'$modelDir = Join-Path $llamaRoot 'models'$binDir = Join-Path $llamaRoot 'bin'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $downloadDir, $modelDir, $binDir | Out-Nullcurl.exe -L --fail --retry 3 --progress-bar ` -o (Join-Path $downloadDir 'llama-b10909-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip') ` 'https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10909/llama-b10909-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip'if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'llama.cpp 下载失败' }curl.exe -L --fail --retry 3 --progress-bar ` -o (Join-Path $downloadDir 'cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip') ` 'https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b10909/cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip'if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'CUDA 运行库下载失败' }Expand-Archive -LiteralPath (Join-Path $downloadDir 'llama-b10909-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip') ` -DestinationPath $binDir -ForceExpand-Archive -LiteralPath (Join-Path $downloadDir 'cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip') ` -DestinationPath $binDir -Force
The two compressed files are approximately 254MB and 391MB, respectively. After extraction, confirm that the program can recognize the graphics card: 123Set-Location $binDir.\llama-cli.exe --list-devices.\llama-server.exe --version
The first item should list your NVIDIA graphics card, and the second item should output information containing... build 10909 The version number. Possible problems
Must write curl.exeDon't just write curl。 In old versions of Windows PowerShell,curl It's an alias for another command with completely different parameters, and it will directly throw an error. Only one compressed file was downloaded.The program will not be able to use the graphics card because the CUDA DLL is missing. Both packages need to be extracted to the same bin Catalogue. Variables are lost when PowerShell is turned off。 If you close the window midway through, you need to reopen it with the above definitions first. $llamaRoot、$downloadDir、$modelDir、$binDir Run those lines again. The "CUDA 12.4" here is just the running environment that comes with this precompiled package.No needYou install the CUDA Toolkit separately.
Step 3: Download the modelTwo files are required, both from Bartowski's Qwen3.5-9B GGUF Repository：
file effect size

123456789101112$qwenModel = Join-Path $modelDir 'Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf'$qwenMmproj = Join-Path $modelDir 'mmproj-Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-bf16.gguf'curl.exe -L --fail --retry 5 --continue-at - --progress-bar ` -o $qwenModel ` 'https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf?download=true'if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Qwen 主模型下载失败' }curl.exe -L --fail --retry 5 --continue-at - --progress-bar ` -o $qwenMmproj ` 'https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF/resolve/main/mmproj-Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-bf16.gguf?download=true'if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Qwen 多模态组件下载失败' }
In the order --continue-at - It's a break-point resumption: If the download breaks midway through, running the same command again will pick up the download from where it left off, without having to start over. Check whether the file is completeIt's not uncommon for a 6GB file to download errors, and a corrupted model file can cause all sorts of inexplicable loading failures. Therefore, be sure to verify it once after downloading: 12345678910111213$expectedHashes = @{ 'Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf' = 'd784ce9eda1a5a7b51e8f705a9e6310844bf4f173654d115823c775fdea56d43' 'mmproj-Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-bf16.gguf' = 'd89c4bc142d02ed64aeed5c0a358bdead9109f21f4ada03a6b2df17a1aa94d9e'}foreach ($modelName in $expectedHashes.Keys) { $modelPath = Join-Path $modelDir $modelName $actualHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $modelPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHashes[$modelName]) { throw "模型哈希不匹配：$modelName" } [pscustomobject]@{ File=$modelName; Verified=$true; SHA256=$actualHash }}
Both files display Verified = True No problem. These two hash values are the values I validated when I downloaded them. Possible problems
Prompt "Model hash mismatch"There are two possibilities. First, if the file is not downloaded completely or is corrupted, run the download command again to continue the transfer and verify it again. Secondly, the repository author later updated the file (in the download link). main (This points to the latest status of the repository). In this case, you can go to the repository page to verify the SHA-256 of the file. I don't want it after downloading half of it.Press directly Ctrl+C Interruption. The remaining half-file extension is... .ggufBut it doesn't work. Don't use it to load; delete it or change the name (I changed it to...). .partialTo avoid confusion later. Step 4: First StartupFirst, start it directly from the command line to confirm that everything is working properly, and then double-click the file to start it. 1234567Set-Location $binDir.\llama-server.exe -m $qwenModel --mmproj $qwenMmproj ` -ngl 99 -c 4096 -np 1 ` --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 ` --image-min-tokens 1024 ` --reasoning off ` --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
A lot of loading information will scroll through the window. Once it has quieted down and the server has started listening, open it with your browser: 1http://127.0.0.1:8080
You will see a chat page. Ask a random question, then try dragging a picture in to describe it. To stop the model, return to the PowerShell window and press Ctrl+C。 What do these parameters mean respectively:
parameter meaning
-m Path to the main model file
--mmproj The path of the multimodal component. You must use the one that matches the main model; you cannot mix it with other models.
-ngl 99 Put all the layers of the model into the graphics card as much as possible. It's not that the model has 99 layers.
-c 4096 The context length is the total amount that the model can "remember" in a single conversation. This is the runtime setting, not the upper limit of the model
-np 1 Only one request is processed at a time, saving resources.
--cache-type-k/v q8_0 Let the session cache use more memory-saving precision. It is different from the quantification of the model itself.
--image-min-tokens 1024 Minimum number of lexical elements used when processing images
--reasoning off Thinking is turned off by default. We'll explain later how to change it to allow switching on the webpage.
--host 127.0.0.1 Allows local access only, not to local area networks or the Internet
--port 8080 Ports used by web pages and interfaces
Possible problems
Insufficient memory, loading failure, or exceptional lagAfter loading the multimodal components with 8GB of graphics memory, there is less than 1GB left (my entire graphics card occupies 7364 MiB). First, close programs that occupy video memory, such as games, other AI software, and browsers with many tabs open. If that doesn't work, then... -c 4096 Smaller, or remove --mmproj $qwenMmproj This paragraph only contains text. I only want to talk about words; I want a longer context.Remove --mmproj That part, put -c Change to 8192。 The 31.3 tokens/s I measured is this configuration, and the video memory usage is 6429 MiB. Text and multimodal use the same model; the only difference is whether or not visual components are loaded. The webpage cannot be openedThe model will take some time to load. It will refresh after the loading information in the window stops. You can also run it in another PowerShell window Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/health' Check if the service is ready. Prompt port is occupiedThis indicates that a program is already in use on the 8080, and it's very likely that the one you started earlier hasn't been closed yet. put --port 8080 Change to another number, for example 8089The website address was also changed accordingly. Do not open two copies at the same time.The two model services use different ports and are also competing for memory from the same graphics card; 8GB is simply not enough. "Multimodal" refers to pictures and videos。 In my configuration, the audio option in the interface is unavailable.
Step 5: Create a file that can be launched by double-clickingIt's too much trouble to type such a long command every time. Just create a startup file and double-click it later. The following PowerShell command will be... llama.cpp Generate under directory start-qwen.cmd。 It's a simplified version of the launcher I use every day, removing the "custom web pages" and "Agent" options. Those two options will be discussed in the advanced section later. 123456789101112131415161718192021222324252627282930313233343536373839$launcherPath = Join-Path $llamaRoot 'start-qwen.cmd'$launcherText = @'@echo offsetlocaltitle Qwen3.5 9B Multimodal - llama.cppset "ROOT=%~dp0"set "BIN=%ROOT%bin"set "MODEL=%ROOT%models\Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf"set "MMPROJ=%ROOT%models\mmproj-Qwen_Qwen3.5-9B-bf16.gguf"if not exist "%BIN%\llama-server.exe" goto missing_filesif not exist "%MODEL%" goto missing_filesif not exist "%MMPROJ%" goto missing_filescd /d "%BIN%"echo Starting Qwen3.5 9B multimodal chat with NVIDIA GPU acceleration...echo The chat page will open at http://127.0.0.1:8080echo Close this window or press Ctrl+C to stop the model.echo.start "" powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Start-Sleep -Seconds 6; Start-Process 'http://127.0.0.1:8080'""%BIN%\llama-server.exe" -m "%MODEL%" --mmproj "%MMPROJ%" -ngl 99 -c 4096 -np 1 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --image-min-tokens 1024 --reasoning off --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080echo.echo Qwen3.5 has stopped. Press any key to close this window.pause >nulexit /b:missing_filesecho ERROR: One or more llama.cpp or model files are missing.echo Installation folder: %ROOT%echo.pauseexit /b 1'@$launcherText = $launcherText -replace "`r?`n", "`r`n"[IO.File]::WriteAllText($launcherPath, $launcherText, [Text.Encoding]::ASCII)
Then double-click in the "Documents\llama.cpp" folder. start-qwen.cmdA black window will pop up to load the model, and the browser will automatically open after 6 seconds. Close that black window, and the model stops. This file does several things: first, it checks if the program and model files are there; if they are missing, it will stop and let you know. use cd /d Switch directories so that they can be used on other drive letters; The startup command is written as a whole line; Finally use pause Guarantee that the window does not flash when an error occurs. Possible problems: The window flashes and disappears after double-clicking, or "no response". This is the pit I've been in the longest. Nothing happens after double clicking on my first version of the startup file. Don't rely on guessing; first, catch the error message: 1cmd.exe /d /c "call `"$launcherPath`""
What I was seeing at the time was this output: 123'NVIDIA' is not recognized as an internal or external command'-NoProfile' is not recognized as an internal or external commandThe system cannot find the path specified.
In other words, CMD splits up fragments that originally belonged to the same command and executes them as independent commands. This has nothing to do with the model or graphics card driver; the problem lies with the text of the batch file itself: encoding, line breaks, and usage. ^ How to write "continue". I didn't conduct control experiments on each item, so I can't say for sure which character caused it, but the following approach has not caused any problems since:
Document content is in English (ASCII) only. The Chinese instructions are written in another document. The filename can be in Chinese, but do not write Chinese characters in the file. Line breaks use Windows' CRLF. The start command is written as a whole line, no need ^ Line break. reserve pauseThis way, you can see the error message when an error occurs.
The last two lines of the command above that generates the startup file correspond to steps 1 and 2. If you edited it manually using Notepad, you can check and correct it using the following command: 123456$launcherText = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($launcherPath)if ($launcherText -match '[^\x00-\x7F]') { throw '启动器里还有非英文字符，请先删掉'}$launcherText = $launcherText -replace "`r?`n", "`r`n"[IO.File]::WriteAllText($launcherPath, $launcherText, [Text.Encoding]::ASCII)
There's another small detail: the browser automatically opens using a fixed 6-second delay, and it doesn't actually detect that the model has completed loading. If the page opens before the model is ready, just wait a few seconds to refresh. At this point, a local AI that can read images is ready for daily use. The following content is optional. Step 6: See how fast it really isIf you want to know the actual speed on your machine, you can have the server report the count automatically. While the model is running, open another PowerShell window: 123456789101112131415161718192021$body = @{ model = 'qwen3.5-9b' messages = @(@{ role='user'; content='请用中文列出五条提高专注力的建议，每条一句话，直接回答。' }) temperature = 0.7 top_p = 0.8 max_tokens = 256 stream = $false chat_template_kwargs = @{ enable_thinking=$false }} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8$resp = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions' ` -Method Post -ContentType 'application/json; charset=utf-8' ` -Body ([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($body)) -TimeoutSec 120[pscustomobject]@{ Reply = $resp.choices[0].message.content CompletionTokens = $resp.usage.completion_tokens SpeedTokensPerSec = [math]::Round($resp.timings.predicted_per_second, 1)} | Format-Listnvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader
SpeedTokensPerSec It refers to the generation speed. Precautions when reading
Test answers that are too short do not count. The speed fluctuates greatly when generating only a few words; it should generate at least one or two hundred words. Don't mistake "prompt word processing speed" for generation speed. Web pages sometimes display numbers of thousands of words per second; that's the speed at which the model reads your question, not the speed at which it writes the answer. Speed is affected by many factors.Whether the laptop is plugged in, power mode, temperature, context length, and whether thinking is enabled. It's normal for the two tests to be different.
Advancement 1: Enabling web pages to switch between "thinking modes"Qwen3.5 supports "thinking": reason a paragraph before answering, which is suitable for questions such as math and coding, but it will seem slow in everyday chat. The previous startup command was used --reasoning off It's turned off by default. Ideally, you can switch between them at any time within the webpage. The problem is, the webpage in version b10909 is...When only one model is loaded on the desktopThe Reasoning submenu is omitted from the "+" menu. You need to distinguish between three things: whether the model supports switching thinking, whether the server is on or off by default, and whether the webpage gives you the toggle. The first two items are fine; the only thing missing is the menu on the webpage. This conclusion only applies to b10909 and does not mean that subsequent versions will have the same problem; The repair method referenced upstream... PR #27985。 First, confirm that the interface itself can indeed close thinking on request (executed in another window while the model is running): 12345678910111213141516171819$chatBody = @{ model = 'Qwen_Qwen3.5' messages = @(@{ role='user'; content='Reply with OK only.' }) stream = $false max_tokens = 16 reasoning_format = 'auto' chat_template_kwargs = @{ enable_thinking=$false }} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8$chatReply = Invoke-RestMethod ` -Method Post -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions' ` -ContentType 'application/json; charset=utf-8' ` -Body ([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($chatBody)) -TimeoutSec 60[pscustomobject]@{ Content = $chatReply.choices[0].message.content Reasoning = $chatReply.choices[0].message.reasoning_content Finish = $chatReply.choices[0].finish_reason}
What I get here is Content = OK，Reasoning It is empty. This means that as long as the webpage sends the selection to the server, that's fine. Next, you need to build your own webpage. This step requires installation first. Git and Node.js(I'm using Node v22.15.0, npm 10.9.2). Build only the web front-end, no C++ compilation required. 1. Download the corresponding version of source code 123$sourceRoot = Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyDocuments')) 'llama-source-b10909'if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sourceRoot) { throw '源码目录已存在，请换一个目录' }git clone --depth 1 --branch b10909 https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git $sourceRoot
2. Change a file Open with any text editor: 1tools/ui/src/lib/components/app/chat/ChatForm/ChatFormActions/ChatFormActionAdd/ChatFormActionAddDropdown.svelte
Change the import statement to introduce the thinking submenu component at the same time: 123456- import { ChatFormActionAddToolsSubmenu, McpLogo } from '$lib/components/app';+ import {+ ChatFormActionAddReasoningSubmenu,+ ChatFormActionAddToolsSubmenu,+ McpLogo+ } from '$lib/components/app';
Then render it in the additional menu on the desktop, adding a separator line: 12<ChatFormActionAddReasoningSubmenu /><DropdownMenu.Separator />
This component is already in the source code, but this menu doesn't use it. So this is just taking back existing things, not inventing a new mechanism. 3. Install dependencies, check, and build. 1234Set-Location (Join-Path $sourceRoot 'tools\ui')npm cinpm run checknpm run build
npm run check The result should be 0 errors and 0 warnings. You may get a "File size exceeds warning threshold" message during build; that's just a warning, not an error. 4. Place the build results in the installation directory. 12345$uiDist = Join-Path $sourceRoot 'tools\ui\dist'$webuiDir = Join-Path $llamaRoot 'webui'New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $webuiDir | Out-NullGet-ChildItem -LiteralPath $uiDist -Force | Copy-Item -Destination $webuiDir -Recurse -Force
5. Modify the startup command Put the startup command --reasoning off Replace with: 1--reasoning auto --path "%WEBUI%"
And add a line to the variable section before the startup file. set "WEBUI=%ROOT%webui"。 If you start it directly in PowerShell, write it as --reasoning auto --path (Join-Path $llamaRoot 'webui')。 After restarting, click the "+" in the lower left corner of the input box to see the Reasoning menu, where you can switch between off, low, medium, high, and maximum. Possible problems
--path You must add it. If you don't add it, the program will still open the same built-in webpage without a menu, and you might think that the changes haven't taken effect. The webpage remains unchanged after modifications.This webpage will be cached by your browser. Press Ctrl+F5 Force refresh; If the page prompts "Available updates", click "Refresh". Used when copying files Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $uiDist '*') Nothing was copied.：-LiteralPath It means "take the path literally" and will not expand. *。 You need to use it as above first. Get-ChildItem List them out before copying them. The higher the level of thinking, the better. The thinking budgets for low, medium, and high are 512, 2048, and 8192 vocabulary elements, respectively. But my total context is only 4096, and the "high" 8192 can't fit at all. Select "Off" for regular chat, and "Medium" for math, coding, or complex reasoning.
Advanced 2: Open the Agent toolThis version of llama.cpp allows the model to call native tools. The approach isThe original complete startup commandPlus --agentIt's not about starting another one that only brings... --agent The process: 12- --reasoning auto --path "%WEBUI%" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080+ --reasoning auto --agent --path "%WEBUI%" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
The parameters may differ between different versions. First, check if it's included in the help for your version: 12& (Join-Path $binDir 'llama-server.exe') --help 2>&1 | Select-String -Pattern '^--agent|\s--agent|--tools' -Context 0,3
After starting, you can check if the tool is ready: 1234567$serverProps = Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/props'$serverTools = Invoke-RestMethod 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/tools'[pscustomobject]@{ Vision = $serverProps.modalities.vision ToolCount = @($serverTools).Count Tools = (@($serverTools) | ForEach-Object { $_.name }) -join ', '}
My server has seven tools: reading files, searching files, searching file contents, executing commands, writing files, editing files, and viewing runtime information. Two more browser-side tools will appear on the webpage, so the total number displayed on the interface is 9, which is not contradictory to the 7 returned by the interface. Security issues must be addressed here. Once the Agent is enabled, the model can read and write files on your computer and execute commands; it is no longer just a chat window. So:
keep --host 127.0.0.1，don'tChange to 0.0.0.0Do not expose it to local area networks or public networks. Monitoring only the local machine does not mean absolute security. When the model is asked to process a web page or document of unknown origin, it may contain text that tricks it into performing an action. Don't add tools when you don't need them. --agent。
I only verified that the tool loaded properly and the menu displayed; I did not make the model execute write files or dangerous commands for testing purposes. Step 3: Change the webpage interface to ChineseThe b10909's web interface is in English, and much of the text is hard-coded into the source code, with no readily available "language" option to switch between. My approach is to translate at the source code level and then rebuild it, using the same process as fixing the thinking menu above. Specifically, I wrote a script that uses the Svelte compiler and TypeScript syntax analysis to read the source code, replaces the text on the interface with a Chinese-English bilingual dictionary, and then manually adds dynamic text that the script cannot handle (such as spelled-out sentences like "maximum 2,048 vocabulary"). The translation scope includes chat pages, sidebars, settings pages, think menus, tools menus, build progress, and statistics. There are hundreds of entries in the dictionary, but I won't post them here. I'll just share a few useful tips for those who want to do it themselves:
Translate only the interface text; do not modify the strings used within the program. Like thinking hierarchy off、mediumThe tool's function names and interface parameter names are agreed upon between programs, and translation will cause errors. I mistakenly translated an internal prefix string halfway through, and only discovered it during checking and changed it back. You can't just rely on "search for English and then replace". Even if you use grammatical analysis, you still have to look at the semantics one by one. Back up before translating. I keep a repaired English version of the thinking menu, which I can switch back to at any time. After the revisions are completed, inspections and tests are required. All 674 unit tests included in the project passed after translation; After that, I added a few more words and redid the checking, building, and browser verification. The model's answers, your input, and the results returned by the tool will not be translated; only the interface will be translated into Chinese.
The final result is that chat, settings, thinking patterns, tool menus, and generation progress are all in Chinese, while the model and startup parameters remain completely unchanged. Access to other softwarellama-server It provides an OpenAI-compatible interface, so many clients that support custom interface addresses can connect directly:

At the endLooking back, this didn't require particularly powerful hardware or knowledge of deep learning. There are three areas where time is really spent: trading off between "fast" and "comprehensive" when choosing a model, getting stuck on the encoding problem of a batch file, and figuring out whether the "think switch is missing" is a problem with the model, the server, or the webpage. Explain these three points clearly, and the rest is just to type the commands in order. A few reminders:
The speed and memory figures in this article are records of my machine at the time; they will be different with different computers and power modes. The model's benchmark score comes from Qwen official website and measures a model with complete accuracy; I'm running the quantified version locally; there are no retests. Local models can also make serious mistakes, and you have to verify important information yourself.
