entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-10: High interest rates test AI investment and policy support | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common thread over the past 24 hours has been that high energy prices and high financing costs are beginning to force governments, businesses, and investors to reprioritize. Global stock markets are still supported by large-cap tech stocks, but the yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds remains above 5%, and fiscal risks in France continue to push up the risk premium in Europe. The massive capital requirements for AI infrastructure therefore face stricter scrutiny of returns. China's 550 billion yuan local government debt outstanding limit to supplement grassroots financial resources and ongoing projects indicates that stabilizing growth is shifting from policy statements to the implementation of funds. Meanwhile, SpaceX's purchase of low-frequency spectrum has impacted the valuation of traditional telecommunications companies, while the Russia-US diesel arrangement directly links inflation, sanctions, and electoral politics. The market remains willing to take risks, but its demands for cash flow, policy credibility, and supply security have increased significantly.
Five key news itemsI. Global stock markets rebounded, but high interest rates and oil prices continued to squeeze valuation space.On October 9, global stock markets rose ahead of the start of earnings season for major U.S. banks: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both closed up about 0.6%, the European STOXX 600 rose 1%, and Asia-Pacific stock indices also generally strengthened. However, the rise in risky assets has not eliminated the pressure on capital costs. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose 2.8 basis points to 5.261% on the day, after hitting a 24-year high earlier this week. The spread between French 10-year government bonds and German bonds is about 138 basis points, reflecting that investors are still demanding higher compensation for fiscal deficits, public debt, and political uncertainty. Brent crude oil closed at around $104 a barrel, gold rose about 1.5% to $4,193, and the euro fell for the fifth consecutive week. The rise in the stock market while bonds and gold remain priced at high risk indicates that funds prefer large technology companies with guaranteed profitability rather than a recovery in overall risk appetite. Next, we need to see whether US inflation data, the Federal Reserve meeting on October 27-28, and the third-quarter results of companies such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo can support the current valuation.Source: Reuters II. China utilizes 550 billion yuan of local government debt outstanding quota to accelerate the implementation of fiscal support.On October 9, China's Ministry of Finance allocated a 550 billion yuan local government debt balance limit, equivalent to approximately US$82 billion, to replenish local financial resources and expand effective investment. Of this, 300 billion yuan will be used to support the daily operation of grassroots governments in counties and districts, while the remaining 250 billion yuan will be focused on projects under construction and eligible infrastructure in major economic provinces. The Ministry of Finance released policy information on its official website on the same day; Reuters points out that this scale exceeds similar arrangements at the end of 2024 and 2025, against the backdrop of weak consumption and investment, a continued real estate adjustment, and pressure on economic growth to target 4.5% to 5% for the whole year. The direct effects of the policy are twofold: firstly, to alleviate cash flow constraints on grassroots finance and reduce the risk of overdue payments and project shutdowns; Second, we will enable existing projects to generate physical work more quickly and avoid excessively long approval cycles for new projects. It is not a comprehensive stimulus, nor will it automatically solve the problems of insufficient resident demand or real estate companies' balance sheets. Therefore, the market should observe the speed of fund allocation, local government supporting financing, whether infrastructure construction has started and private investment has rebounded, and whether policies can improve rather than continue to squeeze the sustainability of local government debt.Source: Ministry of Finance｜Additional reporting: Reuters III. Firmus withdraws $5 billion IPO, AI infrastructure enters "return review" phaseFirmus, an Australian AI data center operator backed by Nvidia, Blackstone, and Coatue, withdrew its planned $5 billion IPO on October 9, instead seeking private equity funding and reserving the possibility of listing in other international markets in the future. This deal was originally set to become the second largest IPO in Australian history, with a proposed offering price corresponding to an equity valuation of approximately US$30.6 billion, nearly three times the company's August funding valuation of US$10.5 billion. Analysts estimate its debt at about $30 billion and its corporate value at about $60 billion. Investor concerns stem not only from high valuations, but also from limited construction records, a partner's withdrawal from a 1.6-gigawatt project, and more lenient lock-up arrangements for existing shareholders. The company currently has only two leased and operated data centers in Melbourne and Singapore, but plans to build five more in the Asia-Pacific region and expects to generate $5 billion in annual revenue within five years. The significance of this event lies in the fact that the capital market has not denied the demand for AI, but has begun to distinguish between chip orders, data center capacity, customer contracts, and realizable cash flow. The subsequent variables are whether private equity firms can replenish funds, whether debt costs will continue to rise, whether the capacity under construction can be launched on schedule, and whether the needs of clients such as OpenAI can be translated into long-term returns.Source: Reuters IV. SpaceX spends approximately $8 billion to acquire low-frequency spectrum, impacting the valuations of traditional telecommunications companies.SpaceX has agreed to acquire an 800 MHz low-frequency spectrum license covering approximately 14 MHz across the United States from Grain Management for a deal valued at approximately $8 billion. The goal is to enable Starlink Mobile to combine satellites with terrestrial networks to provide Mobile services that directly connect to terminals. Low-frequency spectrum has longer coverage distances and stronger building penetration capabilities, making it an important resource for traditional operators to build nationwide networks. Therefore, the news quickly triggered valuation repricing: T-Mobile US fell 13.2%, Verizon fell about 10%, Deutsche Telekom fell 7.9%, and the Eurotelecom index fell by more than 2.9%. Conversely, the three U.S. tower companies rose 6.5% to 13.3% as hybrid networks may still require rooftops, small base stations, and towers. The deal is still pending approval from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission, and SpaceX also needs ground deployment, roaming arrangements, and service quality verification. It will not completely replace cellular networks in the short term. But it pushes satellite communications from a supplementary service in remote areas to mainstream mobile competition, potentially changing spectrum auctions, operator capital expenditures, and cooperative bargaining. Going forward, attention should be paid to FCC review, Starlink terminal compatibility, city capacity performance, and whether traditional operators will respond with alliances, price reductions, or accelerated satellite cooperation.Source: Reuters V. The United States eases restrictions on the import of Russian diesel, creating tension between energy inflation and sanctions policies.On October 9, US President Trump said that Russia agreed to immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the US and global markets, with another 500,000 tons to be supplied in November, followed by an increase of 1 million tons. The U.S. Treasury Department also issued a general license allowing the import of Russian diesel until April 7, 2027. When the arrangement was announced, the average price of diesel in the United States had risen to $6.28 per gallon on October 8, an increase of about 70% since the US-Israel war against Iran began on February 28, putting direct pressure on agriculture, transportation, heating and commodity prices. Following the announcement, U.S. diesel futures fell by more than 4.8% to $4.64 per gallon. The first batch of 300,000 tons is equivalent to approximately 2.25 million barrels, while the United States itself exports about 1.5 million barrels per day. Therefore, analysts believe that its effect on continuously lowering prices is limited. More importantly, it has created policy tension with the energy sanctions imposed by the United States due to the Russia-Ukraine war, which has also drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Zelensky. The incident shows that pre-election cost-of-living pressures are changing the boundaries of energy diplomacy. Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the actual supply capacity of the Russian refinery after the attack, settlement and transportation arrangements, whether the United States will further waive sanctions, and whether the new supply can reduce the price spread of refined oil cracking products rather than just causing temporary fluctuations.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationToday's asset pricing presents a combination of "strong stocks, stressed bonds, high gold prices, and high oil prices". On the interest rate side, the US 10-year yield is around 5.26%, which means that all forward cash flows must be measured using a higher discount rate. Firmus's withdrawal of its IPO is a real case of AI valuation shifting from narrative to financing capabilities. If U.S. inflation exceeds expectations next week, tech stocks may still face valuation compression even with earnings growth. On the exchange rate side, the euro weakened for the fifth consecutive week. The divergence between French fiscal risks and the resilience of US growth remains positive for the dollar, but the rise in gold prices indicates that investors are also hedging against policy and geopolitical risks. On the commodity side, Brent crude oil prices are still above $100, and Russian diesel can only alleviate local shortages of refined oil products, but it is difficult to eliminate the supply risks of Middle Eastern shipping and refineries. In terms of risk appetite, the index's rise mainly relied on large-cap technology stocks, while telecommunications stocks fell sharply due to SpaceX spectrum trading, indicating that funds were not indiscriminately chasing the rise. In China, the 550 billion yuan local government bond quota will help support infrastructure and grassroots finance. If faster spending occurs in the future, it will improve industrial demand and RMB expectations. However, its sustainable effects still depend on household consumption, real estate recovery, and private investment. Today, we will focus on observing US inflation expectations, whether long-term bond yields will hit new highs, the credit quality in bank financial reports, and the actual pace of China's fiscal release.
Cover image:Gatsby Yang / Pexels

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-11: Employment Support and AI Capital Reassessment Go Hand in Hand | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe news of the past 24 hours collectively points to a resource reallocation driven by high costs and security risks. AI remains central to corporate competition and capital expenditure. Nvidia's plans to further invest in or acquire Reflection AI indicate that the chip giant is extending into the model and software layers. However, the sharp drop in AI-related debt issuance also indicates that investors are beginning to rigorously question cash flow and returns in a high-interest-rate environment. After achieving 87.7% of its annual urban employment target in the first three quarters, China is preparing to expand job supply through service sector policies, making stable growth more directly reflected in employment and residents' expectations. Meanwhile, Russian airstrikes caused new heavy civilian casualties, and Saudi Arabia continued to host an energy and investment conference despite the airport attack. Policy support, technological expansion, and geopolitical conflicts are vying for the same batch of capital. The market is no longer just looking at growth rate, but also at financing resilience, supply security, and policy credibility.
Five key news itemsI. AI debt issuance has cooled significantly, and capital has begun to review the returns on infrastructure investment.According to a Financial Times report on October 10, AI-related debt issuance fell to approximately $23 billion in September, less than half that of August and far below the peak of approximately $113 billion in June. There were no new AI bonds issued in the US investment-grade market that month. Since 2026, tech companies have still raised approximately $466 billion in AI-related debt, far exceeding the $101 billion in 2025. However, the rapid decline from its peak indicates that investors are beginning to worry about leverage, high interest rates, and the speed at which data center returns will be realized. Previously, from January to August, U.S. investment-grade issuers had completed approximately $306 billion in financing, while potential deals such as Broadcom's approximately $60 billion financing with Anthropic and SpaceX's approximately $40 billion chip financing are still awaiting market scrutiny. The change does not mean the end of the AI investment cycle, but rather that financing conditions have shifted from "scale first" to prioritizing customer contracts, power supply security, data center utilization rate, and free cash flow. Going forward, we should observe U.S. long-term bond yields, credit spreads, whether new projects are being scaled back, and whether large technology companies can cover capital costs with cloud revenue and model services.Source: Financial Times II. China added 10.52 million urban jobs in the first three quarters, with plans to further expand employment through the service sector.China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security announced on October 10 that 10.52 million new urban jobs were created nationwide from January to September, achieving 87.7% of the annual target. The urban surveyed unemployment rate averaged 5.2% from January to August, and employment remained generally stable. The next step in the policy will be to work with relevant departments to formulate documents to promote employment through the development of the service industry, strengthen the role of the service industry as the main channel for absorbing jobs, stabilize employment in labor-intensive industries, and explore new jobs in emerging and future industries. As of the end of September, the number of people enrolled in basic old-age, unemployment and work-related injury insurance reached 1.079 billion, 251 million and 327 million respectively, with a cumulative surplus of 11.2 trillion yuan in the three social insurance funds. Data shows that the overall target is progressing rapidly, but the special policies for the service industry also reflect that structural pressures still exist: there is a mismatch between college graduates, workers in traditional industries, and new technology positions. Whether policies can improve income expectations and consumption depends on the wages, stability, and social security coverage of newly created jobs, not just the quantity. Going forward, we will focus on fiscal and tax support in service sector documents, platform employment rights, vocational training, and youth unemployment indicators.Source: Human Resources and Social Security System Release｜Additional reporting: Reuters III. Nvidia is in talks to acquire Reflection AI, extending competition from chips to open models.Reuters, citing a Financial Times report on October 10, reported that Nvidia is discussing further investment in Reflection AI or a direct acquisition of the open-weight model startup. Negotiations are still in the early stages and could involve a full acquisition or a "talent acquisition" involving hiring a team and licensing the technology. The deal could be done within weeks, or it could fall through. Nvidia had previously invested $800 million in Reflection. Founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers, the company focuses on automation software development and this week launched its first open weighted model, Beam, in an attempt to compete with low-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi in programming and agent tasks. The company sought a pre-investment valuation of $25 billion when it raised funds this year. If the deal goes ahead, Nvidia will further expand from GPUs and networking equipment into models, development tools, and enterprise applications, while increasing customer stickiness to its hardware and software ecosystem. However, this would also amplify conflicts of interest and regulatory scrutiny: Nvidia both supplies the industry and may control important model assets. Subsequent variables include the transaction structure, the attitude of antitrust authorities, Beam's actual performance, and whether the open weight commitment can be maintained after the merger.Source: Reuters IV. Russian airstrikes in Zaporizhzhia kill 20 people; easing sanctions triggers a stronger backlash.On October 10, Russian forces launched an attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, killing 20 people and injuring 18, including three children. The local area is less than 30 kilometers from the front line. This is the third large-scale casualty attack in Ukraine in a week, following attacks in Kramatorsk and Priluki in the previous two days, which killed nearly 80 civilians. Kyiv was also hit by a new round of drone and missile attacks that day, causing power outages in some areas and the subway to be suspended again. The incident occurred a day after the United States announced a temporary easing of sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, which Zelensky said sent the wrong signal to Moscow that it could continue fighting. US, European, and Ukrainian officials had previously discussed a joint peace plan in Miami, but Putin said that given Ukraine's continued attacks on targets inside Russia, it was unlikely that negotiations would resume immediately. The combination of military escalation and easing sanctions could increase Europe's energy, security, and financial burdens, and make any ceasefire arrangement more difficult to build mutual trust. Further attention will be paid to whether the US special envoy will visit Russia, the non-aggression plan for energy facilities, European aid to Ukraine, and whether diesel trade exemptions will translate into new fiscal revenue for Russia.Source: Reuters V. Following the attack on Riyadh Airport, Saudi Arabia insisted on holding an energy and investment conference.Saudi Arabia confirmed on October 10 that the World Petroleum Congress and the Future Investment Initiative will still be held in Riyadh as planned. Previously, the Houthi rebels attacked King Khalid International Airport, killing four people, severely damaging a passenger plane, and causing widespread flight disruptions. Britain, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid travelling to Riyadh. The World Petroleum Congress is scheduled to be held from October 10 to 14, while the Future Investment Initiative is scheduled for October 26 to 29. Financial figures such as JPMorgan Chase CEO Dimon and Citigroup CEO Fraser were originally included in the list of attendees. The organizers stated that security will be strengthened at airports, venues, hotels, and transportation, and that delegates will be provided with alternative routes, such as entering Riyadh by land from Dammam. However, the Italian energy minister has switched to attending the meeting remotely, and Lufthansa, Etihad Airways, and Dubai Airlines have also suspended some flights. Saudi Arabia insists the conference is aimed at maintaining its credibility in energy diplomacy and attracting foreign investment, but the attacks directly pass on the costs of aviation, insurance, and personnel safety to business activities. Going forward, we will focus on actual attendance, flight resumption, the scope of the Houthi attack, and whether the risk premium will affect Saudi investment projects and oil market expectations.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationInterest rates remain the core variable connecting today's news. Long-term yields in the United States are at multi-year highs, posing higher discount rates for projects with longer payback periods such as data centers, model training, and chip procurement. The cooling of AI debt issuance stands in stark contrast to Nvidia's acquisitions of software assets: capital will continue to flow into AI, but prefers leading companies with cash flow, platform control, and pricing power. In terms of exchange rates, high energy prices and safe-haven demand may still support the US dollar. Europe is also under pressure from the Russia-Ukraine war, fiscal spending, and energy imports, limiting the euro's rebound potential. On the commodity side, while the risks in Saudi airspace and Riyadh airport will not directly disrupt crude oil production, they will increase shipping, aviation, and insurance costs. If regional conflicts escalate, oil prices and inflation expectations could push up bond yields again. Risk appetite is therefore likely to remain divergent: leading technology companies with stable cash flow outperform highly leveraged AI projects, energy and defense assets will benefit relatively, while aviation, tourism, and overvalued growth stocks are more sensitive. If China's service sector employment policies can improve wages and job stability, it will boost consumption and RMB expectations. The real test is whether youth employment, residents' income, and service retail can improve simultaneously. Today, we will focus on AI credit spreads, energy prices, European risk assets, and specific tools for China's employment policies.
Cover image:panumas nikhomkhai / Pexels

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-12: Energy Shocks Coupled with AI M&A and Market Stability Signals | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe common theme of the past day was that security shocks are entering asset pricing and policy choices more directly: the conflict in the Middle East and the attack on Riyadh airport have brought energy, transportation and Gulf risk premiums back to the forefront, and although the Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" was announced by the United States, it has not yet been fully confirmed by both Russia and Ukraine. Meanwhile, ahead of the IMF and World Bank annual meetings, debt, high interest rates, and energy prices were listed alongside each other as core constraints on global growth. On the other hand, Amazon's acquisition of AI startup Decart shows that leading platforms are still willing to pay high valuations for models, computing power adaptation, and robot training capabilities. The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has released policy signals to stabilize the market, introduce medium- and long-term funds, and reserve incremental tools. While macroeconomic and industrial factors may seem fragmented, they essentially point to the same issue: in an environment with high capital costs and more fragile supply chains, whoever can obtain stable financing, energy, and policy support is more likely to maintain growth and valuation.
Five key news items1. IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings Focus on Energy Shocks and High Debt, Global Growth Faces RepricingOn October 11, ahead of global finance ministers and central bank officials traveling to Bangkok for the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, the two institutions listed Middle East wars, energy prices, high interest rates, and debt pressures as the most urgent risks. World Bank President Peng Anjie stated that the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz had affected approximately 20% of global oil flows. The G7 has agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil, but since the outbreak of war in February, more than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released, mainly from commercial inventories, and inventories that can quickly enter the market are dwindling. The IMF predicts that global growth will remain at around 3% in 2026, while warning that global public debt is at its highest level since World War II and could exceed 100% of global GDP by 2030. Developing countries need to pay about $400 billion to external creditors this year. The importance lies in the fact that energy supply shocks not only push up inflation, but also squeeze growth through interest rates, capital outflows, and fiscal austerity. It remains to be seen whether the IMF's new forecast, US September inflation, G20 debt arrangements, and emergency reserves can truly lower refined oil prices.Source: Reuters 2. Amazon reportedly plans to acquire Decart for approximately $7 billion, as AI competition continues to integrate into models and infrastructure.On October 11, Reuters, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Amazon is in talks to acquire AI startup Decart for approximately $7 billion, but the deal has not yet been signed and may still fall through due to the emergence of bidders or the breakdown of negotiations. Decart raised $300 million in May, valuing it at nearly $4 billion, with Nvidia as a new investor; Its Lucy model can edit videos in real time, while Oasis generates simulation environments for robot and autonomous driving system training. If the deal is sold for $7 billion, the valuation jump in just a few months will once again validate the competition among large cloud platforms for scarce AI talent, world models, and chip adaptation capabilities. For Amazon, the transaction can more closely link AWS computing power, Trainium chips, and application models; For the market, this means that AI capital expenditures have not subsided due to high interest rates, but valuations will place higher demands on the speed of commercialization. The next steps will be to focus on a formal offer, regulatory review, whether other buyers emerge, and whether Decart can translate its real-time video and simulation capabilities into stable revenue.Source: Reuters 3. The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) is discussing market stabilization and incremental tools, with medium- and long-term funds and investor returns becoming key policy focuses.On October 10, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) disclosed that Chairman Wu Qing held a discussion with heads of listed companies and experts from securities and fund institutions on the capital market and financial situation. The suggestions at the meeting included strengthening the market stabilization mechanism, broadening the sources and entry methods of medium- and long-term funds, expanding patient capital, encouraging qualified listed companies to increase dividend repurchases, optimizing the issuance and listing system, strengthening transaction supervision and cross-border risk monitoring, and studying and reserving more incremental policy tools. The meeting did not directly announce new measures, but against the backdrop of high external interest rates and global risk appetite being disrupted by energy and geopolitical events, regulators' public discussion of "incremental tools" constitutes a policy signal worth watching. Its impact mainly falls on A-share liquidity, long-term fund allocation such as insurance funds and pension funds, shareholder returns of listed companies, and the pace of IPO financing. We will observe whether specific policy documents are formulated, the scale and channels of capital inflows into the market, the execution rate of repurchase dividends, and how the market stabilization mechanism will be activated when cross-border volatility increases.Source: China Securities Regulatory Commission 4. The attack on Riyadh airport dragged down Gulf stock markets, and regional conflicts spilled over into transportation and capital markets.On October 11, an attack on Riyadh International Airport killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300, making it the worst attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. Yemen's Houthi rebels subsequently warned airlines, passengers, and airport staff to stay away from Saudi airports. News weighed on Gulf markets: the Saudi benchmark index closed down 0.2%, and the Saudi National Bank fell 1.1%; The Qatar index fell 1.5%, marking its fourth consecutive trading day lower and closing at its lowest level since May 2020. Egypt's blue-chip index fell 2%. The significance of the event lies not only in the single casualty, but also in the fact that the risks of war in the Middle East extend from oil tankers and straits to civil aviation hubs, conferences, and business activities, potentially raising insurance premiums, diversion costs, and regional financing risk premiums. If the United States participates in further strikes against the Houthis, the radius of the conflict may expand. Going forward, attention should be paid to the resumption of airport operations, airline adjustments, shipping security in Hormuz, contacts between Saudi Arabia and Iran, and the linkage between oil prices and Gulf sovereign assets.Source: Reuters 5. Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, but Kyiv said details were still pending and attacks were continuing.On October 11, US President Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire "effective immediately," but Moscow did not immediately confirm it, and Ukrainian President Zelensky said he was still waiting for details from the US. Following the announcement, Ukraine stated that Russian forces were still attacking the Kharkiv cogeneration facility; Zelenskyy reiterated that Ukraine is willing to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, provided that Russia simultaneously stops attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure. The United States had previously reportedly pressured Kyiv by suspending intelligence-sharing and arms procurement arrangements, and linked Ukraine's attacks on refineries to rising diesel prices. Trump also stated that Russia will supply more than 300,000 tons, or approximately 2.25 million barrels, of diesel to the U.S. and global markets. If this progress is implemented, it could reduce the risk of damage to refining and chemical facilities and energy outages in Europe during the winter. If it is merely a unilateral political statement, it will exacerbate the rift in mutual trust between the US and Ukraine. The key issues ahead are Russia's official response, the records of the attacks on both sides, the monitoring mechanism, and whether the diesel supply can actually be shipped.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe market has entered a trading framework where "inflationary shocks and policy support coexist". On the interest rate side, rising energy and fertilizer prices will raise inflation expectations, making it more difficult for the Federal Reserve and other central banks to quickly shift to easing. Highly indebted countries are also facing rising refinancing costs, and the maturity premium for long-term government bonds may remain high. On the exchange rate side, high interest rates and safe-haven demand typically support the US dollar and suppress emerging market currencies with high foreign debt. The performance of the RMB depends on whether domestic policies to stabilize growth and capital markets can improve expectations and offset the strength of the US dollar. In terms of risk appetite, the uncertainty surrounding the Riyadh airport attack and the Russia-Ukraine ceasefire will amplify early-week volatility, making Gulf, aviation, transportation, and insurance assets more sensitive. On the commodity side, the focus should be on diesel cracking price spreads, Brent crude oil, and fertilizer prices: emergency reserves can buffer spot shortages, but they cannot replace stable production capacity and shipping in the long term. Technology valuations have diverged. Amazon's potential high premium for Decart indicates that high-quality models and simulation assets are still scarce. However, when risk-free interest rates are high, AI targets with slow cash flow realization are more likely to be discounted. Regarding Chinese policies, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) is discussing medium- and long-term funding, dividend repurchases, and incremental instruments, which can help improve expectations for downside protection in the equity market. However, what truly affects pricing are the speed of instrument implementation, net capital inflows, and corporate profitability. Today, we should observe US inflation expectations, IMF annual meeting statements, oil inventories, whether the attacks on Russian and Ukrainian energy facilities have stopped, and the concretization of A-share market stabilization policies within the same framework. Cover image:Peter Beke / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-13: Oil prices rise in tandem with the US dollar, computing power and trade realign | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past day, the market has faced two types of "cost reassessments" simultaneously: one from war and energy. Saudi Arabia's capital airport was extended after a series of attacks, and Russia was accused by Ukraine of continuing to attack energy facilities. Brent crude oil rose to around $107 a barrel, and the dollar hit an 18-month high on safe-haven concerns and inflation concerns. The other category comes from industry and trade. Microsoft is preparing to deploy its self-developed Maia 300 chip on a large scale to reduce AI computing power costs and reliance on external suppliers; China and Europe, in turn, used import quotas to resolve the dispute over Chinese hybrid vehicles in exchange for predictable trade arrangements. The common theme is that high interest rates have not deterred strategic investment, but they have forced governments and businesses to pay more attention to energy security, computing efficiency, supply chain autonomy, and market access. In the short term, pricing will depend on US inflation and the progress of the conflict; in the medium term, it will depend on whether these costs can be absorbed by productivity, policy support, and industrial upgrading.
Five key news items1. The US dollar rose to an 18-month high as oil prices and safe-haven demand reignited interest rate pressures.On October 12, the US dollar index rose 0.37% to 102.58, its highest level since April 2025; The euro fell to about $1.1156, near a 17-month low, while the dollar rose to 158.66 against the yen. Funds are avoiding the risk of conflict in the Middle East while awaiting this week's US consumer price data for September. Brent crude rose 2.3% to $107.17 a barrel that day, about 45% higher than before the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran, adding to concerns about the resurgence of inflation. The market still gives about a 78% probability that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged this month, but Cleveland Fed President Hamak advocates that restrictive policies should be maintained more quickly. Long positions in the US dollar had increased to approximately $36 billion as of October 7, compared to only $8.4 billion three weeks ago. The impact is further tightening of global financing conditions and increased pressure on the currencies of the euro, yen and high-debt emerging markets. The core variables going forward are the US CPI, the sustainability of oil prices, French debt risk, and communication from the Federal Reserve.Source: Reuters 2. Microsoft releases Maia 300, plans to deploy over a million self-developed AI chips next year.On October 12, Microsoft announced its third-generation self-developed AI acceleration chip, the Maia 300, and plans to begin "multi-gigawatt" deployments starting in 2027, with a potential quantity exceeding 1 million units, for Microsoft's internal AI services and model inference and complex agent tasks on Azure. The Maia 300 uses a chip architecture: the key computing parts use TSMC's 2nm process, while functions such as data transmission use the lower-cost 3nm process. Each rack accommodates 96 chips and consumes approximately 167 kilowatts of power; Microsoft stated that its effective computing power per megawatt is about 40% higher than that of leading GPU systems, but did not disclose specific comparisons. The company expects capital expenditures to exceed $175 billion this year, indicating that the cost reduction goal does not mean cutting AI investment, but rather increasing output per watt and per dollar through the synergy of chips, racks, networks and software systems. For Nvidia and the cloud computing industry, this will strengthen the vertical integration of large platforms. Going forward, it depends on the mass production yield, actual model performance, Azure customer adoption rate, and whether the million-unit scale can be delivered on schedule.Source: Reuters 3. China and the EU finalize hybrid vehicle import arrangements, exchanging quotas for a cooling of trade frictions.China's Ministry of Commerce disclosed on October 12 that after three months of intensive consultations, China and the EU have reached new arrangements for Chinese hybrid vehicles to enter the EU. The EU plans to limit imports of hybrid vehicles from China to 350,000 units per year starting in early December, and allow quotas to increase by 6% annually. The measures will last for four years and will also apply to other trading partners. The EU estimates that this will reduce China's hybrid vehicle exports to the EU by more than half, which could have reached 800,000 units by 2026, and reduce the market share of Chinese-made cars in the EU from about 12% to 6%. China emphasized that the quotas China receives should not be lower than those from other sources, the measures should not target or discriminate against Chinese companies, and should be increased based on the 2025 level to ensure stable growth. The agreement avoids an immediate escalation of the dispute, but it will prompt Chinese automakers to accelerate local production in Europe, model restructuring, and supply chain layout. It remains to be seen whether the EU summit will add trade defense tools, quota allocation details, and whether similar progress can be made in the negotiations on tariffs on pure electric vehicles.Source: China negotiation results, Reuters；Source: Details of EU measures, Reuters 4. Riyadh airport closure extended until Saturday as regional conflict begins to impact aviation and investment activities.On October 12, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authorities extended the closure of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport until 21:00 (GMT) on October 17, citing the need to complete facility security and operational preparations. The airport, Saudi Arabia’s second-busiest after Jeddah, has been suspended since Saturday’s Houthi attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Another round of attacks on Sunday killed one person and injured nearly 12 others. The Houthis claimed another attack on the airport with ballistic missiles on Monday, while Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted a missile aimed at Riyadh, prompting several airlines to cancel or extend their flight suspensions. Importantly, the conflict has expanded from oil tankers, straits, and energy facilities to major civil aviation hubs, directly impacting passengers, cargo, insurance, international conferences, and Saudi Arabia's plans to attract investment. Continued closures will drive up diversion and supply chain costs and deepen the risk premium for Gulf assets. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether the airport will resume flights on schedule, the extent of airline suspensions, the strength of Saudi Arabia's counterattack, and whether the United States will expand its intervention.Source: Reuters 5. Ukraine claims Russian forces attacked six energy targets, prompting the EU to impose its largest sanctions since the invasion.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on October 12 that Russian airstrikes on at least six energy targets overnight and in the morning, including natural gas facilities and gas stations, indicate that the "energy ceasefire" previously announced by US President Trump has not been implemented. Ukraine stated that it did not attack a Russian oil refinery that night and was willing to cease fire if Russia reciprocally complied. The Kremlin said negotiations were still ongoing, but rejected Zelensky's proposal for a 60-day comprehensive ceasefire, emphasizing that Russia was seeking "long-term peace" rather than a ceasefire. The night attack in Kharkiv killed at least three people, and subsequent attacks injured at least 22 more. Kyiv's electricity, water supply, and metro systems had previously been continuously affected. On the same day, EU foreign ministers added 1,569 individuals and entities to the sanctions list, calling it the largest single sanctions package since 2022. The incident means that energy infrastructure remains the core lever of the winter war and fuel prices. The next step will be to observe whether Russia formally accepts verifiable arrangements, attack records, sanctions enforcement, and whether the US-Russia diesel deal will weaken Western pressure.Source: Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe current market chain is relatively clear: risks in the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine are pushing up crude oil and refined oil products, while energy inflation is raising long-term interest rates and the US dollar, ultimately compressing financing space for overvalued assets and emerging markets. If the US CPI is higher than expected, the market may raise the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike again, causing the US dollar index and US Treasury yields to rise in tandem. If the data is moderate, safe-haven demand may still limit the dollar's decline. In terms of exchange rates, the euro is also dragged down by French fiscal risks, while the yen faces expectations of intervention as it approaches the 160 mark. On the commodity side, in addition to Brent crude oil, diesel cracking price spreads, aviation fuel, and shipping insurance premiums should also be monitored, as airport and strait risks are shifting from "expected" to real operational disruptions. The key to technology valuation has shifted from "whether there is a demand for AI" to "computing power per watt and return on capital". Microsoft's self-developed chips strengthen the bargaining power of cloud vendors, which may reduce unit inference costs, but it also means higher upfront capital expenditures, leading to structural differentiation in the power supply chains of Nvidia, TSMC, and data centers. On the Chinese policy and industry side, the Sino-European automotive quota has reduced the uncertainty of the worst-case scenario, but the export ceiling will drive local factory construction, brand concentration, and supply chain relocation. Whether RMB and Chinese equity assets can benefit also depends on domestic demand, corporate profits, and subsequent measures to stabilize growth. Today, US inflation expectations, oil prices, the US dollar, the progress of Riyadh's flight resumption, the loss of Russian and Ukrainian energy facilities, and the details of the implementation of China-EU quotas should be tracked in the same risk map. Cover image:imgix / Unsplash

entry.title: Daily Briefing | 2026-10-14: IMF raises growth, energy and AI risks resonate | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeThe core of the past 24 hours has not been a single positive or negative factor, but rather "growth remains supported while risks rise." The IMF has slightly raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, but this resilience is highly dependent on AI capital spending and has withstood the combined pressure of Middle East wars, oil prices above $100, bond yields, and public debt. Google's full rollout of Gemini 4 Argon to developers and enterprises demonstrates that the competition for cutting-edge models is shifting from parameter competition to complex workflows, pricing, and business conversions. China has approved Visa's establishment of a domestic bank card clearing institution, sending a new signal for financial opening up; Meanwhile, a new window of contact has emerged in the mediation between Russia and Ukraine, and the missile strike on Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex has brought energy security risks to the forefront of the market. Growth, technology investment, and geopolitical shocks are being repriced within the same interest rate and valuation framework.
Five key news items1. The IMF slightly raised its global growth rate, but AI, oil prices, and debt pose common risks.The International Monetary Fund released its latest World Economic Outlook in Bangkok on October 13, projecting global real GDP growth of 3.1% in 2026, an upward revision of 0.1 percentage points from its July forecast. Growth is expected to be 3.4% in 2027, consistent with the July forecast. The United States is projected to grow by 2.3% for both this year and next, the Eurozone has raised its forecast to 1.1% for 2026, and China has lowered its forecast to 4.5% and 4.0% for this year and next, respectively. The main driver of the upward revision comes from AI infrastructure investment and its impact on supply chain economies such as South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, and Thailand, but this resilience is uneven: currently 32 economies contribute 95% of global growth, compared to 54 in April. The IMF's baseline scenario assumes that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen by March 2027; If the war pushes oil prices to $130 a barrel, global growth could decrease by another 0.5 percentage points and inflation could increase by 1.1 percentage points in 2027. If AI productivity fails to materialize and triggers a correction in investment and asset prices, global output could decrease by a cumulative 1.1% in 2028, with the United States experiencing a 1.8% decrease. This means that the market cannot only trade "upward revision of growth", but also keep an eye on oil prices, long-term yields, AI profit realization and fiscal buffer repair.IMF release page｜Reuters 2. Google fully launches Gemini 4 Argon, bringing cutting-edge model competition into enterprise workflows.On October 13, Google launched its flagship model, Gemini 4 Argon, to developers, businesses, and paying users, covering the Gemini API, AI Studio, Google Cloud, Gemini apps, Search AI Mode, and Antigravity encoding tools. The company positions it as a long-chain, multi-step task encompassing software engineering, finance, law, cybersecurity, and science. The enterprise platform documentation shows that it supports approximately 1.049 million token contexts and can configure inference strength. The pricing adopts a clear promotional window: before November 30, input $2 in tokens per million, output $10, and then increase to $4 and $20, with a 95% discount on cache input. Google claims that after internal or early teams used Argon in Antigravity, agent code submissions increased by more than 35% and rollbacks decreased by nearly a third, but these are still data disclosed by the manufacturer. This official opening has shifted the focus of competition from "whether the model is released" to unit task cost, reliability, safety boundaries, and corporate procurement transformation; The next step is to observe retention after the price doubles, independent benchmarks, actual inference costs, and the true degree of substitution for manual review in complex industry scenarios.Google Cloud Announcement｜Introduction to Google Models｜Reuters 3. China approves Visa's establishment of a domestic bank card clearing institution, marking another step forward in financial opening-up.The People's Bank of China has approved Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing institution. Visa must complete the preparations within one year before applying to open for business. Bank card clearing business licenses will only be issued after approval by the People's Bank of China and the State Financial Regulatory Commission. This is a preparatory license rather than a formal opening, but it ends Visa's years-long wait and gives it the potential to enter a huge market dominated by China UnionPay, following American Express and Mastercard, which were approved to conduct related business in 2020. Data from the People's Bank of China shows that in 2025, Chinese bank cards will process 4.6 trillion transactions, totaling 963.60 trillion yuan. The policy significance lies in the fact that, despite the coexistence of external trade frictions and weak domestic demand, Beijing is still sending signals of opening up the service sector and financial markets through the sensitive area of payment infrastructure. For Visa, true business value depends on the final license, shareholding and data compliance arrangements, merchant network access, and synergy with the local mobile payment ecosystem. Going forward, it remains to be seen whether the one-year preparation period can be completed as scheduled, and whether the opening signal will extend to more financial services sectors.Reuters｜Administrative Measures for Bank Card Clearing Institutions 4. Zelenskyy seeks further talks with US special envoy; Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire still depends on fulfillment of agreements.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on October 13 that he had proposed to U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner through his team to hold a new round of talks in the coming days, hoping to push Kyiv and Moscow back onto the negotiating track. Previously, the US explained to Ukraine during last week's talks that the arrangement to allow Russian diesel exports was intended to entice Moscow to return to the negotiating table; Zelenskyy also stated that Ukraine supports Trump's proposal for a ceasefire in energy facilities, but only if Russia complies. The new development is that the window for diplomatic contact has been redefined to "the coming days," but there is still a clear gap between economic incentives and mutual trust on the battlefield: easing restrictions on Russian energy exports may increase negotiating leverage and may also be seen by Kyiv and Europe as providing a source of revenue in advance. The market impact will first be reflected in the risk premium for diesel, crude oil, European natural gas, and shipping, rather than an immediate full ceasefire. Follow-up observation points are whether the talks will take place, whether a verifiable mechanism can be established for the energy ceasefire, and whether any diesel arrangement will include quantity, duration, and sanctions rebound clauses.Reuters 5. A missile hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters complex, causing energy supply chain risks to spill over from waterways to central facilities.Reuters, citing sources at Saudi Aramco, reported that a ballistic missile struck the Aramco headquarters complex in Dahlan, eastern Saudi Arabia, on the evening of October 13, damaging the top three floors of an office tower and causing a fire. The park houses an important operations center that coordinates the network of oil fields, pipelines, refineries and export terminals. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a missile in Dahlan, with debris falling into a residential area. Aramco has not yet officially responded. The Houthi rebels had previously threatened the Dahlan headquarters and the Riyadh refinery by name, and had continued to launch missiles and drones at key Saudi facilities over the past week. The conflict is set against the backdrop of Saudi Arabia's renewed involvement in the Yemeni conflict, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait has become more crucial to global energy transportation after the Strait of Hormuz was affected by the Iranian war. There is currently no evidence of disruption in crude oil production or exports, and therefore damage to buildings cannot be directly equated with a loss of supply; But the attack proves that the risk has extended from the maritime throat to the operational hub. Next, we need to look at the assessment of Aramco's facilities, the intensity of Saudi retaliation, the effectiveness of air defenses, shipping diversions and insurance rates, and whether Brent oil prices are forming a sustained rather than impulsive premium.Reuters Market Correlation and Today's ObservationThe key contradiction in asset pricing is whether AI investment's support for growth can outweigh the impact of energy shocks on inflation and interest rates. The IMF's upward revision of growth could have improved risk appetite, but oil prices above $100, attacks on Saudi energy facilities, and uncertainty over the Straits of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb will push up inflation expectations, shipping insurance, and business costs, making it more difficult for major central banks to cut interest rates quickly and making it easier for long-term government bond yields to remain high. The US dollar remains strong, supported by safe-haven demand and high interest rate spreads, putting pressure on the currencies of energy-importing countries. If verifiable progress is made in the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire negotiations, the premium for diesel, European natural gas, and related risks may decline first. Regarding commodities, a distinction should be made between "facility damage" and "actual production cuts," focusing on Aramco's export data, inventory, and routes, rather than just chasing headlines. Tech stocks face two-way pricing: Gemini 4 Argon strengthens the narrative of AI applications and computing power demand, but the costs after the promotional price expires, company retention, and productivity realization will determine whether the high valuation can be sustained. In China, the approval of Visa's establishment reflects the intention to open up the service sector and improve foreign investment expectations, but it cannot replace the recovery of domestic demand. The RMB, Hong Kong stocks, and payment industry chain need to observe subsequent licensing, capital inflows, and fiscal and consumer policies. The most worthwhile things to watch today are whether oil prices and US Treasury yields will rise in tandem, the strength of the US dollar, earnings expectations for leading AI companies, and whether geopolitical risks can shift from shocks to verifiable diplomatic cooling. Cover image:Jan Jobczyk / Unsplash

entry.title: Who is better at "speaking human language"? Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5 Writing Test | Aden's Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Origin and test environmentThe conclusion is first: after four rounds of testing, both models have their strengths and weaknesses in "speaking human language". Claude Opus 5.5 is better in terms of sense of proportion and "non-fabrication" of SMS messages; Longer articles in Gemini 4 Argon are smoother, but the default writing style is heavy. Neither of them escaped the AI-driven tone when it came to writing long articles.
In my daily use, I've noticed that recent versions of GPT and Gemini are somewhat "non-human". Coincidentally, Gemini 4 Argon was released on October 14, 2026, and I heard that Claude Opus 5.5 had put some effort into writing it, so I tested the two together on the same day. Test Environment:
Gemini 4 Argon: Gemini web version, mode selection "Argon High Point", no developer tools used. Claude Opus 5.5: Used in Claude Code, with a thinking intensity of "medium". GPT did not participate in this test. Each problem and each model was run only once.
Question design and item-by-item scoring were done in another Claude Opus 5.5 dialogue. In other words,Claude is rating himself.This is the biggest source of deviation in this article, and readers can make their own judgments by referring to the original text below. The model output cited in this article is the original text, with only information that can point to individuals replaced with code names, such as "Person A", "School X", "Major X", and "City X". The rest of the content remains unchanged. Test methods and scoring checklistThe test consists of four rounds, each increasing the difficulty of the problems exposed in the previous round:
Default writing styleOnly give the topic, and do not write "speak in plain language" or "use plain language" in the prompts, otherwise it will become a test of whether it will obey instructions. Go to AI cavityI explicitly request that memorable quotes, metaphors, and sublimations be removed, and that I not fabricate my experiences. Ask a question firstTell the model it doesn't know my experience and allow it to ask me first. Insufficient materialsGive me a very thin piece of material and see if it will be embellished.
The first round used three topics to test different problems:
Topic Type What are the main tests?
Explain "overfitting" to parents explanatory type Terminology piling up, false profound
My true feelings about the first semester of studying abroad empirical Chicken soup, empty lyricism
A friend's WeChat reply asking where to go for the weekend daily short message format expansion
The score is based on the following list of symptoms of "not speaking human language". Out of 10 points, the measure is whether it sounds like a normal person's writing, not the amount of information.
Symptoms typical example
"No... but..." The sentence structure is rampant. "This is not just a learning experience, but a transformation."
Empty sublimation and summary In short, ultimately.
Slang and big words Empowerment, tools, underlying logic, closed loop
Stacking metaphors and parallels "It is…, it is…, it is even more…”
format expansion Short content can also be subtitled, bolded, listed, or emoji.
Pretending to have personal experience Fabricate "I remember the first time..." for the user.
Correct nonsense "Everyone's situation is different, and you need to choose according to your own circumstances."
Forced interaction at the end "I hope this helps! Feel free to ask me anytime if you have any questions~”
There are two other quick judgment methods: one isReading testRead the article aloud, and the question is which sentence you would never say to a friend. Seconddeletion testThe fact that half of the content was deleted but almost no information was lost indicates that the original text was inflated. Round 1, Topic 1: Explaining "overfitting" to parentsThis question is tied on both sides, both scoring 8 points, and most of the questions are in plain language. Hint words:
My parents didn't know anything about computers, and they asked me what "overfitting" meant in the machine learning I was learning. Help me write an explanation for them.
Gemini 4 Argon Original text Mom and Dad, you can think of training computers (machine learning) as teaching a student to prepare for an exam, while "overfitting" means that the student has memorized the questions and won't be able to apply them to other situations. When we teach computers to recognize objects, it's like giving students a workbook. Ideally, after completing several sets of tests, students should summarize the problem-solving patterns so that they can do the same when they encounter new problems. But when "overfitting" occurs, the computer is too rigid—it doesn't understand the underlying patterns, but instead memorizes every question in the workbook, even the typos and question numbers. And the result is:
Regular test (using old data): 100 points because I memorized all the questions. Real exam (encountering new situations): It's a complete mess; you just need to change the numbers on the question and you won't know anything at all.
To give another real-life example: Let's say I only use our "brown teddy dog" to teach the computer to recognize dogs. If the computer "overfits," it will rigidly believe that "only dogs are brown, curly-haired, small, or even have a red bell around their necks." When a large golden retriever is brought to it tomorrow, it won't recognize it. Therefore, a large part of my work is to prevent computers from "rote memorization," to teach them to grasp key points, find patterns, and truly apply what they have learned to other situations.
Claude Opus 5.5 Original text The version that can be sent directly to parents: What is "overfitting"? For example, it's like a child preparing for an exam. There was a student whose teacher gave him a workbook. He memorized the answers to every question in it by heart. He was tested on the questions in the workbook and got perfect marks every time. But when it comes to the official exam, if the question is slightly different in number or wording, he won't know how. Because he only memorized the answers and didn't truly understand the principles behind solving the problems. The same applies to computer "learning". We show the computer many examples and let it summarize the patterns on its own. For example, show it thousands of photos of cats to help it learn to recognize cats. If it "overlearns," it will write down the details in these photos as patterns, such as "cats are all on the sofa" or "cats have white walls in the background." As a result, we tested it with photos it had seen, and they were all correct; If you take a new photo, such as a cat on the grass, it won't recognize it. This situation where someone performs well on practice questions but fails when faced with new problems is called "overfitting". One of the important tasks of our research is to make computers learn real patterns like good students, rather than rote memorization, so that they can make correct judgments even when they encounter new situations they have never seen before. If you want it to be shorter, you can just keep the first paragraph of the exam metaphor and the last sentence of the summary. Parents usually understand it immediately.
rating
model score advantage Problem
Gemini 4 Argon 8 The metaphor for memorizing exam questions is apt; "memorizing even printing errors and question numbers" accurately highlights the tendency to treat noise as a pattern. A list was used in a passage addressed to parents; They fictionalized "our brown Teddy dog"; Training with only one dog is closer to "too little data" and is not a typical overfit; The ending is slightly sublimated.
Claude Opus 5.5 8 There are no list symbols throughout the text; "The cats are all on the sofa" and "The background is all white walls" accurately explain how random details are treated as patterns. "We do research" does not correspond to the user's actual identity; An additional subheading was added at the beginning; The ending is also sublimated.
Round 1, Topic 2: Real Feelings of the First Semester of Studying AbroadThis question is worth 5 points on both sides, but the problems are different: Gemini is a fancy motivational quote, while Claude is a plain template that fabricates experiences for the user. Hint words:
I'm writing an article for my juniors who are preparing to pursue graduate studies abroad, sharing their most authentic feelings about the first semester of graduate school.
It should be noted that Claude's conversations have a memory function enabled, so it knows the user's school and major background, while Gemini does not. This allowed Claude to write more specifically, which directly led to the fiction problem mentioned below. Gemini 4 Argon Original text To you about to embark on a long journey: The first semester of graduate school, those real moments no one told you in advance The moment you receive your acceptance letter, apply for your visa, and fill your suitcase, you probably think that the script for pursuing a master's degree abroad is an academic journey full of exotic flavor. But when you actually land, dragging two large suitcases weighing nearly 30 kilograms in front of an empty mattress in an unfamiliar apartment, the true face of the first semester of graduate school is just beginning to be revealed. "Hard landing" without buffer period Many people think that the first two weeks abroad are a "honeymoon period" for adjusting to the time difference, shopping at IKEA, and taking photos to post on social media. In fact, the pace of graduate school is so fast that it doesn't give you any breathing room. You might be struggling on Monday to get a bank card, connect to Wi-Fi, or distinguish between light and dark soy sauce from all-English labels at the supermarket, but on Tuesday you were already sitting in the lecture hall facing dozens of pages of Reading material handed out by the professor and the first week's pre-class quiz. Life's trivialities and academic pressures don't come one after the other; they hit you simultaneously before you've even figured out your way home. The academic gap from "being fed" to "finding one's own way" During undergraduate studies, teachers often break down the knowledge points from the textbook and explain them to you. But in the graduate classroom, the professor assumes that you have mastered the basic tools. In a two-hour class, the PowerPoint presentations were flipped through like a revolving lantern. The class only discussed the core framework and cutting-edge controversies. The rest of the derivation, code implementation, or literature review was all done by myself in the library after class. A more real challenge comes from high-intensity output in an all-English environment. In the first few weeks, you might have looked up a screen full of new words the night before and read the literature thoroughly. The next day, when you go to a Seminar, you still need to race your brain for a few seconds before you can get through to a classmate who speaks at such a fast pace. When it comes to Group projects, you also have to learn how to deal with team members from different cultural backgrounds and routines while advancing the progress. Almost everyone has experienced that frustrating feeling of "trying so hard, but still feeling like you know nothing" late at night in October. Folded Time: A Three-Front Battle Between Study, Life, and Job Search If a four-year undergraduate degree is a marathon, then a one- to two-year master's degree is more like a 100-meter sprint. What causes the most anxiety is often not the coursework itself, but rather...Everything is crammed into the same timeline.。 Many students have only been in school for two weeks and haven't even familiarized themselves with the campus map before having to join the ranks of those seeking jobs in the fall recruitment or local areas. During the day, I attend classes and revise group reports. In the evening, I go to the supermarket to buy discounted meat and vegetables to cook for myself. After washing the dishes and sitting back at my desk at 9 p.m., I also have to revise my resume, do practice questions, and prepare for video interviews across time zones. You will suddenly realize that your parents used to shield you from so many fragments of life; When cooking, washing clothes, fixing light bulbs, and calculating exchange rates all become your own business, even just getting a hot meal on time and seven hours of sleep can be considered a remarkable form of self-discipline. From "social anxiety" to learning to reconcile with loneliness During the first few days of Orientation, you might attend various gatherings and suddenly have dozens of new friends on your phone. But as soon as classes officially start, everyone will quickly return to their respective lives. Graduate students' social interactions are very direct and realistic. There are no fixed classes, class schedules vary, and everyone is in a hurry. Gradually, you will go through a period of extreme quiet: going to the library alone to reserve a seat, going to the supermarket alone with headphones on, and walking home alone with coffee in the evening. You may feel lonely at first, but perhaps after the midterm exams, you will suddenly fall in love with this undisturbed freedom.Transforming "loneliness" into "solitude" is the most important compulsory course in the first semester of studying abroad. When you stop forcing yourself to socialize in order to fit in, and focus your energy on your sleep, meals, and books, your mind will actually calm down. A final piece of truth If you doubt yourself late at night during your first semester because of incomprehensible literature, incompatible data, or a burnt dinner, please remember:This panic is absolutely normal, not because you are not good enough, but because you are simultaneously adapting to a new language, a new set of academic rules, and a completely independent life. In the first semester, don't strive for perfection in everything. Allow yourself to get distracted occasionally in class, allow your first draft to be written in a stumbling manner, and follow the principle of "finish first, then perfect" to deal with the mountain of tasks. When you feel like you can't take it anymore, don't force yourself. Make a video call home, or simply close your computer and go to sleep. After surviving these most chaotic first three months, when you finish submitting your last final paper and walk out of the library into the evening breeze of a foreign street, you will be surprised to find that the version of yourself who used to have to look up translation software even when buying groceries has already grown a tough armor without you even realizing it. Wishing you a smooth start and a first semester of your own.

I hope you have a better understanding before you set off. Pace: So fast that there's no time to adapt School X has a three-semester system, with only about 10 weeks of teaching time per semester. In China, a course can be learned slowly over a semester. Here, homework begins in the second week, and there are quizzes or project milestones in the fourth or fifth week. My biggest feeling is:There is no "adaptation period"。 Having just finished adjusting to the time difference and found the classroom, the first deadline is already right in front of us. By the time you feel like you've "finally figured it out," final exams have arrived. So don't expect to gradually get into the swing of things after school starts. I was already lucky if I could understand half of the lectures in the first week; I relied entirely on watching the recording after class. What's even more difficult than listening to lectures isopen mouth。 During the tutorial, everyone was rushing to speak. I had organized a sentence in my mind, and the topic had already passed. During group discussions, people clearly had ideas, but remained silent for fear of saying the wrong thing. Later I discovered that my classmates actually rarely pay attention to grammar; what they care about is whether you contribute your viewpoints. It's okay if you don't say it perfectly, but not saying it will really be a loss. Learning method: No one is pushing you Undergraduate programs in China have classes, counselors, fixed class schedules, and classmates, and someone will remind you of many things. Here, no one takes attendance, no one presses for homework, and all course information is available on websites and forums. Whether you read it or not is entirely up to you. The homework is also different. Many programming assignments only give a vague requirement, and you have to decide the rest of the design, testing, and report writing yourself. Group projects are more challenging: division of labor, communication, and schedule coordination take more time than the code itself. There is another point that must be emphasized:Academic integrity。 References should be standardized, code should not be copied arbitrarily, and discussions with classmates should also be balanced. This matter is taken seriously here. Life: Loneliness is the norm, not failure In the first few weeks after arriving, novelty overwhelms everything. Beach, coffee, blue sky—I want to take pictures and post them on my WeChat Moments every day. After the novelty wears off, loneliness will slowly emerge. One person cooks, one person meets deadlines, and when they get sick, they have to go to the pharmacy by themselves. It's nighttime in China, but early morning here, so you have to take into account the time difference to talk to someone. I want to tell you: this feeling is normal, almost everyone has experienced it. It doesn't mean you're not suited to studying abroad; it just means you're experiencing true independence. A few suggestions for you
Don't choose a semester that is too full. Give yourself room to adapt first, and your grades and performance will be more stable. List the deadlines for all classes in the first week of school. Stick it on the wall or put it in a calendar, and 10 weeks will go by faster than you think. Recording is a lifeline, but don't rely on it. If possible, go to the site. If you have any questions, ask the teacher or tutor on the spot. Take the initiative to speak, even if it stumbles. Saying one sentence in a tutorial is more useful than memorizing ten words after class. Make good use of school resources. Academic tutoring, writing centers, psychological counseling, and employment services are all free, and many people don't use them until graduation. Make a few friends who can look out for each other. It doesn't have to be a lot, but someone who can lend a hand when you're sick or have a breakdown. Thinking about job hunting as soon as possible. The timeline for internships and campus recruitment starts earlier than you might think, and you can start learning about it in the first semester.
in the end Looking back on the first semester, the hardest weeks were precisely the times when I grew the fastest. I learned to manage my own time, express my opinions in English, and live a good life on my own. If you are preparing to go abroad right now, you don't need to think about studying abroad too much, nor do you need to think about it too difficult. It is an experience that requires you to give it your all and will definitely make you stronger. Wishing you all the best, see you in City X.

background information I didn't ask; I already knew in the conversation. It's reasonable to ask if it doesn't know.
Claude's question is more relevant. Questions like "Were there any periods when you were in particularly bad shape?" and "If you could do it all over again, which practice would you change?" are the only ways to unearth real feelings. However, Claude knows the user's background, which is partly why the problem is more specific. Round 4: Will they fabricate things when there is insufficient material?Both sides maintained their bottom line, not making up a single concrete detail that could be imagined, nor adding any memorable quotes or elevations. Compared to the first round of inspirational articles, this is a qualitative improvement. The difference is that Gemini adds a lot of causal relationships that users haven't mentioned, while Claude is the most restrained but reads like a table. test materialThis answer isfictional test materialWritten by Claude, this is not the actual experience of the testers. There are two types of traps buried in the material. First, the material only contains two or three hundred words of information, but you are required to write 800 words. Let's see if the model keeps it short or relies on clichés and fabrications to make up the word count. Second, some blanks were deliberately left waiting to be filled in:

Gemini 4 Argon Original text Title: School X Major X First Semester: A True Record for Juniors I studied major Y in China for my undergraduate degree. This is my first time going abroad, and I am currently studying major X in city X, school X. Having just finished my first semester, I'm listing a few things I've actually experienced over the past few months as a reference for my juniors who are preparing to come.
When renting and daily life first started, the most troublesome thing was renting a place. Because it was my first time traveling abroad, I couldn't quite understand many of the clauses in the rental contract, which was entirely in English. For the past two weeks, I stayed in a short-term rental, while making a transition and dealing with finding a house and reviewing the contract. The house I later booked was near the school, so I could walk directly to school, saving me commuting time. In terms of food, I've basically been cooking for myself this semester. Because I also have to take care of my studies, my cooking is very simple, just enough for my daily three meals a day. Although I studied major Y as an undergraduate and have a certain professional foundation, it still takes time to adapt to the new all-English teaching environment. In the first semester, I took three courses, including a database course, which was actually more difficult than I had imagined. I usually only understand about half of the lectures I take in this course. What I didn't understand in class, I mainly relied on watching the course Recording myself after class to make up for. Adapting to the language and classroom is relatively slow. At first, I basically just listened in class, and it wasn't until the end of the semester that I dared to speak in the Tutorial (tutoring and discussion class). The fifth week was the hardest part of the semester when it came to rushing homework and group projects. That week, two assignments happened to be due at the same time. I usually have to spend a lot of time watching recordings and catching up on lessons, and I was rushing to finish both assignments at the same time, so I didn't have enough time. I really couldn't keep up that week. Another specific problem is Group projects. There are four people in our group, but one of them hasn't replied to our messages. Projects inherently require time for communication and cooperation. If you can't contact team members, you become very passive in advancing the task. Regarding course selection advice: Looking back over the past few months, if I could do it all over again, I wouldn't choose three courses in the first semester, but two. When I first arrived, it took a lot of effort to deal with the rental contract and get used to cooking for myself. After the start of the school year, you will have to adapt to listening to classes in English and spend a lot of time watching recorded broadcasts to catch up on classes. In the first semester, you have to take three courses directly. If you encounter a situation like the fifth week where several assignments are due at the same time, time will be very tight. It would be much safer to choose two courses first, giving yourself room to adapt to the difficulty of the courses and the pace of life.
#SchoolX #CityXStudyAbroad #CountryXStudyAbroad #SchoolXMajorX #StudyAbroadDaily #CourseSelectionSuggestions
