entry.title: Daily Briefing | 22 October 2026: Prospects for the resumption of trilateral Russia-Ukraine talks, security concerns in Saudi Arabia and further increases in AI capital expenditure | Aden’s Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original. Today's main themeOver the past 24 hours, diplomatic détente and security escalations have occurred simultaneously, with the markets fluctuating between the two. Following talks between US Special Envoy Witkov and Putin in St Petersburg, the Kremlin indicated a willingness to resume trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine negotiations in November; almost simultaneously, the US ordered the evacuation of some diplomatic personnel from Saudi Arabia due to ongoing attacks by the Houthi rebels, causing oil prices, US Treasury yields and the US dollar to rise briefly. Turning to technology companies, Meta’s third-quarter revenue grew by 26 per cent, but substantial legal costs and full-year capital expenditure of nearly US$140 billion pushed free cash flow into negative territory; whilst Tesla’s profit margins rebounded, its operating profit fell sharply. China, meanwhile, is promoting the integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation through documents issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, with the policy focus shifting towards the commercialisation of research outcomes and enterprise-led initiatives. In summary, the market must simultaneously factor in two key developments: when geopolitical risks will subside, and when investment in AI will translate into cash flow.
Key News1. Putin meets with Witkov; Russia agrees to resume trilateral talks in NovemberUS Special Envoy Witkov held talks with Putin in St Petersburg for approximately three hours on 21 October; this marked their ninth face-to-face meeting. Prior to the talks, the Russian side released Stephen Hubbard, a retired American teacher who had been detained. Kremlin aide Ushakov stated that Russia is prepared to resume trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine, possibly in mid-November and likely in Abu Dhabi; Zelenskyy also expressed his support, hoping that a meeting at the negotiating team level would take place “no later than early November”. However, Ushakov also noted that the new proposals put forward by Europe and Kyiv during the Oslo talks “contained little of substance”. The previous round of US-mediated negotiations stalled in February; following the US-Israeli military action against Iran, the talks have remained suspended ever since. The implication is that, once negotiations resume, market expectations regarding European energy, Russian refined oil supplies and European defence spending will all be repriced. However, at present, the two sides have merely agreed to sit down and talk; no public progress has been made on core issues such as the framework for a ceasefire, territorial matters and security guarantees. Key points to watch: the specific date and level of the trilateral talks; whether a ceasefire regarding energy facilities can be implemented first; and whether US sanctions on Russian energy will be further eased. Source:Al Jazeera 2. As attacks by the Houthi rebels intensify, the US has ordered the evacuation of some personnel from Saudi ArabiaOn 21 October, the US State Department ordered the evacuation of non-essential personnel from the US Embassy in Riyadh and its consulates, and requested that some diplomatic staff and family members of US government employees leave Saudi Arabia; this order applied only to Saudi Arabia, whilst other embassies in the Gulf undertook only temporary staff adjustments. According to the Associated Press, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been closed since it came under heavy attack on 10 October; only a few Saudi airlines have recently been permitted to resume operations, whilst Lufthansa and Air France have cancelled flights to Riyadh until mid-November. The Saudi Ministry of Energy stated that the wreckage of an intercepted drone fell at an oil field operated by Aramco in south-eastern Saudi Arabia, resulting in two deaths and two injuries; the Saudi-led coalition reported that Houthi militants launched five drones towards Saudi Arabia in the early hours of the 21st, all of which were intercepted. In the early stages following the announcement of the evacuation order, the market mistakenly believed that the scope covered the entire Gulf region, causing oil prices, US Treasury yields and the US dollar to rise temporarily; however, most of these gains were reversed after the State Council issued a clarification. This demonstrates that the market remains highly sensitive to the security of energy facilities in the Gulf. Key points to watch going forward: whether the Houthi rebels will continue to target Saudi oil facilities; whether countries such as Egypt will become directly involved; and shipping risks in the vicinity of the Strait of Hormuz. Source:Associated Press (reprinted by ClickOnDetroit) 3. Meta’s revenue rose by 26 per cent in the third quarter, but AI investment and legal costs pushed free cash flow into negative territoryMeta announced on 21 October that its third-quarter revenue stood at US$64.6 billion, up 26 per cent year-on-year and exceeding analysts’ expectations; however, operating profit fell by 37 per cent year-on-year to US$13.0 billion, primarily due to a provision of US$9.89 billion for legal costs arising from a settlement with the attorneys general of 52 states regarding adolescent mental health issues. Excluding this item, operating profit was approximately US$22.9 billion. Capital expenditure (including finance lease principal) for the third quarter totalled US$34.9 billion, whilst free cash flow stood at a negative US$2.1 billion, compared with a positive US$10.6 billion a year earlier. The company has narrowed its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to between US$135 billion and US$145 billion, whilst raising its full-year total expenses guidance to between US$175 billion and US$179 billion. Revenue guidance for the fourth quarter stands at between US$73 billion and US$76 billion. Meta also announced that it would issue non-voting Class C shares, to be distributed on a one-for-one basis for each Class A and Class B share held, with effect from 19 January 2027. Meta’s advertising business continues to grow rapidly, but investment in AI data centres has already exceeded operating cash flow. This is direct evidence that the AI investment cycle has entered a ‘cash-burning phase’. Moving forward, the market will place greater emphasis on the return cycle of capital expenditure and funding methods; revenue growth alone is no longer sufficient. Key points to watch: preliminary guidance on capital expenditure for 2027, progress in the commercialisation of the Muse series of models, and the outcome of the appeal against the US$25 billion fine in New Mexico. Source:Meta Investor Relations、Fortune 4. Tesla’s profit margins have rebounded, but operating profit has fallen by 56 per centTesla announced its third-quarter results on 21 October: revenue stood at US$28.05 billion, unchanged from the same period last year and broadly in line with expectations; non-GAAP earnings per share were US$0.48, slightly higher than the market forecast of US$0.45. The gross margin rebounded to 19.6 per cent (from 16.8 per cent in the second quarter), but operating expenses rose by 39 per cent year-on-year, with research and development expenditure increasing by 69 per cent to $2.76 billion. Consequently, operating profit fell by 56 per cent to $718 million, with an operating margin of just 2.6 per cent. Deliveries in the third quarter totalled 486,500 vehicles, exceeding expectations; energy storage deployments amounted to 13.7 GWh, falling short of the expected figure of approximately 15.9 GWh, whilst revenue from the energy business fell by 16 per cent. Capital expenditure for the third quarter stood at US$4.73 billion, bringing the total for the first nine months to US$13.0 billion; the company has not updated its full-year guidance of ‘over US$25.0 billion’. Tesla is channelling its profits into autonomous driving, robotics and AI computing power, resulting in a significant squeeze on short-term profitability. The stabilisation of the automotive gross margin is good news, but whether the valuation can hold up will depend on when R&D investment translates into new sources of revenue. Key areas to watch going forward: the pace of robotaxi expansion; whether Q4 capital expenditure will meet the full-year guidance; and whether the energy storage business can return to growth. Source:Electrek 5. The General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council have issued a document to promote the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovationOn 21 October, the General Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council issued the ‘Opinions on Promoting the Deep Integration of Scientific and Technological Innovation and Industrial Innovation’, which focuses on establishing an innovation system led by enterprises and characterised by collaboration between industry, academia and research institutions. The document stipulates that, in principle, national science and technology programme projects with clear industrial application objectives should be led by enterprises, which should also take the lead in the commercialisation of results; project acceptance shall be based on ‘assessing technology through application and products through the market’, utilising milestone-based management and phased funding disbursements. Supporting measures include: encouraging state-owned enterprises to establish a research and development reserve fund system exempt from asset preservation and appreciation assessments and allowing for a margin of error; increasing the additional tax deduction ratio for research and development expenses of science and technology-based small and medium-sized enterprises; government-funded venture capital funds should “invest early, in small enterprises, for the long term, and in hard technology”; establishing proof-of-concept centres and pilot production platforms; encouraging universities and research institutes to licence their research outcomes to small, medium and micro-enterprises on a “use-first, pay-later” basis; and fully implementing a patent open licensing system. The document does not specify quantitative targets or funding levels; it constitutes a policy framework setting out general directions. However, by shifting the focus of performance assessments from academic papers and patents towards industrialisation and market validation, it will have practical implications for ‘hard tech’ enterprises, venture capital firms and research institutes. Key points to watch: the implementation guidelines from various ministries and local authorities; the specific extent of adjustments to the additional tax deduction ratio for R&D expenditure; and the pace of expansion of the ‘Technology Board’ in the bond market. Source:Xinhua News Agency Market Correlation and Today's ObservationOn 21 October, US shares closed slightly higher, with the S&P 500 index rising by around 0.2 per cent to close at around 7,759 points; the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note remained largely unchanged at around 5.13 per cent, whilst the winning yield at the 20-year Treasury auction was 5.469 per cent; WTI crude oil briefly touched around US$102 during the session, before closing down by approximately 0.4 per cent at around US$99.4 (figures are approximate, based on Babypips’ closing review). Judging by the day’s price action, news of Russia-Ukraine talks weighed on oil prices in early trading, whilst a misinterpretation regarding the evacuation of nationals briefly pushed up oil prices, yields and the US dollar in the afternoon, illustrating that the geopolitical premium on energy prices continues to fluctuate rapidly in response to news developments. As for technology stocks, the earnings reports from Meta and Tesla tell the same story: whilst revenue or profit margins are improving, AI-related investments are consuming significant amounts of cash. In an environment where US Treasury yields remain above 5 per cent, companies with negative free cash flow are more likely to be asked to justify the payback period for their capital expenditure. China’s science and technology innovation policies are unlikely to directly improve profitability in the short term, but policy expectations are providing support for sectors such as hard technology, venture capital and pilot-scale testing services. Checklist:
Have the date, venue and agenda for the trilateral talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine been finalised? Have the Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities and airports escalated? Will WTI hold steady at $100, and will the yield on 10-year US Treasuries break through 5.15 per cent? The market’s reaction to Meta’s capital expenditure and negative free cash flow, as well as AI spending guidance in other tech companies’ earnings reports this week Changes in interest rate expectations ahead of the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy meeting on 28 October Detailed rules issued by relevant ministries and commissions, and local supporting policies relating to the ‘Opinions’
Source:Babypips Market Review Cover image:Maria Baranova / Unsplash

entry.title: Anthropic, with a loss of 80.7 billion, is currently in the healthiest state in its history – why? | Aden’s Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original.
Introduction: The Wall Street Journal recently revealed a confidential draft of Anthropic’s S-1 prospectus, with a headline that is nothing short of staggering:The net loss for the first half of 2026 amounted to as much as US$80.7 billion. The public sphere was instantly in an uproar, with cries of ‘AI money-guzzlers running amok’ and ‘a massive bubble’. However, if you really look beneath the surface of the financial statements, you will arrive at a startling conclusion that is the exact opposite:Far from being a bad thing, this massive loss is, in fact, a direct consequence of the company’s immense popularity in the primary market; and this company, which on the surface appears to have ‘lost 80 billion in half a year’, has in fact just passed its profitability inflection point and is now enjoying the healthiest period in its commercial history.
Introduction: Sensational Figures and Public MisconceptionsIn recent days, the AI venture capital community has been rocked by a leaked document. According to reports in *The Wall Street Journal* and Reuters, as Anthropic—the leading large-language model company and parent firm behind Claude—races towards its upcoming trillion-dollar IPO on the Nasdaq, key financial figures from its confidential draft S-1 prospectus have come to light:
Net loss for the first half of 2026：US$80.7 billion(compared with US$13 billion in the same period last year); Total revenue for the first half of 2026：US$16.3 billion(compared with just US$1.1 billion in the same period last year); Commitment to the Procurement of Booked Computing Power: Gundam US$518 billion to over US$600 billion。
The first reaction of many readers who are not from a financial background is: ‘Burning through $80 billion in half a year – is the commercialisation of AI really one huge scam?’ If you, too, have such doubts, that’s perfectly normal—because the traditional income statement is producing an utterly absurd picture when applied to today’s super-unicorns, which are raising funds at a frenetic pace through ‘convertible bonds’.Accounting Illusions That Defy Common Sense。 I. The truth behind the 80.7 billion loss: the more valuations soar, the worse the financial statements lookTo understand this loss of US$80.7 billion, we must first ‘break it down’: Of this US$80.7 billion, exactly US$72 billion (accounting for as much as 89.2 per cent)…it was not at all a payment to Nvidia for chips, nor was it staff salaries, and not a single penny left the company’s bank account—It is entirely a non-cash fair value adjustment loss.。 Anthropic 2025 Financial Structure Waterfall Chart: Discrepancy between Revenue and Changes in Fair Value Figure 1Anthropic financial structure waterfall chart: taking 2025 as an example, $4.59B in revenue, $7.33B in computing power expenditure, and an operating loss of $8.06B; however, non-operating fair value adjustments amounting to as much as $33.9B push the net loss directly to $41.97B – four-fifths of this ‘massive loss’ lies below the operating line. (Data: Reuters / Draft S-1; Chart: SweetValueLab) How exactly does this accounting paradox work?Before going public, modern Silicon Valley super-unicorns often raise funds throughConvertible NotesOr raise funds through senior financing instruments that include valuation-based redemption clauses. Investors (such as Amazon and Google) have lent tens of billions of dollars to Anthropic, with the agreement that these loans will be converted into ordinary shares at a certain discount upon a future IPO. In accordance with US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP, specifically ASC 470-20):
Prior to listing, this type of convertible bond must be treated as the company’sLiabilities, and revalued on a period-by-period basis in accordance with current market fair value. Whilst Anthropic was the talk of the global primary market and its valuation soared from tens of billions to a trillion,The value of the shares that these convertible bonds will be converted into in the future has soared—in other words, the company’s ‘fair value of debt’ has increased significantly! GAAP standards strictly stipulate that:Any increase in liabilities must be recorded as a ‘book loss’ of the same amount in the current period’s profit and loss account!
This is one of the most counter-intuitive scenes in modern fintech:The more a company is recognised by investors and the more its valuation soars, the larger the ‘non-cash losses’ it is forced to recognise on its books! After deducting this revaluation impairment of 72 billion, Anthropic’s results for the first half of 2026The actual operating loss amounted to only approximately US$8.7 billion。 Anthropic: Financial Comparison – H1 2025 vs H1 2026 Figure 2Comparison of revenue and net losses for H1 2025 and H1 2026: Revenue surged nearly 15-fold, whilst the main reason for the sharp rise in the reported net loss was a revaluation provision relating to convertible bonds worth US$10 billion. (Data: Reuters; Chart: Notebookcheck) This is not even the first time this has happened: for the full year 2025, Anthropic recorded revenue of US$4.59 billion and an operating loss of US$8.06 billion, whilst the net loss ultimately reported was equally as high as US$41.97 billion(Of this, approximately US$34 billion was due to a revaluation of assets of a similar nature.) The same applies to OpenAI next door: of its net loss of approximately US$39 billion in 2025, around US$30 billion was attributable to such one-off accounting entries. Once the company goes public with a bell-ringing ceremony, all convertible bonds will be converted into ordinary shares; this ‘loss multiplier’ will be completely wiped out overnight, and the financial statements will instantly be cleared of any losses. II. The True Key Performance Indicators: From ‘Burning Cash for Growth’ to ‘Turning Efficiency Around’If we strip away the accounting illusion, how well does Anthropic’s underlying business machine actually perform? The answer is:It is truly astonishing, and a fundamental transformation is currently taking place. 1. A 15-fold surge in revenue and a leap in scaleIn the first half of 2025, Anthropic’s revenue stood at just US$1.1 billion; by the first half of 2026, this figure had jumped to US$16.3 billion, with a year-on-year increase of nearly 15 times。 Revenue for the first half of this year alone already amounts to the full-year revenue for 2025 (US$4.59 billion) More than 3.5 times. There is scarcely a parallel to this rate of expansion in the entire history of modern commerce. Anthropic’s Quarterly Revenue Trends and Quarter-on-Quarter Growth Rates Figure 3Quarterly revenue trends: Q1 $4.7B ➔ Q2 $11.6B ➔ Q3 $16.8B. Q3 revenue alone was 3.7 times the full-year figure for 2025. (Data: Reuters / S-1 draft; Chart: SweetValueLab) 2. The underlying dynamics behind the ‘slowdown in growth’Another major point of contention in the public debate on the draft was the ‘sharp slowdown in month-on-month growth’:
The quarter-on-quarter growth rate from Q1 to Q2 once reached as high as +145%； However, the quarter-on-quarter growth rate from Q2 to Q3 plummeted to +45%… a drop of no less than 100 percentage points.
TickerTrends: Quarterly Revenue and the Trend Towards Slowing Growth Figure 4Chart showing quarter-on-quarter growth trends: from an exceptionally rapid surge in Q2 to a marked step-like slowdown in Q3. (Data: FT / Reuters; Chart: TickerTrends) Many people interpret this as demand for large language models having peaked, but the real reason is more strategic in nature:According to a report by *The Information*, external organisations had previously used APIs to extract Claude’s outputs for model distillation; this type of business had previously accounted for approximately 5 per cent to 7 per cent of Anthropic’s revenue. In the third quarter,Anthropic has proactively tightened its risk control measures regarding anti-distillation technology; it would rather sacrifice a portion of its short-term revenue than give competitors any opportunity to copy its approach.. This proactive move to sacrifice growth in exchange for a technological moat clearly demonstrates that the management is laying the groundwork for long-term competitive advantages following the IPO. 3. The most impressive figure: a return of $1.70 for every $1 of computing powerWhilst the slowdown in revenue growth was largely anticipated, what has excited Wall Street investment banks most about this draft S-1 filing is the following curve illustrating the return on computing power investment: Revenue generated per US$1 of computing power costs has surged Figure 5A transformation in revenue efficiency per unit of computing power: the revenue generated per US$1 invested in computing power is set to surge from US$0.15 in 2024 to US$0.63 in 2025, reaching a staggering US$1.70 in Q3 2026. (Data: Reuters / S-1 draft; Chart: SweetValueLab)
2024: For every US$1 spent on computing power, you can only bring back 0.15 US dollars Revenue (typically a pre-training phase characterised by heavy cash burn); 2025: For every US$1 spent on computing power, the return is US$0.63； Q3 2026: For every US$1 spent on computing power, you can already recoup your investment US$1.70 Revenue!
Capital expenditure on computing power has finally evolved from a mere ‘cost centre’ into a ‘profit generator’ with strong operating leverage. It is precisely for this reason that Anthropic is projected to achieve an adjusted operating profit of approximately US$559 million in Q2 2026 and an adjusted operating margin of 11%）The company has now posted adjusted operating profits for two consecutive quarters, and its cash flow is now self-sustaining.！ That is why we say:Anthropic is currently in the best financial shape it has ever been since its foundation. III. The $100-billion chain and the ‘closed-loop capital theory’ of the tech giantsAlthough the business has begun to generate its own revenue, another astronomical figure in the prospectus still reveals the perilous nature of this AI war—Binding Commitment on Computing Power Procurement。 The draft reveals that the total value of the long-term computing power procurement agreements signed by Anthropic amounts to US$518 billion(spanning approximately 10 years); as the latest expansion negotiations progress, this figure has risen further to Over US$600 billion, and could even reach US$750 billion. $518 billion in computing power commitments, broken down by counterparty Figure 6Distribution of counterparties for the $518 billion in firm computing power commitments: the four companies—Broadcom, Google, Amazon and Microsoft—account for a combined total of $413.7 billion (nearly 80 per cent), which constitutes fully irrevocable, binding contracts. (Data: Reuters / S-1 draft; Chart: SweetValueLab) Taking a closer look at the distribution of opponents: Broadcom: Approx. $161B(in-house, custom-designed ASIC computing clusters); Google: not less than $111B(TPU computing power procurement); Amazon: not less than $110B(AWS Trainium and cloud computing power); xAI: not exceeding $84.5B； Microsoft: not less than $31.4B； AMD: Super $20B。
Of these, the top four giants have cumulatively US$413.7 billion (accounting for nearly 80 per cent) is entirely comprised of ‘take-or-pay’ agreements。 This reveals the most surreal aspect of Silicon Valley at presentCircular Economy：In 2025, Anthropic will have a full 47 per cent of sales revenue They are sold directly to customers via Amazon AWS and Google Cloud.In other words,Amazon and Google are not only major shareholders in Anthropic (Amazon holds approximately 15–21 per cent, whilst Google holds approximately 14 per cent), but also its largest providers of computing power and its most important distributors; at the same time, they are developing their own competing models (Titan/Gemini). Whilst this nested model—‘you invest in me, I buy your cloud services, and you help me sell them’—accelerated the growth of a business worth hundreds of billions in its early stages, it also sowed the seeds of a very high risk of market concentration:The S-1 form shows that,The two largest clients alone accounted for nearly 20 per cent of total revenue in the first half of 2026(This figure is set to rise to as much as 25 per cent by 2025), and the two parties are not bound by any long-term contracts. As recently as mid-October, the well-known AI programming unicorn Replit announced that it had switched its default underlying model from Claude to OpenAI—should major clients begin to drift away, this would directly result in a visible fluctuation in quarterly figures. IV. Countdown to the IPO: ‘Unconventional’ Timing and Privileges in the ProspectusIn the run-up to its forthcoming initial public offering, Anthropic has been intensively pursuing a series of preparatory steps that, whilst appearing entirely standard, are in fact fraught with subtleties:
Key steps in IPO preparations Current Status of Anthropic’s Implementation Strategy and Governance: Implications
Confidential Filing of Form S-1 ✅ Submitted confidentially on 1 June 2026, the recently leaked document is a draft amendment In accordance with the confidential audit rules for emerging growth technology companies permitted under the US JOBS Act
Clearing the Cap Table ✅ A provision of $72B has been recognised on the books as the project enters its final stages Once the listing is completed and the bell is rung, the convertible bonds will be converted into ordinary shares as agreed, and the financial statements will be fully cleared following the listing.
Strengthening the Founder’s Absolute Control ✅ Establishment of a 5-tier complex shareholding structure + Founder LLC + LTBT trust The seven founders hold only around 14 per cent of the shares, but through Founder LLC they hold Class F shares with super-voting rights,Hold a firm 50.1 per cent majority of voting rights, whilst retaining the Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) structure
Arrangements for existing shareholders to realise their holdings ✅ It has been reported that early shareholders will be permitted to sell their shares and realise their profits when the company is listed via an IPO. DeliberatelyUnlike SpaceX The practice of locking up existing shares at the time of listing, as a means of appeasing and rewarding the venture capitalists who made substantial investments at an early stage
Formation of an investment banking underwriting syndicate ✅ The four major banks have joined forces to take the lead Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi are jointly underwriting the deal
Pre-launch roadshow and listing dates 🔄 Intensive preparations are under way A closed-door ‘Investor Day’ was held in San Francisco on 14 October, at which baseball caps bearing the word ‘Thinking’ were handed out;Market rumours suggest that a nationwide roadshow is expected to begin in the week of 9 November, with the aim of listing on the Nasdaq on the eve of Thanksgiving (26 November).
A spectacle in the prospectus: an 80-page ‘warning of apocalyptic risks’In the 261-page prospectus—which companies typically use to disclose their financial and market strategies—Anthropic actually devoted the entire Page 80 Its astonishing length provides an exhaustive account of the ‘risk factors’ surrounding technology and ethics. For the first time ever, the document states in black and white:“Advanced artificial intelligence may pose catastrophic or even existential risks to the entire human race.” This commitment to effective altruism (EA) and compliance, upheld by founder Dario Amodei and his team, appears both absurd and profoundly serious against the backdrop of a trillion-dollar capital frenzy. V. Valuation and Scenario Analysis: Will Wall Street Buy into It?Previously, market expectations regarding Anthropic’s IPO had been hyped up to 2 trillion dollars ($2T) skyline (corresponding to a price-to-sales ratio of as high as 436 times full-year 2025 revenue). However, with quarter-on-quarter growth in Q3 slowing from 145 per cent to 45 per cent, the balance of pricing in the capital markets is undergoing a subtle realignment:
Role-play scenario Probability of occurrence Macroeconomic and fundamental trigger thresholds Analysis of Valuation and Market Performance
Baseline scenario(Fixed price) ~55% • The final S-1 filing, made public at the end of October, confirmed that the convertible bonds had been successfully converted and fully settled;• The roadshow in mid-November was met with strong oversubscription from mainstream mutual funds and sovereign wealth funds;• The market has fully recognised the quality of its earnings, with an ‘adjusted operating profit margin of 11 per cent in Q3’, and has factored in the slowdown in growth. A consensus has been reached on an IPO valuation range of between $1.5T and $2.0T。Based on Q3 annualised revenue (approximately $67B), the P/S valuation multiple has fallen to approximately 22–30 times… and is within a reasonable range for a ‘giant’ premium. Its performance on the first day of trading is likely to be similar to that of SpaceX (with a 15–20 per cent turnover of shares following the listing, before stabilising at the support level).
Scene from the market(Enthusiastic acclaim) ~25% • The GAAP financial statements released to the public show free cash flow that is stronger than expected;• The new generation of cutting-edge models (the Claude 3.8 / 4.0 series) has achieved a generational leap in dominance within the enterprise-level programming and agentic AI markets;• Expectations of a year-end interest rate cut by the Federal Reserve are growing, and liquidity in the technology sector has once again become abundant. Listing price hits the upper end of the $2.0T range, with the subscription multiple exceeding 15 times; on its first day of listing, it attracted indiscriminate position-building by global long-term institutional investors.
The following scenario(Valuation compression) ~20% • Q4 revenue was affected by tighter anti-distillation measures and the loss of major clients (such as the Replit incident), causing quarter-on-quarter growth to fall below 30 per cent;• Against the backdrop of high macroeconomic interest rates, there are widespread doubts regarding the sustainability of the commitment to one trillion in computing power (US$518 billion in capital expenditure);• US technology growth shares have experienced a systemic correction across the board. The IPO pricing may be forcibly capped within the $1.2T to $1.5T range, or the company and the underwriting syndicate may even choose to reduce the size of the fundraising or postpone the listing date.
VI. Honest Explanation of Data Definitions (Key Factual Boundaries)When evaluating the above analysis, it is essential to be fully aware of the limitations of the current data:
The final version of the S-1 filing has not yet been made fully available to the public: All current data is derived from direct quotations and verification of the confidential draft dated 20 October 2026 by leading authoritative financial media outlets such as The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg and Reuters; the final GAAP disclosure may be subject to minor adjustments; There is a discrepancy between the two measurement methods regarding full-year revenue for 2025: The Wall Street Journal reported that total revenue for 2025 was US$4.59 billion(net accounting method), whilst media outlets such as CNBC had previously reported that its annualised run rate had reached ‘approximately US$10 billion’. This discrepancy most likely stems from the difference between ‘gross versus net accounting’ when distributing via AWS/GCP, and an authoritative breakdown is awaited in the publicly available version of the prospectus; The real names of the two top-five clients have not yet been disclosed: The draft merely states that two major non-affiliated customers accounted for approximately 20 per cent of revenue in the first half of the year; their specific company codes remain confidential until the official version is published.
Conclusion: The general public looks at the profit and loss account; investment banks look at cash flow.The general public tends to fixate on the net loss at the very bottom of the profit and loss account, reacting with alarm and exclaiming, ‘A colossal loss of 80.7 billion’; whilst Wall Street investment banks and sovereign wealth funds, well versed in the logic of capital operations, have long since been calculating itsReturn on investment in computing power ($1 computing power ➔ $1.7 revenue)andThe ‘profit-generating flywheel’ that has delivered adjusted profits for two consecutive quarters。 Far from weighing down Anthropic, every fraction of this US$80.7 billion paper loss has instead served to confirm the primary market’s insatiable appetite for its skyrocketing valuation. As it heads for the Nasdaq with a 261-page prospectus, an irrevocable chain of 100 billion units of computing power, and a founder’s trust that controls the company despite holding just 14 per cent of the shares, the largest AI capital gamble in business history has only just begun. Main Sources of Information and Verification Index Reuters In-depth Report (20 October 2026): Anthropic recorded a net loss of over $80 billion in the first half TechStartups Fact-Check: Anthropic reports a staggering net loss of $80.7B ahead of its IPO Notebookcheck Financial Results Analysis: Anthropic reports a loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026 but continues to grow Fortune Feature: Insights from Anthropic’s IPO S-1 prospectus income statement SweetValueLab’s Illustrated Breakdown: Figures from Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus TickerTrends Data Insight: Anthropic’s Q3 revenue growth slowed CryptoBriefing reports: Anthropic’s draft IPO revenue and net loss breakdown Luminix Industry Research Report: What do we know about the Anthropic IPO?
