Politically, according to Bloomberg, Flávio has called for the election results to be declared invalid on the grounds that a Supreme Court justice ‘changed the rules’ by ordering a two-hour extension to polling hours. Key points to watch: how the court will rule on Flávio’s claims; whether the Central Bank of Brazil will intervene in the foreign exchange market; whether Lula’s team can present a credible fiscal framework as soon as possible; and whether foreign capital will continue to withdraw. Source:CNN Brasil、Bloomberg (reprinted from the Spokesman-Review)、MercoPress、TheStreet 2. Anthropic has publicly filed its prospectus, with plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ‘ANT’On 26 October, Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 prospectus with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, planning to list its Class A shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT; the company had previously filed a confidential application in June. According to a summary of the prospectus by TipRanks and TNW, the company’s revenue for the first half of 2026 was US$16.29 billion, compared with US$1.16 billion in the same period the previous year; full-year revenue for 2025 was US$4.59 billion. The net loss for the first half of the year stood at US$80.7 billion, although approximately US$72.4 billion of this was a non-cash accounting charge arising from convertible notes as the company’s valuation rose; according to TNW, second-quarter revenue was US$11.6 billion, with the company achieving an operating profit for the first time. The lead underwriters are Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, with a further 20 banks participating. The prospectus did not specify a price range or the number of shares to be issued. According to The Wall Street Journal and Reuters, citing sources familiar with the matter, the listing is likely to take place in mid-November, with a target valuation of approximately US$1.5 trillion and the potential to raise US$100 billion or more. The prospectus also reveals key features regarding costs and governance. According to *The Wall Street Journal*, the company’s future commitments to computing power expenditure could reach as much as US$750 billion, primarily arising from cloud contracts with Google, Amazon and Microsoft; the top five clients accounted for approximately 25 per cent of revenue in the first nine months. In terms of governance, the company remains a public benefit corporation, with Class F shares held by the founders controlling 50.1 per cent of the voting rights on ordinary matters, whilst a long-term benefit trust elects a majority of the board seats via Class T shares; Class A shareholders on the open market are effectively unable to influence shareholder voting. If the offering proceeds on its current scale, it will be one of the largest IPOs in history and will serve as a test of the market’s capacity to absorb AI companies. Key points to watch going forward include the offering price range and valuation, OpenAI’s listing timetable, and the impact of non-cash losses, computing power commitments and the dual-class share structure on pricing. Source:TipRanks、TNW 3. Meta plans to raise up to US$95 billion through an equity offering to fund AI infrastructureAccording to Reuters (as reported by Business Standard), Meta announced on 26 October a plan to raise up to US$95 billion through equity financing, describing it as the largest equity fundraising in the company’s history. Of this, approximately US$35 billion will be raised through a public offering of ordinary and preference shares; according to the *Daily Economic News*, this includes US$22.5 billion in Class A ordinary shares and US$12.5 billion in mandatorily convertible preference shares; a further US$60 billion will be raised in tranches via an ‘at-the-market’ (ATM) programme, which will commence once the new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, expected in the first quarter of 2027. NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom have expressed their intention to subscribe for up to US$5 billion worth of Class A shares in total. Meta plans to issue Class C shares in January 2027, equivalent to a 2-for-1 stock split. The fundraising comes against a backdrop of weakening cash flow. Meta’s free cash flow for the third quarter stood at a negative US$2.12 billion, the first negative figure in over a decade; last week, it raised the lower end of its capital expenditure forecast for the year to between US$135 billion and US$145 billion, and committed to approximately US$825 billion in future spending, primarily for data centres and computing power. As at the end of September, the company held approximately US$82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities, whilst its long-term debt stood at approximately US$80.92 billion. Meta’s share price fell by approximately 1.4 per cent in early trading that day. Earlier this year, Alphabet also expanded the scale of its share issue to US$84.75 billion. Key points to watch: the capital expenditure guidance in this week’s earnings reports from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon; whether more technology companies will turn to equity financing; and the dilution effect on share prices and earnings per share resulting from large-scale share issues. Source:Business Standard (Reuters)、Bloomberg 4. Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have travelled to Tehran to mediate, whilst CNN reports that US forces could launch a large-scale strike against Iran within 96 hoursOn 26 October, high-level delegations from the three signatory states to the ‘Mecca Joint Defence Agreement’ visited Tehran: According to Al Jazeera, Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Chief of Army Staff Munir and Turkish Intelligence Chief Kalin met with Iranian President Pezeshizyan. The Iranian side stated that all parties agreed to continue dialogue and seek peace; the Saudi side indicated that the purpose of the talks was to open channels for negotiation and prevent a recurrence of military escalation. The talks also addressed missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Houthi rebels. Additionally, according to Reuters, Qatari mediators also travelled to Tehran under US coordination. Pezeshizian arrived in Moscow that evening to attend the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit and is expected to meet Putin on 27 October. Meanwhile, according to CNN, citing two US officials, the US military has deployed sufficient forces in the Middle East to launch a new, potentially large-scale operation within 96 hours of Trump giving the order; the list of targets includes Iran’s energy, military and nuclear facilities. The officials believe the order is most likely to be issued after the US mid-term elections and before the end of the year; Trump has not yet made a decision. CNN also reported that the US has asked Israel not to act unilaterally until preparations for a joint operation are complete; Israeli Defence Minister Katz denied any disagreement, stating that Israel “has never intended to launch an attack on Iran before the general election”. US Treasury Secretary Bessent told Iran International that there are no longer any crude oil shipments from Iran’s Khalk Island, and that pressure over the next eight weeks would be “even more intense”. Israel is holding parliamentary elections today (27 October), with Netanyahu stating his intention to work with Trump to “permanently eliminate the Iranian nuclear threat”. Key points to watch: the outcome of the Israeli general election and the formation of a new government; whether mediation by Qatar and the signatories to the ‘Mecca Agreement’ can open a channel for US-Iran negotiations; and US military decisions following the mid-term elections on 3 November. Source:Al Jazeera、The Tribune (citing CNN)、Fox News、Reuters (reprinted by Investing.com) 5. The renminbi closed above 6.67 against the US dollar, its strongest level since June 2022According to The Paper, on 26 October, the onshore renminbi closed at 6.6681 against the US dollar at 16:30, appreciating by 30 basis points from the previous trading day and closing below 6.67 for the first time since 8 June 2022; The offshore yuan rose to an intraday high of 6.66715, its strongest level since mid-June 2022. The yuan’s central parity rate for the day was set at 6.7162, an increase of 18 basis points, bringing the year-to-date appreciation to 4.45 per cent. Caitong Securities believes that geopolitical tensions and risk-averse sentiment are altering the relative attractiveness of domestic and foreign assets, whilst the resilience of the domestic economy, capital inflows via the financial account and corporate demand for foreign exchange conversion are collectively driving the appreciation of the renminbi; it expects the appreciation trend to continue, though the pace may slow. In terms of market performance, according to Sina Finance, the Hang Seng Index rose by 0.51 per cent on the day, whilst PetroChina’s Hong Kong-listed shares climbed by more than 5 per cent; on the A-share market, the Shanghai Composite Index closed higher, whilst the Shenzhen Component Index and the ChiNext Index fell by more than 1 per cent. Trading volume on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges totalled 1.61 trillion yuan, a decrease of 347.5 billion yuan compared with the previous trading day. A stronger renminbi helps to reduce the cost of energy imports and provides some cushion against high oil prices, but it also squeezes the profit margins of exporting firms. Key points to watch going forward: the forthcoming September industrial enterprise profit figures, the direction of the US dollar following the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy meeting, and whether the central bank will adjust the pace of appreciation via the central parity rate. Source:The Paper、Sina Finance Market Correlation and Today's ObservationOn 26 October, US shares rose, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.70 per cent to 7,676.80 points, the Nasdaq rising 0.82 per cent to 26,169.38 points, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbing 0.28 per cent to 52,361.52 points; The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note remained broadly unchanged at around 4.98 per cent. Anthropic’s filing of its prospectus boosted sentiment in technology shares, but Meta’s share price fell following the announcement of a share issue, indicating that whilst the market welcomes the listing of AI companies, it is willing to accept price pressure resulting from large-scale dilution. As for oil prices, mediation efforts in Tehran caused Brent crude to fall by 0.8 per cent on 26 October, closing at US$115.81, whilst WTI closed at US$101.76; the Houthi rebels’ claim of attacks on pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s east-west oil pipeline limited the extent of the decline. The sharp fall in Brazil was largely due to domestic political and fiscal issues; whilst the spillover effect on other emerging markets remains limited for now, it will prompt investors to pay closer attention to election risks and fiscal discipline. Looking at several news items together: the funding requirements of AI giants have become so substantial that they must be met directly by the stock market; both Anthropic’s IPO and Meta’s share placement will draw capital away from the secondary market; whilst high oil prices and the prospect of further interest rate rises by the Federal Reserve are keeping interest rates at elevated levels. For the A-share and Hong Kong stock markets, the strengthening of the renminbi and the resurgence of foreign investment in Chinese assets are providing support, but the technology sector remains subject to fluctuations in AI valuations in global markets. Checklist:
The results of the Israeli general election on 27 October, and progress in the US-Iran mediation efforts The Federal Reserve’s 28 October monetary policy statement and expectations for a rate rise in December Capital expenditure and cloud business growth in the financial reports of Microsoft, Alphabet (28 October) and Amazon (29 October) Anthropic’s offering price range and valuation, and the pricing of Meta’s share placement How do Brazilian courts handle election-related claims, and does the Central Bank of Brazil intervene in exchange rates? September’s industrial enterprise profit figures, and whether the renminbi can stabilise below 6.67
Source:TheStreet、Reuters (reprinted by Investing.com) Cover image:Arturo Añez / Unsplash

entry.title: Anthropic officially unveils its S-1 prospectus: a deep dive – the bets we placed a week ago have all been revealed today | Aden’s Space
entry.content:
Automatically translated. Read the Chinese original.
Introduction: Over the past two months, we have been closely following Anthropic’s capital frenzy: first inReports on the leaked draftIt analysed the accounting intricacies behind the “huge book loss of 80.7 billion”, and subsequently compared it with OpenAI’sNasdaq jumps the gun. At the time, all speculation was based on unofficial sources—on 26 October 2026, the official announcement was made: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 registration statement with the SEC, and the stock code was finalised ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading a consortium of around 20 investment banks; the roadshow is expected to begin in the week of 9 November. This regulatory filing, comprising 335 pages of main text and 65 pages of financial notes, has finally brought the ‘moment of truth’ into sharp focus—Nine sets of previous inferences: five were confirmed, two were clarified, and two were significantly revised; one of these directly overturned the conclusion reached in our previous article.
Introduction: From rumours to the official seal – the formal ‘money-checking moment’For investors interested in the commercialisation of generative AI, 26 October 2026 is a date to note. Following the formal filing of Anthropic, PBC’s (Registration No. 333-299633) S-1 form with the SEC’s EDGAR system, this mega-IPO—co-led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, and backed by around 20 investment banks including JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays and Wells Fargo—has, for the first time, allowed everyone to cross-check all the rumours circulating over the past two months, one by one. On the eve of investment banks launching their full-scale US roadshow in November and making a final push to list on the Nasdaq before Thanksgiving, we have laid out the key conclusions drawn from our two previous in-depth analyses side by side with this formal document—which is strictly governed by law—and compared them point by point. The results of the card draw were quite solid:“Loss of 80.7 billion primarily due to the revaluation of convertible bonds” “Revenue surges 14-fold” “Five-tier shareholding structure with super voting rights”All of this has been confirmed by the official financial reports; and, even more unexpectedly, two key figures that had previously caused widespread concern saw a dramatic turnaround following the official announcement, proving to be in far better shape than rumours had suggested. I. Overview of the Card Reveals: Our previous comparison table of the nine sets of inferencesBefore you delve into the in-depth analysis, take a look at this definitive report card:
# Our previous conclusions (based on leaked drafts and media reports) Results of the disclosure in the SEC’s formal S-1 prospectus Final verification and assessment In-depth Facts and Explanation of Definitions
1 Net loss for the first half of 2026 was approximately $80.7B $80,748M (approximately US$80.748 billion) ✅ A perfect match The officially audited profit and loss account confirms that this figure has increased more than sixfold compared with the $12,969M (approximately US$12.97 billion) recorded in the same period last year.
2 Losses of approximately $72B (nearly 90 per cent) Fair value revaluation of convertible bonds $72,388M (approximately US$72.388 billion, accounting for 89.7 per cent) ✅ A perfect match This non-cash provision amounted to $1.04 billion, $5.43 billion and $34.31 billion in 2023, 2024 and 2025 respectively, increasing year on year as valuations rose.
3 The actual operating loss for the first half of 2026 was $8.7B The actual operating loss amounted to just US$693 million ($693M) ❌ Major amendments The most astonishing reversal! The previously reported “loss of 8.7 billion” was actually calculated as “net loss less changes in fair value” (approximately US$8.36 billion); the actual operating loss was less than 700 million.
4 Total revenue for the first half of 2026 was approximately $16.3B $16,286M (approximately US$16.286 billion) ✅ A perfect match A sharp rise compared with the $1,163M figure for the same period in 2025 approximately 14 times, and is already more than 3.5 times the full-year revenue for 2025 ($4,585M)
5 Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was approximately $16.8B The profit and loss account is presented on a full-year and half-year basis; quarterly revenue is not disclosed separately, and nine-month figures are only mentioned sporadically in discussions such as those on customer concentration. ⚠️ To be completed with due care The figure of $16.8 billion for a single quarter cited during the draft stage has not been verified by official documents and is not referenced in this article; the run-rate figure will be addressed in the S-1/A filing.
6 The total value of computing power procurement commitments is approximately US$518 billion (80 per cent non-cancellable) S-1: No single numerical heading is provided; the total of the individual items amounts to approximately US$515 billion to US$535 billion, and the officially audited fixed/minimum commitment is US$265.6 billion ($265.6B) ⚠️ Clarification of the scope The figure of $518B represents the media’s aggregate total of the various framework caps; the prospectus establishes a mandatory minimum liability threshold.
7 The top two clients accounted for approximately 20% total revenue In the first three quarters of 2026, no single customer accounted for more than 10 per cent of the total., with the top five customers accounting for approximately 25 per cent in total ❌ Major amendments Customer concentration is significantly diversified, and previous market concerns regarding reliance on a single major client have been disproved by the facts.
8 Approx. 47% Revenue from sales is routed via the cloud providers’ (AWS/GCP) marketplaces 47 per cent in 2025, rising slightly to 48 per cent in the first half of 2026 ✅ Confirmation Update The closed-loop distribution systems of the cloud computing giants remain robust, serving as their most important commercial moat.
9 5-tier equity isolation + Class F shares with 50.1 per cent voting rights + LTBT (Long-Term Beneficiary Trust) All of it has been confirmed in black and white… and also disclosed further details, including the actual transfer of a 5 per cent stake to a charitable foundation and the allocation of Class E shares to employees ✅ A perfect match The seven founders have secured 50.1 per cent of the total voting rights through a single Class F share, implementing a dual-layered defence mechanism combining commercial and ethical safeguards.
II. Two Major Rebuttals: The actual operating loss was less than 700 million, and the concerns over customer concentration proved to be a false alarmIn this substantial S-1 prospectus, what deserves the closest scrutiny from all secondary market analysts and technology observers are two points that completely overturn the market’s previous negative narrative:Major amendments： Clarification 1: The actual operating loss was only US$693 million, not the rumoured US$8.7 billionDuring the period when the draft was leaked, the claim that ‘even after deducting the 72 billion fair value revaluation, Anthropic’s actual loss for the first half of the year still amounted to a staggering 8.7 billion’ was widely circulated—including in our own previous article. A glance at the official S-1 income statement reveals the truth: In the first half of 2026, Anthropic’s total operating revenue was US$16.286 billion, Total Operating Expenses—which cover computing power leasing, model R&D, staff remuneration and sales management—amount to US$16.979 billion。 Subtracting one figure from the other, the actual operating loss amounted to just US$693 million ($693M) – compared with an operating loss of US$2,135 million ($2,135M) in the same period of the previous year. The prospectus states in black and white:
“Our operating loss was $693 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026.”(For the six months ended 30 June 2026, our operating loss was US$693 million.)
A Breakdown of Anthropic’s Official Profit and Loss Statement for the First Half of 2026 Figure 1Breakdown of Anthropic’s official profit and loss figures for the first half of 2026: revenue of US$16.286 billion, with an actual operating loss of just US$693 million; nearly 90 per cent of the massive reported loss (US$72.388 billion) was attributable to the revaluation of convertible bonds at fair value. Source: SEC EDGAR S-1 formal prospectus. So where exactly did the previously circulating figure of ‘US$8.7 billion’ come from? This is a classic example ofConfusion over terminology： Total net loss $80,748M Less: revaluation of the fair value of convertible bonds $72,388M, the difference being approximately US$8.36 billion. This shortfall comprises three components: an actual operating loss of 693 million, net non-operating expenditure of approximately 7.65 billion (interest income of 1.11 billion, other non-operating net expenditure of −8.76 billion, the latter primarily comprising changes in the fair value of strategic investments and financial instruments), and income tax of approximately 20 million. To describe the entire difference resulting from ‘stripping the fair value revaluation from the net loss’ directly as an ‘operating loss’ is tantamount to cramming non-operating items into the operating line—this was precisely the terminology error committed by financial reports at the time (including when we ourselves paraphrased them); it was only with the formal filing of the S-1 that this line was truly drawn. Given a total revenue of over US$16.2 billion, an operating loss of just under US$700 million means that:Anthropic’s operating loss margin for its core business has narrowed to approximately -4.2 per cent (compared with approximately -184 per cent in the same period last year), bringing it within touching distance of breaking even. Case Study 2: Fears over customer concentration disproved by the factsDuring the period when the draft was leaked, the market had expressed concerns that “the top two clients accounted for 20 per cent of revenue in the first half of the year”, whilst the decision by the AI programming tool Replit to switch its default model to OpenAI also caused a brief stir. The official S-1 filing provides a compelling rebuttal: In the first three quarters of 2026,No single customer accounts for 10 per cent or more of total revenue(In the first half of the year, Customer C alone accounted for 11 per cent), with the top five customers collectively contributing approximately 25 per cent; the S-1 filing also disclosed that in the third quarter of 2026, revenue from the ‘long tail’—i.e. customers other than the top five—accounted for approximately 79 per cent, a further increase from the approximately 64 per cent recorded in the first quarter. In its place is a healthy, horizontal customer funnel:
Revenue over the past 12 months (TTM) exceeded US$100,000 The number of corporate clients has reached Over 11,900(Just over 950 a year ago, representing a growth of more than 12-fold); TTM revenue exceeded US$1 million has more than 1,900； Revenue in excess of US$10 million Super Lighthouse’s client base of approximately 250 companies； More than half of the Fortune 500 companies have already adopted Claude’s enterprise services, with a penetration rate of over 30 per cent amongst the Forbes Global 2000.
The so-called structural weakness of ‘over-reliance on one or two major clients’ has been thoroughly debunked in the light of official data. III. A stronger-than-expected financial foundation: a return to profitability and ample cash reservesIn addition to these two major reversals, a series of in-depth financial indicators disclosed for the first time in the formal prospectus demonstrate the financial resilience of a mature software giant:
Adjusted operating profit has returned to positive territory：After excluding non-cash items such as share-based payment expenses ($2,185M) and liabilities relating to the charitable matching scheme ($126M), Anthropic’s adjusted operating profit for the first half of 2026 amounted to +US$1.618 billion, adjusted operating profit margin 10%(compared with −US$1.849 billion in the same period last year, marking a complete turnaround); adjusted net profit also recorded +US$2.671 billion。 Operating cash flow (CFO) generates genuine self-sustaining revenue：In the first half of 2026, the company’s net cash flow from operating activities amounted to +US$3.93 billion (+$3,929M), compared with a net outflow of US$1.51 billion in the same period last year. This means that even without external equity financing, the company’s day-to-day operations alone are already generating a steady stream of real cash. A massive cash moat of US$131.65 billion：As at 30 June 2026, Anthropic’s total book value of cash, cash equivalents and highly liquid short-term investments amounted to US$131.65 billion ($131.65B)…exceeding the reserves of the vast majority of S&P 500 constituents, providing a substantial liquidity buffer for the future race for high-intensity computing power. Statutory definition of historical funding amounts：Section 15 of the prospectus (Item 15) disclosed for the first time the official figures for the two most recent rounds of substantial funding:Series G-1 preference shares raised US$23.5 billion, Series H-1 raised US$45.7 billion, and Series H-2 raised US$19.5 billion。 An impressive Net Retention Rate (NRR)：NRR, the key metric used in the enterprise software sector to measure customer retention, recorded Approximately 900 per cent. The average net revenue contribution from our existing customer base is approximately nine times what it was a year ago—not due to churn, but rather to an almost explosive rate of organic growth. The ‘inflated revenue figures’ disclosed in all honesty：The prospectus makes the rare admission that in the first three quarters of 2026, there were approximately 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue comes from customers who breach our usage policy or commercial terms(The S-1 form does not specify the exact type; the risk section mentions ongoing external attempts to replicate, distil and extract the model). With the company set to comprehensively strengthen monitoring and enforcement between August and September 2026, this portion of revenue is expected to decline in subsequent quarters—the fact that the company has taken the initiative to proactively eliminate inflated figures in its prospectus demonstrates a strong commitment to compliance.
IV. A Detailed Breakdown of the 100-billion-yuan computing power chain: Media estimates vs the audit baselineThe “US$518 billion computing power procurement commitment”, which we discussed previously in our series of articles, has been subject to the most comprehensive statutory breakdown to date in the notes to the financial statements of the formal S-1 filing. It should be clarified that,The main text of Form S-1 does not directly state a single figure of ‘US$518 billion’ in bold., This is a consolidated total compiled by financial media outlets of the maximum contract values for the major cloud service providers: Anthropic’s computing power procurement commitments, broken down by supplier Figure 2A breakdown of Anthropic’s computing power procurement commitments: the total value of contracts with major suppliers amounts to approximately US$518 billion ($518B), whilst the fixed/minimum commitments, as per the officially audited figures in the S-1 filing, stand at US$265.6 billion ($265.6B). Source: SEC EDGAR S-1 formal prospectus. Supplier contract-by-contract breakdown: Broadcom: Five-year lease agreement for specialised hardware equipment, totalling approximately US$125.2 billion ($125.2B), interest-free and irrevocable; rent is payable quarterly, with a maximum of US$42 billionthe supply chain financing facility secured by the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA (asset-backed notes); SpaceXAI (formerly X.AI, part of the Musk ecosystem): Up to US$120.5 billion (≤$120.5B) The cluster computing power procurement agreement (NVIDIA GPUs) entails monthly expenditure of approximately US$3.1 billion when operating at full capacity; the initial irrevocable term runs until 1 March 2027, after which either party may terminate the agreement by giving 90 days’ notice—an increase on the estimate given during the draft stage; Google: Irrevocable TPU computing power guarantee agreement US$114.5 billion (≥$114.5B), covering the period from April 2026 to July 2033; any shortfall must be made up via a true-up; in addition, the forecast for 2028–2031 is US$125 billion to US$150 billion the procurement of additional computing power (not included in the fixed commitment table); Amazon: The irrevocable minimum threshold for computing power procurement US$110.0 billion (≥$110.0B), with a term running from May 2026 to April 2036—a period of ten years—and also incorporating a true-up mechanism; Microsoft: Irrevocable procurement threshold US$44.9 billion (≥$44.9B), valid from November 2026 to May 2033; payment is required regardless of actual usage—Claude is currently available via the three major cloud platforms: AWS, GCP and Azure; AMD: No fixed amount is committed; if the entire initial batch of computing power is purchased, the expenditure will exceed US$20 billion (>$20B); in return, AMD has undertaken to purchase up to US$5 billion Class N non-voting shares (unlocked in tranches upon the achievement of GPU delivery milestones).
The absolute minimum requirements for statutory audits： After excluding all optional cancellation clauses, flexible arrangements and potential options, the financial notes to the prospectus (F-59) provide the audited figures for firm contracts—The total value of fixed/guaranteed procurement commitments spanning 1 to 20 years amounts to US$265.6 billion ($265.6B)。 Whether it is the framework cap of 518 billion or the statutory obligation of 265.6 billion, Anthropic has, through these massive contracts spanning a decade, secured the core production capacity of global semiconductor and cloud computing giants for its own purposes. V. Details of Top-Level Governance: Super Voting Rights, Independent Trust and the Conversion of the 5 per cent Public Welfare Fund into Equity SharesIn the area of governance and control—which attracts the most attention in the capital markets—the formal S-1 filing reveals the ingenious safeguards this not-for-profit organisation has put in place to strike a balance between commercial interests and ethical autonomy: 1. The design of a five-tier shareholding structure and absolute control Class A Ordinary Shares: One voting right per share, for trading on the open secondary market; Class N shares: The economic rights are the same as those of Class A shares, but they carry no voting rights; upon transfer to an unrelated third party, they are automatically converted into Class A shares. Amazon’s convertible bonds are subject to a 12 per cent conversion cap (any amount exceeding this is converted into rolling notes with no additional issuance rights), and external investors such as Google also hold primarily this type of share to prevent the cloud giant from holding an excessive stake; Class E Employee Incentive Shares: Details revealed for the first time in the official version—employees are automatically allocated one Class E share for every six months they have worked at the company, with each share carrying one voting right; Class T shares: Held exclusively by the Long-Term Benefits Trust (LTBT), which has no economic interest, and is responsible for appointing certain directors (Class T directors) and participating in specific governance arrangements; Class F Founder’s Exclusive Shares: Through a dedicated Founder LLC Held separatelya stream. This group, which has no economic stake but holds sway over the entire company 50.1 per cent of the total voting rights—The seven co-founders (Dario, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah) thereby retained decisive control over the company’s strategic direction.
The individual economic stakes held by the seven founders were not disclosed as a single figure in the beneficial ownership table of the formal S-1 filing (external estimates during the draft stage put this at approximately 14 per cent) ; what is certain is the governance arrangement itself: the company is eligible for an exemption from certain governance requirements under the Nasdaq ‘Controlled Company’ rules, but the S-1 states that it intends to apply this exemption only to the Nomination Committee, with the majority of the Board of Directors still comprising independent directors. Another new detail is:The seven founders have each pledged to donate 80 per cent of their personal shareholdings in Anthropic to charitable causes.(A voluntary, revocable long-term commitment). 2. A genuine B Corp: a charitable trust receives a 5 per cent equity stakeUnlike many companies, which merely make vague charitable pledges in their prospectuses, Anthropic has gone ahead and completed a transfer of shares involving real money: The company has provided the independent Anthropic Public Benefit Fund Injection 847 million shares (846,840,960 shares) of Class N shares, representing 5 per cent of the fully diluted economic interest(Based on the assumption that the convertible bonds are converted in full). Furthermore, the Articles of Association stipulate that whenever the share price rises by 50 per cent compared with the previous price, the Board of Directors may, at its discretion, issue up to a further 2 per cent of shares to the fund to support long-term AI governance, alignment research and public interest initiatives. 3. A risk warning spanning approximately 94 pages and the challenges faced by the insurance industry in underwritingThroughout the prospectus,The ‘Risk Factors’ section begins on page 26 and continues for approximately 94 pages (up to around page 119)—This is probably the most substantial prospectus of any AI company to date. The document contained strong language rarely seen in the prospectuses of publicly listed companies:
“…sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity…”(AI systems that are sufficiently advanced may pose catastrophic or even existential risks to humanity if they lack appropriate safeguards, oversight and security measures during their development, deployment and operation.)
“With the scale of harm that could result from a catastrophic AI-related incident, no single insurer, and potentially the insurance industry in the aggregate, may have sufficient capacity or expertise to underwrite insurance commensurate with such exposure.”(Given the scale of damage that a catastrophic AI incident could cause, no single insurer—or even the entire insurance industry taken as a whole—is likely to possess the underwriting capacity or specialist expertise required to deal with it.)
Including the statement that ‘commercial insurance may not cover AI disasters’ in formal securities disclosures not only reflects the founding team’s roots in Effective Altruism (EA), but also fulfils, from a legal perspective, the ultimate duty to inform the public of potential risks. VI. Simulation of New Scenarios on the First Day of Listing (Updated 50 / 35 / 15)Given that the underlying financial fundamentals are significantly better than expected and concerns regarding customer concentration have been allayed, we have updated our assessment of the probability of market volatility on Anthropic’s first day of trading:
Role-play scenario Probability of occurrence Key trigger thresholds and macroeconomic conditions Market and Valuation: Definitions
Scenario A(Open higher and remain stable) ~50%(Base case) • If the amended S-1/A filed in early November sets the pricing range at the level currently being discussed in the market, $1.5T to $2.0T Implied valuation range (Note: this range is currently only being discussed in the media; the official document leaves this field blank);• Roadshow orders were oversubscribed several times over by sovereign wealth funds and long-term mutual funds;• Macroeconomic liquidity in the US stock market remained stable in early November. A resounding victory lays the foundations: On the first day of trading, the shares changed hands smoothly, with the initial gain falling within the 10 per cent–20 per cent range. This establishes a public market pricing benchmark for ‘enterprise-grade AI software’ (specific valuation multiples can only be calculated once the run-rate is disclosed in the S-1/A filing), from which OpenAI, which is next in line, will benefit directly.
Scenario B(Slightly higher than the previous close) ~35% • The pricing is close to the lower end of the $1.5T valuation range;• With the market under macroeconomic pressure from the 10-year US Treasury yield remaining above 5 per cent, trading in technology and growth stocks has been cautious across the board;• Institutional investors chose to take moderate profits after the market opened. Soft landing: Performance on the first day of trading was relatively subdued (with the share price fluctuating within a range of ±5 per cent). The underlying business logic remains sound, but the ‘AI miracle valuation’ has come under rigorous scrutiny in the open market.
Scenario C(The shock of a share price falling below its issue price) ~15% • Short sellers in the secondary market are focusing their efforts on the company’s 265.6 billion rigid hashrate commitment and the impact of the 5 per cent–7 per cent decline in non-compliant transaction volume to drive short selling;• A repeat of the market performance seen in June this year, when SpaceX’s share price fell by more than 30 per cent within two weeks of its listing. Across the board: The share price fell by more than 15 per cent below its issue price in its first week of trading, triggering a downward shift in the valuation benchmark for technology growth stocks; this will deal a blow to the narrative surrounding OpenAI’s planned 2027 IPO.
(The probability represents the findings of this study rather than a predictive conclusion; should the trigger conditions not be met, the probability will be adjusted accordingly.) VII. Honest Explanation of Data Definitions (Key Factual Boundaries)When reading this card-laying report, readers must maintain an objective and rigorous understanding of its scope:
The price range and offering size were deliberately left blank in the initial S-1 filing: In accordance with SEC practice, the current filing constitutes a preliminary registration statement (Subject to Completion); the specific price range per share, the actual number of shares to be issued and the amount to be raised by existing shareholders will be formally finalised in a subsequent amendment to Form S-1/A; The valuation of between 1.5 trillion and 2 trillion US dollars currently being discussed in the media represents a non-binding indicative offer and has not been included in any formal documentation; This article does not cite any third-quarter figures whatsoever.: The statutory audited financial statements in Form S-1 are presented on a full-year and half-year basis; revenue for the third quarter alone does not appear separately in the statements (figures covering the nine-month period are only mentioned sporadically in discussions regarding customer concentration and the proportion of non-compliant revenue); the figure of $16.8 billion for a single quarter, which circulated during the draft stage, has not been verified by any official document; The roadshow schedule is taken from various financial news reports: The timeframe of launching the roadshow in the week of 9 November and listing before Thanksgiving (26 November) is the consensus timeline reported by media outlets such as Bloomberg and Reuters; the S-1 filing itself, in accordance with standard practice, merely states ‘as soon as practicable’; All financial figures in this article are taken from the audited S-1 financial statements and the original text., available at Original text from SEC EDGARCheck each item individually.
Conclusion: The True Test of the Commercialisation of Coming-of-Age CeremoniesHaving worked my way through this S-1 prospectus—comprising 335 pages of main text and financial notes up to F-65—what struck me most was the pace of evolution demonstrated by this company, founded by idealistic tech geeks. Just over five years ago, when they left OpenAI to found Anthropic (in January 2021), there were those who questioned whether they were merely a group of armchair academics, sitting in an ivory tower and spouting empty rhetoric about ‘model alignment’ and ‘AI safety’, and who believed they stood no chance commercially against the ChatGPT empire backed by Microsoft. Yet what is now before global investors is a textbook example of a financial statement: Revenue surged 14-fold, surpassing the US$16 billion mark, whilst the actual operating loss narrowed to less than US$700 million, net operating cash flow stood at nearly US$4 billion, with over US$130 billion in cash reserves sitting on the balance sheet, whilst the company has also institutionalised the injection of 5 per cent of its actual shares into a charitable foundation. When the ticker symbol ‘ANT’ lit up on the Nasdaq screen in November, it was not only a crowning moment for Dario Amodei and his team, but also a coming-of-age ceremony for the entire generative AI industry. They laid their cards on the table for the world to see, using an official ledger:Large-scale models are not only capable of devouring capital, but have also, for the first time, demonstrated their ability to generate their own revenue under audit criteria—as for how high a price the market is willing to place on this ledger, the answer will soon be displayed on the Nasdaq screen. Main Sources of Information and Verification Index Official original registration statement on SEC EDGAR: Anthropic, PBC Form S-1 Registration Statement (CIK 0002130357, File No. 333-299633, 26 October 2026)(All financial figures in this article are sourced directly from the original sources and have been verified item by item prior to publication.)
